result.axis: CHALLENGE-D — assume the design is flawed (visual truth, state coverage, motion, design-system boundary, proportion/seat law)
result.modelObserved: Opus 5 (1M context) — exact model ID `claude-opus-5[1m]`. Matches the explicit Opus 5 declaration at spawn; seat is declared, not inherited.
result.strongestDefect: D-1 — the per-swatch copy verb is wholly inert. `GenerateControls.vue:203` passes `tag="button"` to `WatercolorDot`, but glass-ui 7.0.0 removed that prop (P051 abrogation) and its dist render function emits `<span aria-hidden="true" style="pointer-events:none">`. Measured live: tagName SPAN, ariaLabel null, tabIndex -1, pointerEvents "none", elementFromPoint at the dot centre returns the PARENT div. The action is simultaneously unclickable by pointer, unreachable by keyboard (0/5 focusable) and absent from the accessibility tree — a silent failure, since Vue drops an undeclared prop without warning and synthetic dispatchEvent bypasses the hit-test that kills the real click.
result.negativeProof: N/A — verdict is DEFECTIVE. Recorded sound areas so the next seat need not re-probe: (1) `verbatimModuleSyntax` clean — all four type-only imports use `import type` (:21, :32, :33); (2) `prefers-reduced-motion` covered at foundation scope via the `*` guard in `demo/styles/animations.css:184-193`, not a component defect; (3) forced-colors/print colour fidelity correctly granted at foundation level (`foundation.css:689`, `:834`), not per-instance; (4) route coarse gates green in all four Safari matrices — 0 blank, 0 pageErrors, 0 consoleErrors, 0 horizontalOverflow, main=1, darkClassMissing=0 (REPORT.md:124,139,154,169); (5) no god module — 311 lines, one job; (6) the seed-exact dropdown preview claim at `:94-100` genuinely verifies — `generatePalette` is pure and mulberry32-seeded, so the preview strips and the resulting selection are the same bytes. That is the one comment in the file whose claim measurement confirms.

defects.defect: Per-swatch copy verb is inert: `tag="button"` is not a prop in glass-ui 7.0.0. The producer renders a `<span aria-hidden="true">` with inline `pointer-events:none`, so the click cannot land, the `aria-label` is discarded, and the element is not focusable. Directly re-litigates the P051 abrogation that names Generate as an execute site.
defects.evidence: demo/workbenches/generate/GenerateControls.vue:199-208 passes `tag="button"` + `:aria-label` + `@click`. Producer prop set is `{color,variant?,animate?,cycleDuration?,range?,seed?}` (node_modules/@mkbabb/glass-ui/dist/components/watercolor-dot/WatercolorDot.vue.d.ts) — no `tag`. Render fn (dist/watercolor-dot.js): `o("span", {"aria-hidden":"true", ... style: u([f.value,{...pointerEvents:"none"...}])})`. Live measure on /#/generate: `{tagName:"SPAN", ariaHidden:"true", ariaLabel:null, tagAttr:null, role:null, tabIndex:-1, pointerEvents:"none", cursor:"pointer", rect:{w:40,h:40}}`; `hitTestAtDotCentre:{tag:"DIV", cls:"px-3 pb-1 flex flex-wrap gap-1.5", isTheDot:false}`; `swatchRowFocusable:0`. `grep -rn "generate-swatch" demo/ src/` returns only GenerateControls.vue:205, foundation.css:689, foundation.css:834 — no pointer-events override exists. Canon: VISUAL-CONSTITUTION.md:91 and OPTICAL-BENCH-COMPOSITIONS.md:108 both abrogate the `tag="button"` host and name Generate an execute site.
defects.mechanism: F1 — producer contract drift: glass-ui 7.0.0 landed the P051 removal while the consumer still writes the 6.x interactive-host idiom; Vue discards the unknown prop silently, so no typecheck, console warning or unit test fires.
defects.reproduction: Dev server live at localhost:9000. Navigate to http://localhost:9000/#/generate, then in the page: `const d=document.querySelector('.generate-swatch'); const r=d.getBoundingClientRect(); document.elementFromPoint(r.x+r.width/2, r.y+r.height/2)` → returns the parent `DIV.px-3.pb-1.flex.flex-wrap.gap-1.5`, not the dot. `d.tagName` → "SPAN"; `d.getAttribute('aria-label')` → null; `d.tabIndex` → -1; `getComputedStyle(d).pointerEvents` → "none". Clicking any swatch in the UI copies nothing.
defects.proposedCure: Architectural, per the canon's own prescription (OPTICAL-BENCH-COMPOSITIONS.md:108): the dot becomes a noninteractive face inside a NAMED GEOMETRIC SEAT — a native `<button type="button">` at >=44px carrying the accessible name, the focus ring and the click, with the untouched organic dot as its child. Structurally identical to the Gradient stop treatment already specified at VISUAL-CONSTITUTION.md:206. This single transposition restores the copy verb, the accessible name, the keyboard path and the tap floor at once. BLOCKED-ON-GLASS-V8 (RC-1, RC-2, RC-3).

defects.defect: The editable plate title is a false affordance: the typed palette name is emitted, then discarded at the persistence boundary. The consumer's handler signature has one parameter and hard-codes the literal "Generated Palette".
defects.evidence: GenerateControls.vue:48-52 declares `save: [colors: string[], name: string]`; :102-104 emits `paletteName.value`. GeneratePane.vue:14-20: `function onSave(colors: string[]) { ... pm.createPalette("Generated Palette", paletteColors); }` — the `name` arg is dropped. Live reproduction result: `{inputValueAfterType:"ZZ-CHALLENGE-D-NAME", libraryMentionsTypedName:false, libraryMentionsDefault:true, storedNames:["\"name\":\"Generated Palette\""], liveRegions:[]}`. Compounding: measured at-rest affordance on the input is `{border:"0px solid", textDecoration:"none", background:"rgba(0, 0, 0, 0)"}` — the dashed underline at :148 is `hover:` only, so on touch the control is permanently undiscoverable (PROPORTION-AUDIT.md:51 PR-07).
defects.mechanism: F2 — the emit that ends nowhere: a value is produced, typed, named and emitted at every layer except the one that persists it. The in-file comment at :44-47 records the gap as 'its owner's one-liner' and asserts 'this emit is already truthful' — provenance prose defending a wire that was never connected.
defects.reproduction: Navigate to http://localhost:9000/#/generate. Set the plate title input to `ZZ-CHALLENGE-D-NAME` (native value setter + dispatch `input`), click the `Save palette` button, wait 700ms, then read `localStorage['color-palettes']`. The persisted entry is `"name":"Generated Palette"`. The typed string appears neither in the DOM nor in storage, and no status/alert/aria-live region is emitted.
defects.proposedCure: Gestalt, not the one-line signature patch: a rename affordance with no visible boundary, no label and no confirmation does not belong on the specimen plate. VISUAL-CONSTITUTION.md:102 already homes it — 'rename/lifecycle/export actions and durable operation state live in the selected inspector.' Delete the plate field; the Library inspector owns rename. That is also the KISS cure and costs the user nothing. If the field is retained instead, `onSave(colors, name)` must carry the name AND gain a visible at-rest boundary plus a durable save confirmation. BLOCKED-ON-GLASS-V8 (same hold covers GeneratePane.vue).

defects.defect: The generated palette — the workbench's entire output — is wholly absent from the accessibility tree. Both renderings of the specimen are aria-hidden, so a screen-reader user receives zero colour information.
defects.evidence: PaletteColorStrip.vue:2-5 declares `aria-hidden="true" role="presentation"` with the comment 'color strip is a decorative visual, hidden from AT'. The WatercolorDot producer hard-codes `aria-hidden="true"` on its root (dist/watercolor-dot.js render fn). Live measure: `accNamesOnPlate: ["INPUT:Palette name","BUTTON:Save palette","BUTTON:Copy all colors"]`, `plateSelfLabel:"Generated palette"`. The full AT transcript for the region is: a text field, the numeral 5, three verbs, and `seed: 71f806ff`. Canon: VISUAL-CONSTITUTION.md:83 — 'Selected, failed, pending, withdrawn and disabled states are never color-only.'
defects.mechanism: F1 — producer contract drift. Both depictions were independently marked decorative on the assumption that some other surface carried the data; neither does, because the interactive host that was supposed to name them was abrogated (D-1).
defects.reproduction: Navigate to http://localhost:9000/#/generate and enumerate accessible names within `[data-generate-plate]`: `[...document.querySelector('[data-generate-plate]').querySelectorAll('[aria-label]')].map(e=>e.tagName+':'+e.getAttribute('aria-label'))` → exactly 3 entries, none a colour value. Both `.generate-swatch` and the strip root report `aria-hidden="true"`.
defects.proposedCure: OPTICAL-BENCH-COMPOSITIONS.md:108 states the shape: 'data-bearing static faces remain present as noninteractive NAMED list/text content with zero activation/focus/drag semantics.' The generated palette is data-bearing, so it requires a named list/text rendering of the colour values distinct from the decorative face — which the D-1 seat transposition supplies for free once each dot sits inside a named button. BLOCKED-ON-GLASS-V8 (RC-2).

defects.defect: The identical five colours are drawn three times inside one plate (full-bleed strip, WatercolorDot row, count-slider track gradient), and the constitutionally named protagonist renders at 38% of the area of its own redundant copy.
defects.evidence: Live measure, one frame: `stripSegColors` and `dotColors` are byte-identical five-element arrays of the same `oklch()` strings; the slider gradient carries the same five values as stops at 0/25/50/75/100%. Visible in all four Safari captures.
defects.mechanism: F3 — depiction inflation: when a datum is uncertain of its own presentation it is drawn again rather than drawn better. Compounded by a sideways import: GenerateControls.vue:16 reaches from `workbenches/generate` into `palettes/browser/card` internals for the strip, while the same file's composable comment (:23-24) proudly documents the correct feature-to-shared direction for the generation core.
defects.reproduction: Navigate to http://localhost:9000/#/generate and compare `[...document.querySelectorAll('[data-generate-plate] > :first-child *')].map(e=>getComputedStyle(e).backgroundColor)` against `[...document.querySelectorAll('.generate-swatch')].map(e=>getComputedStyle(e).backgroundColor)` — identical arrays. Then read `getComputedStyle(document.querySelector('div[style*="linear-gradient"]')).backgroundImage` — same five values again.
defects.proposedCure: Delete the borrowed `PaletteColorStrip` (which also severs the cross-feature import), and grow the WatercolorDot row into the 61.8% chassis stage it is constitutionally named as. One datum, one depiction, at the size its protagonist status justifies. defects.defect: The count slider's horizontal axis simultaneously encodes two incompatible quantities: palette index (0..n-1 mapped to 0..100% of the track) and cardinality (count 1..12 mapped to 0..100%). The resulting affordance is affirmatively misleading.
defects.evidence: GenerateControls.vue:65-73 paints the track by index: `const pct = colors.length === 1 ? 50 : (i / (colors.length - 1)) * 100`. :297-307 drives the thumb by count, `:min="1" :max="12"`. Live measure at count=5: gradient stops at `0%, 25%, 50%, 75%, 100%` while `thumbCentreFrac: 0.367` (aria-valuenow 5, min 1, max 12 → (5-1)/11 = 0.364). The five colours span the entire track while the thumb sits at 36.7% of it, so 63% of the track is painted with colours that already exist — reading as 'drag right to reach these'. The comment at :62-64 claims 'the instrument shows its own state'; it shows a second, contradictory state.
defects.mechanism: F3 — depiction inflation. The extract k-slider pattern was transplanted without its precondition: there, track position plausibly IS cluster index; here the axis is cardinality, so the two meanings cannot coexist on one rail.
defects.reproduction: Navigate to http://localhost:9000/#/generate. Read `getComputedStyle(document.querySelector('div[style*="linear-gradient"]')).backgroundImage` → stops at 0/25/50/75/100%. Read the slider: `document.querySelector('[role="slider"]').getAttribute('aria-valuenow')` → "5", min 1, max 12. Compute the thumb centre as a fraction of the gradient layer's rect → 0.367. The last colour sits at 100% of a track whose thumb is at 36.7%.
defects.proposedCure: Give the rail one unit. Either paint the track neutral and let it be a pure cardinality axis (the honest reading), or redefine the ramp's x-position to mean count. Then adopt the §5 domain-neutral axis composition whole — VISUAL-CONSTITUTION.md:104 names 'Generate count' explicitly and requires label, unit and reserved live value. BLOCKED-ON-GLASS-V8.

defects.defect: Every verb is rendered twice on the same screen: the Dock 'Tools' action bar and the plate chrome each carry Regenerate, Save and Copy with identical icons. The plate cluster is itself three action species within one 29px gap.
defects.evidence: demo/shell/usePaneRouter.ts:191-201 builds the /generate action bar with `{key:"regenerate", icon:RefreshCw}`, `{key:"save", icon:Save}`, `{key:"copy", icon:Copy}`. GenerateControls.vue:157-184 renders `RefreshCw`/`Save`/`Copy` again inside the plate — one `primary-audacious` labelled pill plus two unlabelled `ghost` icon circles. Canon: VISUAL-CONSTITUTION.md:194 — 'Regenerate, Save/Publish and Copy live in ONE Dock control set'; OPTICAL-BENCH-COMPOSITIONS.md:41 — 'one action region ... one Dock action species'; PROPORTION-AUDIT.md:50 PR-06 — 'Three adjacent action species or duplicated selected fills — REMOVE — One action/selection owner across Generate'.

The comment at :120-128 celebrates that 'the orphan toolbar row is DEAD', but the row deleted was the LOCAL one while the Dock set survived; the duplication was inverted rather than resolved, and a fourth interactive species (the invisible title input) joined the same row.

defects.defect: All seven interactive seats in the Generate pane fall below the 44px tap-target floor, including a 12x24 slider thumb that is the primary drag target of the count instrument.

The D-1 seat transposition supplies this for the swatches; the slider thumb needs the same treatment (a transparent hit area around the 12x24 glyph), and the icon buttons need the producer's floor-bearing size rather than `size="sm"`. defects.defect: The plate chrome row wraps at the primary desktop viewport, contradicting the component's own stated design intent that it wraps only at 390. The wrapped result is optically ragged: a 96.5px-tall row with an unowned void at bottom-left.
defects.evidence: GenerateControls.vue:138-142 states: 'The row WRAPS gracefully ... AT 390 the verbs settle onto their own right-aligned line, never a clipped title.' Live measure at 1440x900: `{rowRect:{y:369.7,h:96.5,w:460}, nameTop:379.7, verbsTop:416.2, wrapped:true}`. The comment's premise is wrong — /generate is a two-pane desktop scene (Generate | My Palettes), so the plate content box is 460 CSS px and the row wraps at every supported width. The stated single-line design has no rendered instance anywhere. Visible in safari-desktop-light/generate.png and safari-desktop-dark/generate.png: title hard-left on line 1 with the badge floating far right, line 2 empty on the left with a right-jammed verb cluster.
defects.mechanism: F4 — housing by accretion. The row was designed against an assumed full-width pane that the route composition never provides.
defects.reproduction: Navigate to http://localhost:9000/#/generate at 1440x900. `const p=document.querySelector('[data-generate-plate]'); const row=p.querySelector('div.flex.flex-wrap'); const n=row.querySelector('input'); const v=row.lastElementChild; ({nameTop:n.getBoundingClientRect().top, verbsTop:v.getBoundingClientRect().top})` → 379.7 vs 416.2, i.e. the verb cluster is on a second line at desktop.
defects.proposedCure: Cured for free by D-6: deleting the plate verb cluster leaves title + count, which fits one line at 460px and at 390. No responsive work, no breakpoint, no wrap logic. This is the KISS resolution — the row does not need to wrap gracefully, it needs to stop carrying duplicated verbs. BLOCKED-ON-GLASS-V8.

defects.defect: Nested cartoon casters and a triple boundary: a bordered, cartoon-shadowed plate sits inside a bordered, cartoon-shadowed Card, while the binding composition inventory specifies zero boundaries for this route.
defects.evidence: Live measure — plate: `border "1px solid oklab(0.216128 0.00350075 0.00518669 / 0.12)"`, `bg oklab(0.913295 ...)`, `shadow "oklab(0.28 ... / 0.32) -2px 2px 0px 0px, ..."` (shadow-cartoon-sm). Outer `.pane-scroll-fade`: `bg oklab(0.928268 ... / 0.664)`, `shadow "color(srgb 0.11 0.098 0.09 / 0.8) 8px 8px 0px 0px"`, `border 1px`. OPTICAL-BENCH-COMPOSITIONS.md:75 is binding: `| Generate | [] | none | none | ...` — boundaries [], reserve none. The hard offset drop shadows are visible on both nested surfaces in all four captures.
defects.mechanism: F4 — housing by accretion: three independent boundary expressions (border, fill, cartoon shadow) were each added locally, twice over, because no chassis owned the boundary decision.

defects.proposedCure: Adopt P122 `InstrumentChassis` for the route with the `[]` boundary set and `reserve="none"` that OPTICAL-BENCH-COMPOSITIONS.md:75 binds. That single move deletes the plate border, the plate cartoon shadow and the outer Card together. Cannot be cured by consumer CSS — VISUAL-CONSTITUTION.md:92 forbids the consumer hiding a producer divider. BLOCKED-ON-GLASS-V8 (RC-4).

defects.defect: The route has no `InstrumentChassis`; it is housed in a default Card with a uniform flex stack, so the specimen, the model inspector and the commit action are given identical structural weight. The count instrument additionally has no visible label arm.
defects.evidence: GeneratePane.vue:31 wraps the route body in `<Card tier="resting" class="pane-scroll-fade ...">`; :35 and GenerateControls.vue:119 are both `flex flex-col gap-4`. :219 is a `grid grid-cols-2` local grid. Canon: VISUAL-CONSTITUTION.md:46 binds Generate's outer housing to `InstrumentChassis`; OPTICAL-BENCH-COMPOSITIONS.md:41 requires 'P122 golden: WatercolorDot specimen 61.8033989%; model inspector 38.1966011%' and 'Landmark-neutral chassis; no nested flat Card/local grid'; VISUAL-CONSTITUTION.md:38 — 'Card ... is never the default page primitive.' Label defect measured live: `sliderRowText: "5"` (the count row's entire visible text is a bare numeral) versus `selectLabels: ["Preset","Harmony"]`. VISUAL-CONSTITUTION.md:104 names 'Generate count' in the one Slider composition and requires a label arm. Count is additionally triplicated: `countDepictions: ["DIV|badge-atom.inline-flex|5","LABEL|text-mono-small.font-bold|5"]` plus aria-valuenow.
defects.mechanism: F4 — housing by accretion. The uniform `gap-4` between the three regions is precisely why nothing on the plate reads as hierarchy: everything is one rhythm, so no region can be protagonist.
defects.reproduction: Navigate to http://localhost:9000/#/generate. `document.querySelector('.pane-scroll-fade').className` shows the Card housing; there is no chassis element and no 61.8/38.2 split in the layout. For the label: `document.querySelector('[role="slider"]').closest('.flex.items-center.gap-2').innerText.trim()` → "5", while `[...document.querySelectorAll('.section-label')].map(e=>e.textContent.trim())` → ["Preset","Harmony"].
defects.proposedCure: Adopt `InstrumentChassis` `golden` with three named regions — specimen stage, model inspector, commit action — replacing the three equal siblings. Give the count rail the §5 axis composition whole (label, unit, reserved live value) as Preset and Harmony already have, and delete the badge duplicate from the specimen plate: it is a model INPUT value rendered as specimen metadata on a plate whose stated job is to own only its own chrome. BLOCKED-ON-GLASS-V8 (RC-4).

defects.defect: Dark-mode chrome carries 44% more chroma than light-mode chrome, moving away from the constitutionally required 'restrained neutral pole' and biasing the perceived hue of the specimen sitting on it.
defects.evidence: Measured plate `background-color`, converted to OKLCh — light: `oklab(0.913295 0.00550478 0.0130424)` → L 0.9133, C 0.0142, h 67.1 deg. Dark: `oklab(0.345295 0.0103877 0.0175526)` → L 0.3453, C 0.0204, h 59.4 deg. The dark well is the MORE tinted of the two. VISUAL-CONSTITUTION.md:21 — 'Dark chrome uses the restrained neutral pole. Seed tint is forbidden outside the ambient field, active accent, WatercolorDot/specimen, and pastel Palettes lanes.' The plate is chrome — §2's tier-4 'specimen well: opaque/quiet neutral stage; the specimen supplies color'. Visible in safari-desktop-dark/generate.png and safari-mobile-dark/generate.png, where the plate reads warm brown/taupe rather than neutral.
defects.mechanism: F4 — housing by accretion. The well token was not audited for neutrality in the dark scheme, so the dark arm inherited more warm chroma than the light arm it was derived from.
defects.reproduction: Navigate to http://localhost:9000/#/generate. `const p=()=>getComputedStyle(document.querySelector('[data-generate-plate]')).backgroundColor; const r=document.documentElement; const light=p(); r.classList.add('dark'); const dark=p(); r.classList.remove('dark'); ({light,dark})` → light `oklab(0.913295 0.00550478 0.0130424)`, dark `oklab(0.345295 0.0103877 0.0175526)`; chroma sqrt(a^2+b^2) = 0.0142 vs 0.0204.
defects.proposedCure: Resolve the dark well to the restrained neutral pole so the specimen dots sit on an unbiased ground — this is the one surface in the product where colour fidelity IS the product. Fix at the token/root level, never as a per-instance override (owner edict 5). BLOCKED-ON-GLASS-V8 (RC-4).

defects.defect: The workbench's single most important state change — Regenerate — has no motion register at all. Every specimen surface measures `transition-duration: 0s`, so all five colours, both depictions, the gradient and the seed hard-cut.
defects.evidence: Live measure: plate `{prop:"all", dur:"0s"}`; strip `{prop:"all", dur:"0s"}`; stripSegment `{prop:"all", dur:"0s"}`; gradientLayer `{prop:"all", dur:"0s"}`; `anyKeyframeAnimationInPlate: []`. The dot's own `{prop:"transform, border-radius, filter, box-shadow", dur:"0.2s, 0.6s, 0.2s, 0.2s"}` is the producer morph register and never fires here (`active:scale-95` is dead per D-1; `animate` defaults false). Canon: VISUAL-CONSTITUTION.md:139-140 — 'Spatial continuity uses one producer-owned glass-ui spring register. Color/opacity effects use the corresponding short effect curve; exit is shorter than entry.' The `--animation-slide-sm/md/lg` tokens are unused here.
defects.mechanism: F5 — states nobody drew: the populated happy path is the only designed state, so the transition between two populated states was never considered. Dragging count 5→12 likewise pops seven dots into existence with no entry.
defects.reproduction: Navigate to http://localhost:9000/#/generate and read `['[data-generate-plate]','[data-generate-plate] > :first-child','div[style*="linear-gradient"]'].map(s=>getComputedStyle(document.querySelector(s)).transitionDuration)` → ["0s","0s","0s"]. Click Regenerate and observe the instantaneous hard cut of every colour surface.
defects.proposedCure: Claim the constitutional curve: the specimen swap takes the producer-owned glass-ui short effect curve for colour/opacity, with exit shorter than entry. This is an absence rather than a deletion, so owner edict 6 is not violated — but the register is unclaimed and the tokens unused. Note the latent hazard: `transition-property: all` on the plate/strip/gradient is inert at 0s today, but it is a layout-animating declaration on a container whose height changes with count; it must not be given a duration as-is. BLOCKED-ON-GLASS-V8.

defects.defect: Dead masking fallback: an unreachable zero-length branch in the slider gradient encodes a phantom 'empty' state the design never has.
defects.evidence: GenerateControls.vue:66-67 — `const colors = palette.value; if (colors.length === 0) return "var(--muted)";`. But `palette` is `computed(() => generatePalette(count.value, preset.value, harmony.value, seed.value))` (demo/workbenches/generate/composables/useColorGeneration.ts:26-28) and `count` is bounded to [1,12] by the slider (`:min="1"` at GenerateControls.vue:301). `palette.value.length === count.value >= 1` always, so the branch is unreachable. Owner edict 2 forbids masking fallbacks.

The result is a live model whose own serializer emits CSS that its own parser rejects, and a rail ramp with decreasing sub-stop positions that CSS clamps into a flat band.

LIVE round trip: feeding that CSS back into [aria-label="Gradient CSS"] yields verdict "stop positions must be non-decreasing (hard-stop reordering isn't modeled)". HEADLESS: `npx vite-node` on the demo modules -> serialized `linear-gradient(90deg, oklch(0.75 0.15 145) 70%, oklch(0.7 0.16 200) 50%, oklch(0.65 0.18 265) 100%)` -> re-parse REJECT with the same reason. defects.mechanism: unique-semantic-ownership violated — a model invariant enforced by whichever mutator remembers it rather than by the type that carries it
defects.reproduction: http://localhost:9000/#/gradient -> click the rail at ~50% (adds a stop) -> drag the leftmost handle to ~80% -> read the CSS box: positions descend (80%, 50%, 100%). Retype that same string into the CSS box -> the destructive verdict appears. Headless equivalent: vite-node script calling updateStop-shaped mutation then serializeGradient -> parseGradientCSS.

A model/stops.ts owns the ordering algebra and is the ONLY producer of an `OrderedStops` (readonly branded array): insertStop / moveStop (re-sorts, stable — the CSS-native behaviour a user expects from dragging past a neighbour) / removeStop. serializeGradient, sampleCoalescedStops and parseGradientCSS all take OrderedStops, so the parser's reject-branch becomes unreachable-by-construction instead of a runtime tripwire aimed at the app itself.
