Through the demo parser (npx vite-node): `linear-gradient(90deg, oklch(), blue)` -> UNCAUGHT TypeError; `linear-gradient(90deg, rgb(), blue)` -> UNCAUGHT; `linear-gradient(90deg, color(), blue)` -> UNCAUGHT; `linear-gradient(90deg, red, blue)` -> ok.
defects.mechanism: a published API whose type says ParseResult<CssColor> and whose runtime says "or I throw" — partiality hidden behind a non-null assertion; every consumer written against the type is structurally wrong
defects.reproduction: npx vite-node with `import { parseGradientCSS } from 'demo/workbenches/gradient/composables/gradientParse'; parseGradientCSS('linear-gradient(90deg, oklch(), blue)')` -> uncaught TypeError. Or type that string into the gradient CSS box on a mounted pane.
defects.proposedCure: Totality is the library's contract, not the consumer's try/catch. Replace the non-null assertions in parseFunctionalColor with an explicit empty-body reject (failure(source,"css_syntax",["components"])), and add a property test over {rgb,rgba,hsl,hsla,hwb,lab,lch,oklab,oklch,color} × {""," ","/",",,"} so the surface can never regress to partiality. Do NOT wrap isColorToken in try/catch — that moves the library's contract into its consumer.

defects.defect: The rail axis is mapped twice over two different boxes: the forward map (pointer -> position) is TypeScript over the BORDER box (getBoundingClientRect), while the inverse map (position -> pixels) is CSS calc where `100%` resolves against the PADDING box. They disagree by the 1px border at each end, so the two maps are not inverse.
defects.evidence: GradientStopEditor.vue:75-81 (forward: origin rect.left=224, span rect.width-20=442) vs :55-57 (inverse: `calc(10px + (100% - 20px) * p/100)` where 100%=460, origin=225). LIVE measured: rail x=224.0 width=462.0 borderLeft=1px; handle "Gradient stop at 0%" style.left="calc(0% + 10px)" measured centre cx=235; handle "…100%" style.left="calc(100% - 10px)" cx=675. Forward map at those exact pixels: pos(235)=0.226, pos(675)=99.774. LIVE confirmation: clicking the bar at x=235 — the exact pixel where the 0% handle is painted, at y=railTop+4 so the bar owns the gesture — minted a stop at 0.2%, rendered `style.left="calc(0.2% + 9.96px)"`, cx=235.88.
defects.mechanism: one geometric law with two implementations in two languages over two coordinate origins; the CSS one silently changes meaning if a border or padding is ever added to .gradient-rail
defects.reproduction: http://localhost:9000/#/gradient -> in the console, click the rail at exactly `bar.getBoundingClientRect().x + 11` with clientY = rail top + 4 -> the new stop reads 0.2%, not 0%, and its handle lands ~0.9px right of the pointer. Error is antisymmetric: 0 at 50%, ±0.23% at the ends.
defects.proposedCure: A single useRailGeometry(el, halfPx) exposing toPosition(clientX) and toOffsetPx(position) over ONE box, built on clamp+scale from @mkbabb/value.js/math, with the handle positioned in px rather than calc(%) so the two directions are provably inverse. Ghost and handle then ride the same map by construction.

defects.defect: The self-declared "ONE sampling law" is implemented twice, and the model's interpolation space never reaches the emitted CSS. GradientVisualizer.colorAtPosition re-implements the interval walk / easing / mix that sampleCoalescedStops owns, then injects it into this component as an optional function prop — so the ghost dot and the rail it floats over are painted by two different implementations. Separately, rampGradient emits `linear-gradient(90deg, …)` with no `in <space>` clause, so the browser blends between sub-stops in sRGB while the model's law is oklch; COALESCE_RESOLUTION=32 exists to make that error small, i.e. the coalescing machinery is a polyfill for a CSS Color 4 feature the target browsers already ship.
defects.evidence: useGradientCSS.ts:171-174 declares "The ONE sampling law"; useGradientCSS.ts:175-216 implements it; GradientVisualizer.vue:64-88 re-implements it and passes it as `:color-at` (GradientVisualizer.vue:139) into GradientStopEditor.vue:16. useGradientCSS.ts:223 `return \`linear-gradient(90deg, ${parts.join(", ")})\`` — no interpolation-space clause though model.interpolationSpace is in scope. Live computed --rail-ramp confirms: `linear-gradient(90deg, oklch(75% …) 80.00%, …)`, no `in oklch`.
defects.mechanism: the concept "the colour of this ramp at position p" has no exported home, so it leaks into a component prop; and the model's declared interpolation space is dropped at the serialization boundary, forcing a 32-sample approximation of an exact platform feature
defects.reproduction: Structural — two call sites, both quoted with file:line. The sRGB-vs-oklch deviation between adjacent sub-stops is bounded by the 32-sample density and was NOT separately measured: that half is labelled a HYPOTHESIS.
defects.proposedCure: model/sample.ts exports both sampleAt(model, position) -> AnyColor (the ghost AND the bar-click mint) and sampleRamp(model); model/serialize.ts emits `linear-gradient(<dir> in <space>, …)` and coalesces ONLY across intervals whose easing is non-linear. Since parseGradientCSS seeds every parsed interval to the `linear` preset (gradientParse.ts:295-298), the common case collapses to an exact two-stop `linear-gradient(in oklch, …)`. The colorAt prop is deleted.

defects.defect: Two dead re-export shims and a three-hop alias chain — the exact legacy/dual-path shape edict 2 forbids. useGradientModel.ts:19-29 is a re-export block whose own comment reads "preserve public API surface"; five of its seven names have zero consumers through that door. useGradientInterpolation.ts:13-17 is a second shim whose comment states its purpose is that consumers "keep their import path".
defects.evidence: useGradientModel.ts:19-29 re-exports INTERPOLATION_SPACES, HUE_INTERPOLATION_METHODS, serializeGradient, serializeCoalescedGradient, serializeRailRamp, linearInterval, parseGradientCSS, GradientParseResult, ParsedGradientModel. grep over demo/ test/ e2e/ shows every real consumer bypasses it: GradientEasingEditor.vue:31 imports serializeIntervalRamp direct from useGradientCSS; test/gradient-parse.test.ts:10-11 imports parseGradientCSS from gradientParse and serializeGradient from useGradientCSS direct; test/gradient-v4-consume.test.ts:4-7 imports linearInterval/easingFnOf/sampleCoalescedStops/serializeCoalescedGradient direct. The one live use is INTERPOLATION_SPACES/HUE_INTERPOLATION_METHODS, whose chain is color-session/color-space-meta -> useGradientInterpolation.ts:17 -> useGradientModel.ts:21 -> GradientVisualizer.vue:19, while the sibling workbench does it in one hop: MixConfigBar.vue:18 imports color-space-meta directly. GradientVisualizer.vue also imports interpolateStopColors direct from useGradientInterpolation:23 while importing the constants through the barrel — two doors to one module in one file.
defects.mechanism: migration shims that outlived their migration; a barrel that exists to preserve import paths nobody uses, which is also what forces the type-graph cycle in L-7
defects.reproduction: grep -rn 'serializeGradient|serializeCoalescedGradient|serializeRailRamp|linearInterval|parseGradientCSS|GradientParseResult|ParsedGradientModel' demo/ test/ e2e/ — zero hits importing them from useGradientModel.
defects.proposedCure: Delete both re-export blocks. GradientVisualizer.vue imports color-space-meta directly, exactly as MixConfigBar.vue does. One line of call-site churn, because nothing else uses the door.

defects.defect: demo/ui/ is a 19-module alias barrel over @mkbabb/glass-ui — pure `export { X } from "@mkbabb/glass-ui"` with no variant, no adaptation — and this component's only parent imports the design system through three different doors in one file.
defects.evidence: demo/ui/slider/index.ts is exactly `export { Slider } from "@mkbabb/glass-ui";`; demo/ui/button/index.ts is `export { Button } from "@mkbabb/glass-ui";`; `grep -rl "@mkbabb/glass-ui" demo/ui/ | wc -l` = 19. GradientVisualizer.vue:9 imports Select from "../../../ui/select", :10 Slider from "../../../ui/slider", :12 writeClipboard from "@mkbabb/glass-ui", :13 DockControl from "@mkbabb/glass-ui/dock". glass-ui@7.0.0 publishes ./select and ./slider as first-class subpaths (verified in its package.json exports).
defects.mechanism: a shadow design-system layer (edict 4) built entirely from aliases (edict 2), producing three import doors to one dependency
defects.reproduction: cat demo/ui/slider/index.ts; grep -rl '@mkbabb/glass-ui' demo/ui/ | wc -l
defects.proposedCure: Delete demo/ui/ and import @mkbabb/glass-ui/<subpath> everywhere — glass-ui publishes 60+ subpaths including ./select, ./slider, ./chip, ./button, and the subpath door is the tree-shakeable one.

defects.defect: The gradient domain TYPES live inside the state-factory module, so every module needing only a shape must import the factory — producing two type-graph cycles, and anchoring this component's prop contract on the cycle's apex.
defects.evidence: GradientStop/GradientType/GradientInterval/GradientModelState declared at useGradientModel.ts:33-62, in the same module that builds reactive state (73-193) and re-exports the serializers and parser (19-29). Edges: useGradientModel.ts:15 -> useGradientCSS (VALUE: useGradientCSS, linearInterval); useGradientCSS.ts:31-34 -> useGradientModel (TYPE) = cycle. useGradientModel.ts:16 -> gradientParse (VALUE: parseGradientCSS); gradientParse.ts:23-27 -> useGradientModel (TYPE) = cycle. GradientStopEditor.vue:4 imports type GradientStop from that apex.
defects.mechanism: types homed in a stateful module instead of a leaf; stated precisely — both cycles are TYPE-ONLY, so verbatimModuleSyntax erases them and the RUNTIME graph stays acyclic (model->css, model->parse->css). The declaration graph is cyclic, and it is why L-5's dead barrel cannot be deleted without first moving the types.
defects.reproduction: Read the five import statements above; the cycle is visible in the declaration graph, not in the emitted JS.
defects.proposedCure: A leaf model/types.ts with zero intra-tree imports (only value.js and glass-ui TYPE imports) carrying GradientStop | GradientType | GradientInterval | GradientModelState | OrderedStops. Everything depends on the leaf; nothing depends on the factory except the Vue layer. GradientStopEditor.vue:4 becomes `import type { GradientStop } from "../model/types"` and stops transitively naming the parser, the serializers and vue's watch.

defects.defect: The demo TYPE-resolves value.js against the installed node_modules package while it RUNTIME-resolves against the working-tree dist/ — two byte-different builds in one app — and tsconfig.demo.json#paths advertises three specifiers that package.json#exports does not publish, two of which point at .d.ts files that do not exist.
defects.evidence: tsconfig.demo.json paths declare `@mkbabb/value.js -> ./dist/index.d.ts`, `@mkbabb/value.js/parsing -> ./dist/subpaths/parsing.d.ts`, `@mkbabb/value.js/units -> ./dist/subpaths/units.d.ts`, and have NO entry for `/css` which 10 demo files import. package.json#exports publishes exactly seven subpaths (color, value, css, easing, math, transform, quantize) and NO "." root. `ls dist/index.d.ts dist/subpaths/parsing.d.ts` -> both "No such file or directory". vite.config.ts:41-50 GENERATES its alias set from package.json#exports, so no runtime alias exists for any of the three phantoms. `npx tsc -p tsconfig.demo.json --noEmit --explainFiles | grep subpaths/css` -> "Imported via \"@mkbabb/value.js/css\" … with packageId '@mkbabb/value.js/dist/subpaths/css.d.ts@4.0.0'" (node_modules), while vite aliases to the repo's own dist/. `cmp node_modules/@mkbabb/value.js/dist/subpaths/css.js dist/subpaths/css.js` -> DIFFERENT.
defects.mechanism: the type gate and the runtime gate are different artefacts, so the exports map is not the single authority; this is the crack through which L-2 shipped — the .d.ts promises ParseResult while the .js throws
defects.reproduction: ls dist/index.d.ts dist/subpaths/parsing.d.ts ; cmp node_modules/@mkbabb/value.js/dist/subpaths/css.js dist/subpaths/css.js ; npx tsc -p tsconfig.demo.json --noEmit --explainFiles | grep subpaths/css
defects.proposedCure: Delete the tsconfig.demo.json paths block entirely and make node_modules/@mkbabb/value.js a workspace link to the repo, so ONE artefact serves both types and runtime and package.json#exports is the single gate. A demo that dogfoods a different build than it typechecks is not a dogfood.

defects.defect: Every drag frame emits update:position TWICE, and the comment asserting why it does not is factually wrong. Pointer capture retargets events to the handle but does not stop them bubbling to the bar, so the handle's pointermove handler runs and then the bar's `draggingId` branch runs on the same event with the same value.
defects.evidence: GradientStopEditor.vue:91-99 — the branch comment reads "Fallback path while a handle drag is live (capture sits on the handle)." Handle listener at :266, bar listener at :206. MEASURED LIVE: a listener added to the bar element counting pointermoves whose target is not the bar, during a four-step handle drag, returned handleMovesThatAlsoReachedBar = 4 of 4. Cost per frame: two model rewrites and two full recomputes of railRampCSS + coalescedCSS (32 colour mixes each).
defects.mechanism: a branch documented as a fallback that is in fact the always-path — DOM bubbling is not blocked by setPointerCapture
defects.reproduction: In the page console: `bar.addEventListener('pointermove', e => { if (e.target !== bar) n++ })`, then dispatch four bubbling pointermoves on a handle -> n === 4.
defects.proposedCure: Either terminate onHandlePointerMove with e.stopPropagation(), or — in the greenfield lattice — a useRailGesture FSM owns capture and dispatch and the bar carries no drag branch at all.

defects.defect: The selected stop has two write channels for one fact, and the outer defineModel that receives them is bound by nobody.
defects.evidence: GradientStopEditor.vue:26 defineModel("selectedId"); :129 `selectedId.value = id` (channel 1) immediately followed by :130 `emit("select", id)` (channel 2). GradientVisualizer.vue:140 binds `v-model:selected-id="selectedStopId"` AND :144 `@select="(id) => selectedStopId = id"` — writing the same ref twice. GradientVisualizer.vue:51 declares `defineModel<string|null>("selectedStopId")` but its only parent renders `<GradientVisualizer ref="visualizerRef" />` at GradientPane.vue:24 with no binding.
defects.mechanism: dual write path for one piece of state (edict 2) plus a defineModel with no parent binding — a local ref wearing a public-API costume (edict 3 contrivance)
defects.reproduction: Read GradientStopEditor.vue:129-130 against GradientVisualizer.vue:140,144 and GradientPane.vue:24.
defects.proposedCure: Delete the `select` emit and the @select handler; demote selectedStopId to a plain ref until a parent actually binds it.

defects.defect: An optional collaborator that is never actually optional, with a masking fallback: colorAt has one call site which always passes it, yet is declared optional with `= undefined` and consumed as `colorAt?.(p) ?? null`, silently degrading the add-affordance to a transparent dot instead of failing.
defects.evidence: GradientStopEditor.vue:6 `const { stops, railRamp, colorAt = undefined } = defineProps<{ … colorAt?: (position:number)=>string }>()`; :71-73 `hoverPos.value !== null ? (colorAt?.(hoverPos.value) ?? null) : null`; :219-221 falls back to a bare `var(--alpha-checker)` ghost. Sole call site: GradientVisualizer.vue:139 `:color-at="colorAtPosition"` — always provided.
defects.mechanism: masking fallback (edict 2) plus a no-op `= undefined` destructure default (edict 3)
defects.reproduction: grep -rn 'GradientStopEditor' demo/ -> one call site (GradientVisualizer.vue:14,136) which always passes :color-at.
defects.proposedCure: Under L-4 the prop disappears: the component calls sampleAt(model, p) from the model module. Either way there is no branch left to mask.

defects.defect: The component hand-rolls clamp twice while the library it exists to dogfood publishes clamp AND scale on @mkbabb/value.js/math — and sibling demo files already import them, so the demo carries two idioms for one primitive.
defects.evidence: GradientStopEditor.vue:80 `Math.round(Math.max(0, Math.min(100, (x/span)*100))*10)/10`; :177 `Math.max(0, Math.min(100, stop.position + delta))`; gradientParse.ts:282 `Math.min(100, Math.max(0, s.position))`. Published: src/subpaths/math.ts exports clamp, scale (src/foundation/math.ts:2 and :7 — `scale(value, fromMin, fromMax, toMin, toMax)` is literally the rail's axis map). Already dogfooded elsewhere: demo/picker/controls/SpectrumCanvas/SpectrumCanvas.vue:37 and demo/workbenches/mix/MixAnimationCanvas/composables/mixStage.ts:15 both `import { clamp } from "@mkbabb/value.js/math"`. vite.config.ts:63-66 states the constitutional position that the demo is the dogfood proof.
defects.mechanism: inconsistent proof-of-use for a published subpath — the demo simultaneously proves and disproves that /math is the home for range primitives
defects.reproduction: grep -rn 'Math.max(0, Math.min' demo/ vs grep -rn 'from "@mkbabb/value.js/math"' demo/
defects.proposedCure: import { clamp, scale } from "@mkbabb/value.js/math" in the new useRailGeometry.ts (L-3) and in gradientParse.ts. Zero new surface; it deletes hand-rolled arithmetic and reduces the axis map to one expression.

defects.defect: A track-with-thumbs instrument built entirely from raw divs and buttons plus 88 lines of scoped CSS re-deriving focus rings, forced-colors handling and touch-target inflation — while glass-ui 7.0.0 publishes ./slider, ./chip and ./button, and the component's own comments locate it inside that vocabulary.
defects.evidence: GradientStopEditor.vue:196-198 comment: "a pill-silhouette instrument (T-46 — the glass-ui slider-track rounding register)"; :335 "the ONE --focus-ring-inner/-outer recipe, focus-ring.css". Implementation: :200 raw <div class="gradient-rail …">, :229-273 raw <button class="rail-handle …">, :284-300 raw <button class="rail-remove-chip …">, :305-392 scoped CSS re-deriving box-shadow focus rings, @media (forced-colors: active), and the ::before hit-expander. glass-ui@7.0.0 package.json exports include "./slider", "./chip", "./button" (its Slider wraps reka-ui SliderRoot, which supports an array model and therefore N thumbs).
defects.mechanism: design-system primitives re-created in the consumer (edict 4) with per-callsite styling recipes rather than root-level ones (edict 5)
defects.reproduction: Read GradientStopEditor.vue:190-392 against `python3 -c "import json;print(list(json.load(open('node_modules/@mkbabb/glass-ui/package.json'))['exports']))"`.
defects.proposedCure: Honest bound: a gradient rail is genuinely more than a Slider (it inserts/deletes thumbs and each thumb carries its own colour fill), so the cure is not "use Slider" — it is landing a variant="rail" (or a SliderThumb content slot) IN glass-ui and consuming it, with the focus-ring recipe and the --touch-target inflation moving into the producer's SliderThumb root where every consumer inherits them.

defects.defect: The bar-click add path destroys the authored-literal invariant that the parse path is explicitly built to protect: a minted stop carries a 15-significant-digit machine literal in a different oklch dialect from the authored stops beside it, in a readout the user is meant to copy.
defects.evidence: gradientParse.ts:17-18 calls literal preservation "a welcome corollary" and serializeGradient (useGradientCSS.ts:158) keeps stop.cssColor verbatim. LIVE, after one rail click: `linear-gradient(90deg, oklch(0.75 0.15 145) 0%, oklch(74.979999519572% 0.150060001441 145.240005765141deg) 0.2%, oklch(0.65 0.18 265) 100%)` — lightness re-expressed as a percentage, hue re-expressed with a deg unit, 15 significant digits. Source: GradientVisualizer.vue:79-85 interpolateStopColors -> demo/color-session/color-utils.ts:23 colorToCss.
defects.mechanism: a full-precision debug serializer (colorToCss) used as an authoring serializer — one concept, two literal grammars, both alive in the same string
defects.reproduction: http://localhost:9000/#/gradient -> click anywhere on the rail -> read the CSS box.
defects.proposedCure: model/literal.ts exports one formatColorLiteral(color, precision) used by the mint, the parse fallback and the readout alike, so the model carries a single dialect.

result.axis: CHALLENGE-C — implementation defect hunt on demo/workbenches/generate/GenerateControls.vue (pinned consumer under the CARRY-LEDGER §D glass BJ W4 hold)
result.modelObserved: Opus 5 (claude-opus-5[1m]) — the model this seat was explicitly spawned with; declaration honoured, seat not inherited.
result.strongestDefect: D1 — the five specimen swatches render as inert `<span aria-hidden="true">` with `pointer-events:none` and ZERO attached Vue listeners: `tag="button"`, `@click="copyColor(css)"` and `:aria-label` are all silently dropped because glass-ui 7.0.0's WatercolorDot has no `tag` prop, sets `inheritAttrs:false`, and forwards only `class`/`style`. Per-swatch copy is entirely absent from the shipped build, and — since PaletteColorStrip is also aria-hidden — the generated palette has no textual representation anywhere in the plate (WCAG 1.1.1 failure on the component's primary output).
result.negativeProof: N/A — verdict is DEFECTIVE. (Proved-sound sub-areas are recorded in the report's "Sound by measurement" section: no defineModel/stale-read path; the compiled render proves `count.value = v[0]` so the slider does write; no ValueUnit, no HSV round-trip, no rAF loop (animate defaults false and glass-ui's loop is pauseWhenHidden+respectReducedMotion), no listeners/observers/timers to leak, no WebGL, no parsing, all three type imports are `import type`, seedHex domain-safe, and REPORT.json records 0 console errors / 0 page errors / 0 overflow / 0 nameless buttons on /#/generate across all four matrices.)

defects.defect: The five palette swatches are inert, AT-invisible spans: `tag="button"`, `@click="copyColor(css)"` and `:aria-label` are all dropped by glass-ui 7.0.0's WatercolorDot (no `tag` prop; `inheritAttrs:false`; only class/style forwarded; hardcoded `<span aria-hidden="true">` with inline `pointer-events:none`). copyColor() is unreachable dead code while `cursor-pointer`/`active:scale-95` still advertise the affordance.
defects.evidence: demo/workbenches/generate/GenerateControls.vue:199-208 vs node_modules/@mkbabb/glass-ui/dist/components/watercolor-dot/WatercolorDot.vue.d.ts (props: color|variant|animate|cycleDuration|range|seed — no `tag`) and dist/watercolor-dot.js (`inheritAttrs: !1`, `o("span", { "aria-hidden": "true", … pointerEvents: "none" })`). Live probe at http://localhost:9000/#/generate returned {"tag":"SPAN","ariaHidden":"true","ariaLabel":null,"tagAttr":null,"pointerEvents":"none","tabIndex":-1,"vueListeners":[]}; sw.focus() then document.activeElement===sw === false. PaletteColorStrip.vue:3-4 is also aria-hidden/role=presentation.
defects.mechanism: glass-7 API break unmigrated by the W44 adoption commit f2c8f565; `inheritAttrs:false` silently swallows consumer listeners and ARIA — a class of failure Vue's type system cannot surface.
defects.reproduction: Load http://localhost:9000/#/generate; evaluate [...document.querySelectorAll('[data-generate-plate] .generate-swatch')].map(el=>({tag:el.tagName,ariaHidden:el.getAttribute('aria-hidden'),pointerEvents:getComputedStyle(el).pointerEvents,vueListeners:Object.keys(el._vei||{})})) — all five are SPAN / "true" / "none" / []. Clicking a swatch copies nothing.
defects.proposedCure: Transpose the seat, don't patch the prop: the glass-7 dot is a FACE, not a SEAT. Wrap it in a real `<button type="button" :aria-label="`Copy ${css}`">` that owns the click, the accessible name and the focus ring, with `<WatercolorDot>` as its already-aria-hidden child. Restores verb, name and keyboard operability in one move with no per-instance styling. Same fix retires the identical dead `tag="button"` seats at MixSourceSelector.vue:168,215 and CurrentPaletteEditor.vue:98. BLOCKED-ON-GLASS-V8.

defects.defect: The component's ONLY automated oracle is red and CI never runs it. o20-generate-plate.spec.ts test 2 fails on an irreconcilable serialization mismatch (raw `oklch(83.35…% … 333.86…deg)` stamped vs computed `oklch(0.833541 0.0926939 333.865)`), and no GitHub workflow invokes `test:e2e`. The surviving test 1 is vacuous.
defects.evidence: `npx playwright test e2e/smoke/oracles/o20-generate-plate.spec.ts --project=smoke --reporter=line` → "1 failed / 1 passed (38.1s)", diff at spec line 105. `grep -rn "playwright test|e2e" .github/workflows/*.yml` → no output; ci.yml runs lint, 2× vue-tsc, build, `npm test` (=vitest run), verify-packed-surface only. Stamp source: color-chips/sample.ts:88 + generate-color.ts:240.
defects.mechanism: A gate that is both RED and unexecuted is not a gate; the spec asserts across two different color encodings, and its one green leg asserts only visibility, so every real defect (D1, D3, D4) passes through it.
defects.reproduction: npx playwright test e2e/smoke/oracles/o20-generate-plate.spec.ts --project=smoke  (output pasted above). Named green-keeping mutations for test 1: no-op save(); no-op copyColors(); delete paletteName+emit; break the count slider; break the harmony Select; render swatches as inert aria-hidden spans (shipped); flatten all three button registers (shipped).
defects.proposedCure: One serialization on both sides — parse the stamped stops through the app's own parser before comparing, or stamp the computed encoding. Then wire `npm run test:e2e` into ci.yml (this leg is OUTSIDE the §D hold — it touches no demo/ file) and add the missing behavioural legs: swatch click copies, Save carries the typed name, the slider moves the palette.

defects.defect: The plate's editable title is discarded at the emit seam. GenerateControls emits `save: [colors, name]` but GeneratePane's handler declares only `colors` and hardcodes `pm.createPalette("Generated Palette", …)`. Renaming the plate does nothing; the UI shows one name and saves another.
defects.evidence: demo/workbenches/generate/GenerateControls.vue:44-50,102-104 (comment: "this emit is already truthful") vs demo/workbenches/generate/GeneratePane.vue:14,19. Live: typed "MY CUSTOM NAME", clicked Save → bodyText "My Palettes 2 (2 saved) … Generated Palette 5   Generated Palette 5".
defects.mechanism: TypeScript cannot catch a handler with fewer parameters — it is assignable — so the emit contract is unenforced at the only seam that matters.
defects.reproduction: At http://localhost:9000/#/generate set the plate input to 'MY CUSTOM NAME' via a native input event, click the 'Save palette' button, read the Palettes pane: the saved entry reads 'Generated Palette'.
defects.proposedCure: Consume the emitted name (`function onSave(colors: string[], name: string)`), and guard the empty string at the emit site rather than the sink — a decorative rename field is worse than no field. BLOCKED-ON-GLASS-V8.

defects.defect: `variant` is not a glass-ui 7.0.0 Button prop. `variant="primary-audacious"` and two `variant="ghost"` fall through $attrs as junk DOM attributes; all three plate verbs render at the default `emphasis="secondary" tone="neutral"`, so the documented "deliberate-primary register" and the two ghost icon buttons are visually identical.
defects.evidence: GenerateControls.vue:158,167,176 vs dist/components/button/Button.vue.d.ts (`ButtonProps { emphasis?: "primary"|"secondary"|"quiet"|"text"; tone?; size?; iconOnly?; … }` — no `variant`). `grep -rl "primary-audacious" node_modules/@mkbabb/glass-ui/dist --include="*.js"` → nothing. Live DOM: all three buttons carry `data-emphasis=secondary` plus a raw `variant=…` attribute and the `glass-wash glass-capsule glass-capsule-hover` classes glass-ui applies only to neutral primary/secondary. Visual: shots/safari-desktop-light/generate.png — Regenerate reads identically to the icon buttons, unlike the dock's real primary Login pill.
defects.mechanism: Vue fallthrough attrs make an unknown component prop a silent no-op that vue-tsc cannot flag; the W44 glass-7 adoption migrated the pin but not the emphasis axis — demo-wide (27 files use `variant=`, only 2 occurrences of `emphasis=` exist).
defects.reproduction: Load /#/generate; evaluate [...document.querySelectorAll('[data-generate-plate] button')].map(b=>[...b.attributes].map(a=>a.name+'='+a.value).join(' | ')) — every row shows data-emphasis=secondary alongside the dead variant attribute.
defects.proposedCure: `emphasis="primary"` on Regenerate, `emphasis="quiet"` on the two icon buttons; delete `variant` outright — no alias, no compat shim (edict 2). Structurally, only an eslint rule (or making the barrels typed wrappers) can turn unknown component attributes into errors; relay the API break to the glass-ui BH inbox. BLOCKED-ON-GLASS-V8.

defects.defect: Both clipboard verbs discard the discriminated CopyResult that glass-ui deliberately made non-boolean, and the component emits no success or failure feedback for any async verb — no aria-live, no toast, nothing.
defects.evidence: GenerateControls.vue:106-113 (`await writeClipboard(...)`, result unbound) vs dist/composables/dom/useClipboard.d.ts: `type CopyResult = {ok:true}|{ok:false;reason:"clipboard-api"|"no-api"}` with the doc "Returns the discriminated result … rather than a lossy boolean, for identical call ergonomics: const { ok } = await writeClipboard(text)". `grep -rn "aria-live|role=\"status\"|toast" demo/workbenches/generate/` → no matches. Live save probe produced no announcement and no in-plate change.
defects.mechanism: A Result whose failure arm is dropped is indistinguishable from success; on an insecure origin (LAN dev with server.host:true, and the mbabb.fi.ncsu.edu/colors/ deployment) `no-api` is swallowed and the user believes the copy landed.
defects.reproduction: NONE for the failure arm (I did not force an insecure origin) — the dropped-Result and absent-live-region facts are CONFIRMED by the pasted contract and the empty grep; the insecure-origin consequence is labelled a hypothesis.
defects.proposedCure: Route Save and both Copy verbs through glass-ui's `useClipboard()` and bind its `status` ref to ONE `aria-live="polite"` region inside the plate — one region, three verbs, no per-instance chrome, no new shared/ dir. BLOCKED-ON-GLASS-V8.

defects.defect: Two unchecked `as PresetName` / `as HarmonyName` casts of reka-ui's `AcceptableValue` (which admits null), with asymmetric failure modes: an invalid preset THROWS inside the `palette` computed and blanks the pane; an invalid harmony silently yields an EMPTY palette that save() will happily persist.
defects.evidence: GenerateControls.vue:75-81; generate-color.ts:220,227 (`GENERATION_PRESETS[preset]` unguarded, then `p.l[0]`) and :101-146 (`switch` with NO default → returns []). Executed against an esbuild bundle of the real module: `invalid preset -> THREW TypeError: Cannot read properties of undefined (reading 'l')`; `invalid harmony -> array len 0`; `count 0/-1/NaN -> array len 0`; `count 1.5 -> array len 2`.
defects.mechanism: A cast is not a check. The throw escalates from a computed read into the render function — the shipped-blank class already in this repo's record; the silent-[] arm is worse still because save() at :103 emits [] with no guard at either end.
defects.reproduction: node on a bundled demo/color-session/generate-color.ts: generatePalette(5,"nope","golden",1) throws TypeError; generatePalette(5,"vibrant","bogus",1) returns []. Reachability of a non-PresetName value THROUGH reka-ui is a HYPOTHESIS — I did not force reka-ui to emit null; the crash mechanism itself is CONFIRMED.
defects.proposedCure: Validate at the boundary against the already-exported PRESET_NAMES / HARMONY_NAMES and ignore anything else — one narrow function per select, zero casts. In the core, make `generateHues` exhaustive (a `never` arm) and the preset lookup non-optional, so the two paths cannot diverge into crash-vs-silence again. BLOCKED-ON-GLASS-V8.

defects.defect: The plate chrome row wraps at 1440 px desktop — overflowing by exactly 3 px — while the component's own comment claims the wrap only happens "at 390". The count badge is flung to the far right of line 1 and the plate grows ~40 px taller than designed at every width below ~1500 px.
defects.evidence: GenerateControls.vue:138-142 (the claim) and :148 (`flex-1 basis-[10rem]`). Measured live at the audit's own matrix (capture.mjs:45 → 1440×900): {"plateW":462,"rowContentW":436,"input":{"y":363,"w":398},"badge":{"x":643,"w":30},"cluster":{"y":399,"w":233},"wrapped":true}. Hypothetical line sum 160+30+233+16 = 439 > 436. Visible in shots/safari-desktop-light/generate.png and safari-mobile-dark/generate.png.
defects.mechanism: `flex-wrap: wrap` breaks lines on hypothetical main sizes (flex-basis) BEFORE `flex-1` shrinking applies, so a 160 px basis forces a break the shrink would have absorbed.
defects.reproduction: Load http://localhost:9000/#/generate at viewport 1440×900; measure the `.flex-wrap` row's input and `.ml-auto` cluster bounding boxes — cluster.y (399) > input.y (363): wrapped.
defects.proposedCure: `basis-0` (or drop `basis-*` and keep `flex-1 min-w-0`) so the title lane's hypothetical size is zero and the row breaks only when the verb cluster itself cannot fit — one class, and the comment then becomes true. BLOCKED-ON-GLASS-V8.

defects.defect: The component's single contribution to the visual audit's 5 small tap targets on /#/generate is the 12×24 px count-slider thumb. The other four rows belong to the co-mounted Palettes/slug surfaces, not to this component.
defects.evidence: REPORT.json safari-desktop-light /#/generate a11y.smallTapTargets includes {"w":12,"h":24,"tag":"span","label":"Color count"}; live probe confirms {"tag":"SPAN","w":12,"h":24,"role":"slider","aria":"Color count","valuemin":"1","valuemax":"12"}. Width from glass-ui CSS `.slider-thumb { width: calc(var(--slider-thumb-size,1rem) * .75) }`. The 160×23 input row reports label "" whereas this component's title input carries aria-label="Palette name" and measures 398×31 live — so it is NOT this component's.
defects.mechanism: Producer token `--slider-thumb-size` sets the thumb geometry; the consumer instantiates it without widening. WCAG 2.2 SC 2.5.8's spacing exception plausibly applies (sole target on its row, >24 px clearance), hence MINOR rather than a hard failure.
defects.reproduction: Load /#/generate, evaluate document.querySelector('[role=slider]').getBoundingClientRect() → width 12, height 24.
defects.proposedCure: Raise `--slider-thumb-size` at the glass root (a producer token set, never a per-instance override) or record the 2.5.8 spacing-exception judgement in writing so the audit row stops re-litigating. Relay the 12 px default to the glass-ui BH inbox.

defects.defect: The in-file performance claim that the dropdown previews are "sub-millisecond" is false by 2.3×, measured; the preview generators are unmemoised plain template calls re-executed on every render of the open menu.
defects.evidence: GenerateControls.vue:90-93 (the claim) and compiled.js:267,312 (`stops: presetStops(p)` / `stops: harmonyStops(h)` inside the render, not computeds). Measured on an esbuild bundle in node 26: `per generatePalette(5): 0.1752 ms`; `per 10-row preset menu render @count 12: 2.2628 ms`.
defects.mechanism: Synchronous library work in the render function, priced by a comment nobody re-measured; the harmony menu adds ~1.4 ms on the same path.
defects.reproduction: node on a bundled demo/color-session/generate-color.ts, 50 iterations of the 10-preset × count-12 loop → 2.2628 ms mean.
defects.proposedCure: Memoise per (count, harmony, seed) in a computed keyed map — or state the real number. The seed-exact truth law itself is sound (both sides call generatePalette with identical args on a pure mulberry32 core); only the cost claim is wrong. BLOCKED-ON-GLASS-V8.

defects.defect: Dual import paths to one package inside one file: Select*/Slider/Button/Badge arrive via `../../ui/*` alias barrels while writeClipboard and WatercolorDot are imported directly from `@mkbabb/glass-ui`. The barrels add nothing but a second spelling.
defects.evidence: GenerateControls.vue:3-15; `cat demo/ui/select/index.ts demo/ui/slider/index.ts demo/ui/button/index.ts` → three pure `export { … } from "@mkbabb/glass-ui";` lines.
defects.mechanism: Edict 2 (no aliases/dual paths). Operationally this is WHY D4 survived review: the `../../ui/button` spelling reads like a local component whose props are the demo's own business.
defects.reproduction: NONE required — the two import forms are on adjacent lines of the same file.
defects.proposedCure: One import path to `@mkbabb/glass-ui`; retire the alias barrels this file touches rather than adding a third spelling. BLOCKED-ON-GLASS-V8.

defects.defect: Masking optional-chains over a guaranteed defineExpose surface, across three call layers typed `Ref<any>`, serving a duplicated command surface: the dock action menu repeats Regenerate/Save/Copy — the same three verbs the plate owns.
defects.evidence: GenerateControls.vue:115 (`defineExpose({ regenerate, save, copyColors })`); GeneratePane.vue:22-26 (`controlsRef.value?.regenerate?.()`); demo/shell/usePaneRouter.ts:196-198 (`paneRefs.generate.value?.save?.()`) with `PaneActionRefs.generate: Ref<any>` at :109. GeneratePane.vue:12 also uses `ref<InstanceType<typeof GenerateControls>|null>` where Vue 3.5's `useTemplateRef` is the idiom (edict 7).
defects.mechanism: `?.` after a method defineExpose guarantees is a masking fallback (edict 2): a rename degrades to a silent no-op with no error at any of the three layers, and `any` removes the last check. The duplicate dock surface is also why o20's "the orphan row is dead" clause is vacuous — the second Regenerate merely happens to be in a closed menu at assert time.
defects.reproduction: NONE — structural; read the three cited call sites.
defects.proposedCure: Type the exposed surface (drop `Ref<any>`), delete the `?.` chains, and decide whether the dock duplicate survives at all — one verb, one seat. Swap the pane's manual ref for `useTemplateRef`. BLOCKED-ON-GLASS-V8.

defects.defect: The colour count is rendered twice ~200 px apart — a `<Badge>{{ count }}</Badge>` in the plate chrome and the slider's own `{{ count }}` label — and the badge carries no accessible name, so AT announces a bare "5".
defects.evidence: GenerateControls.vue:150-152 and :287-291; live probe `badgeText: ["5"]`.
defects.mechanism: Duplicate display of one reactive value; the copy nearest the control that changes it is the useful one.
defects.reproduction: Load /#/generate and read the plate: '5' appears in the chrome badge and again as the slider's left label.
defects.proposedCure: Drop the badge (the slider label is adjacent to its control) or give it a name; fold this into the D7 layout cure, which frees the 30 px that forces the wrap.

defects.defect: NOT A DEFECT — recorded to prevent one being filed. The transparent-track + hand-rolled gradient underlay looks like an edict-5 per-instance override plus an edict-3 contrivance, but it is producer-sanctioned and PINNED by the same hold that pins this file.
defects.evidence: GenerateControls.vue:292-307 vs docs/tranches/V/reformation/CARRY-LEDGER.md:73-77: "Preserve … transparent K/count underlays … add no `--track-bg`, v7 alias, copied CSS or local mask." Live: gradient div and slider root both 434×24; `.slider-track` computes background rgba(0,0,0,0); spectrum `.slider-range` computes backdrop-filter: none in Chromium (via the demo restatement at demo/styles/foundation.css:571-574).
defects.mechanism: The obvious 'simplification' (`--slider-track-bg: countSliderGradient`) is exactly what the §D hold forbids until the v8 seam rename lands.
defects.reproduction: NONE — the arrangement is measured correct; this row exists so a later seat does not 'fix' it and break the hold. I also make no claim about the paler ramp seen in the Safari shots: that is continuous interpolation between 5 stops, and I could not reproduce any blur in Chromium.
defects.proposedCure: Leave untouched. At Glass 8, migrate the property NAME only: `--slider-track-bg` → `--glass-slider-track-background`, preserving pixels, and retire foundation.css:571-574 only once both installed public CSS entries carry backdrop-filter:none AND -webkit-backdrop-filter:none and a real browser computes both as none.

defects.defect: Route drift observed twice: http://localhost:9000/#/generate settled and then the app navigated itself to #/gradient — once ~3 s after load, once on a viewport resize. Not this component (it owns no routing), but it will flake every oracle for this route.
defects.evidence: Two Playwright evaluates returned {"url":"http://localhost:9000/#/gradient","plate":false,"bodyText":"Gradient\n\nBuild gradients with per-interval easing and CSS output. …"} after navigating to #/generate; the second followed page.setViewportSize({width:1440,height:900}).
defects.mechanism: Shell-level: the dock/view restoration appears to race the hash route.
defects.reproduction: page.goto('http://localhost:9000/#/generate') then wait ~3 s, or resize the viewport — location.href becomes #/gradient. Non-deterministic across runs (a 1.5 s probe succeeded, a 1.8 s probe drifted).
defects.proposedCure: Belongs to the mega-tranche's shell lane, not to this component: make the hash route the single source of truth for the active pane and let restoration write to it rather than around it.

result.axis: CHALLENGE-D — design of demo/workbenches/gradient/GradientVisualizer/GradientStopEditor.vue
result.modelObserved: Opus 5 (claude-opus-5[1m], 1M-context arm) — the tier explicitly declared for this seat; declaration present and matched, not inherited, not undeclared.
result.strongestDefect: D-1 — the rail carries TWO different position axes: the ramp is painted across the full border-box (`background-size:100% 100%`, `serializeRailRamp` emits `linear-gradient(90deg,…)`) while handles/ghost/hit-maths ride an inset `[11, W-11]` track (`handleLeft`, `getPosition`, `HANDLE_HALF=10`). They agree only at 50%. Measured: the 0% swatch sits 11px = 2.38% of the ramp (desktop, W=462) / 3.40% (mobile, W=324) right of where the ramp paints 0%; a click at rail-fraction 12% mints a stop labelled 10% and 88% mints 90%. The file's own doc-comment (lines 8–13) asserts "handles, add-ghost and ramp share one axis by construction" — the exact opposite of what ships. This one mechanism explains the wrong ghost colour, the wrong minted colour, the wrong click→position map, and the end-of-rail dead bands.
result.negativeProof: Not applicable to the verdict (DEFECTIVE), but recorded as the seat's honest negative findings in §15 of the report: motion is fully tokenised and resolves (computed `box-shadow 0.2s cubic-bezier(0.4,0,0.2,1), transform 0.44s linear(…)`, no ad-hoc durations, animates only transform/box-shadow — no layout-forcing property); prefers-reduced-motion is honoured by inheritance from glass-ui `dist/styles/utilities/a11y-overrides.css` whose `transition-property: opacity, color, background-color, border-color, box-shadow !important` outranks the inline shorthand and drops `transform` (measured `transitionDuration 0.1s` under reducedMotion:reduce); every token the file names resolves non-empty (`--spring-snappy-duration` = `calc(0.44s * 1)`, `--focus-ring-inner/-outer`, `--alpha-checker`, `--touch-target`, `--radius-pill`, `--shadow-sm`); the dual-contrast focus ring composes with `--shadow-sm` exactly as claimed; the visual REPORT's "20×20 small tap target" rows are a border-box measurement artefact — the real hit region is 24×24 on fine pointers (elementFromPoint sweep `hitSpanX [-12,11,24]`), so WCAG 2.5.8's minimum is met at rest; RTL correctly does not mirror per VISUAL-CONSTITUTION §5.2; zero console errors, zero page errors, zero horizontal overflow on /#/gradient across all four Safari matrices and all 11 probe runs; `verbatimModuleSyntax` and Vue 3.5 idiom (useTemplateRef, reactive props destructure) are clean. Evidence gap declared: WebKit does not implement forced-colors, so the shipped `forced-colors-desktop` matrix renders in full colour and the component's `@media (forced-colors: active)` block at :353–359 is UNTESTED — not claimed as a finding.

defects.defect: On touch, tapping inside a SELECTED stop handle's own advertised hit region DELETES the stop. The remove chip (top-11, 44px below the rail) carries the same always-on hit inflation (--touch-target 2.75rem = 44px) as the handle, and the selected handle's scale(1.25) also scales its ::before expander to 55px, so the two invisible regions overlap with the destructive one on top (chip z-20 vs handle z-10). No undo, no confirmation, no visual cue.
defects.evidence: iPhone 14 / WebKit, evidence/p4.mjs T11: `T11 before {"n":3,"pos":["0","50","100"]}` → select mid stop → `T11 after tap at handle-centre + 20px {"n":2,"pos":["0","100"]}`. Hit map from p3.mjs T7: `handle-hit offsets -26 → 13 | chip-hit offsets 14 → 40` (offsets from handle centre); `expander 44px x 44px`. Source: GradientStopEditor.vue:288 (top-11, z-20), :262 (scale 1.25), :374-391 (::before expander), :385-391 (coarse 44px).
defects.mechanism: two invisible expanded hit targets stacked on one axis, with the destructive one painted on top
defects.reproduction: node docs/tranches/V/megatranche/audit/components/wb-gradient-stopeditor/evidence/p4.mjs — block T11 (iPhone 14 context against http://localhost:9000/#/gradient)
defects.proposedCure: The remove verb leaves the rail entirely and lives in the selected-stop inspector, where VISUAL-CONSTITUTION §5 already puts lifecycle actions ('Full detail, rename/lifecycle/export actions and durable operation state live in the selected inspector'). This is the same transposition that cures D-4 and D-9. If a rail-local remove must survive, it goes on the opposite side of the rail from the drag axis and the two expanders are made mutually exclusive.

defects.defect: No ordering invariant: a drag can carry a stop across its neighbour, leaving stops[] non-monotonic. sampleCoalescedStops then emits DESCENDING percentages into a CSS linear-gradient, which the browser clamps into a hard band, and the per-interval easing curves silently re-pair because intervals are keyed by array index rather than by the stop pair.
defects.evidence: evidence/p4.mjs T10: `T10 stops after cross {"n":4,"pos":["0","29","8","100"],"centers":[235,362.6,270.6,675]}`; painted rail percentages `[…,26.36, 29, 27.1, 25.2, 23.3, 21.4, 19.5, 17.6, 15.7, 13.8,…]` with `descendingPairs=[[12,29,27.1],…,[21,11.9,10]]`. Screenshot evidence/D02-cross-drag-hard-band.png shows the resulting seam. Source: useGradientModel.ts:127-131 (updateStop never sorts; addStop at :118 does), useGradientCSS.ts:195-200 (pos = s0.position + t*(s1-s0), negative range), GradientVisualizer.vue:64-88 (colorAtPosition assumes sorted). Interval labels stay index-keyed: p2.log T3 `["1 → 2","2 → 3"]`.
defects.mechanism: an ordinal identity that exists in the UI vocabulary ('stop 2', '1 → 2') but has no representation the model defends
defects.reproduction: node docs/tranches/V/megatranche/audit/components/wb-gradient-stopeditor/evidence/p4.mjs — block T10
defects.proposedCure: The model owns the ordinal: re-sort on every position commit and re-key intervals to the stop PAIR, or clamp a dragged stop into (prev, next). Only then is VISUAL-CONSTITUTION §5.2's explicit reorder grammar (Space grabs, 'position of total' announcement, Escape cancels) implementable at all.

defects.defect: The instrument has two different position axes for one domain quantity. The ramp is painted across the full border-box; handles, the add-ghost and the pointer inverse ride an inset [HANDLE_HALF, W-HANDLE_HALF] track. They agree only at 50%. The file's own doc-comment asserts they 'share one axis by construction'.
defects.evidence: evidence/p1.mjs: `BAR x=224.00 w=462.00`, handle 'Gradient stop at 0%' `centerX=235.00` (ramp paints 0% at x=224), handle 'Gradient stop at 100%' `centerX=675.00` (ramp paints 100% at x=686) → 11px = 2.38% of the ramp. evidence/p5.mjs (iPhone 14): bar w=324, centres 44/346 → 11px = 3.40%. evidence/p3.mjs T6: ten clicks at rail fractions .12 .20 .28 .36 .44 .52 .60 .72 .80 .88 produce `pos ["0","10","19","27","35","44","52","60","73","81","90","100"]` — click at 12.0% mints 10%, click at 88.0% mints 90%. Source: GradientStopEditor.vue:317-326 (.gradient-rail background-size 100% 100%, origin/clip border-box), useGradientCSS.ts:266 (linear-gradient(90deg,…)), GradientStopEditor.vue:55-57 (handleLeft), :75-81 (getPosition), :8-13 and :49-53 (the false claim).
defects.mechanism: two coordinate systems for one domain quantity, neither derived from the other
defects.reproduction: node docs/tranches/V/megatranche/audit/components/wb-gradient-stopeditor/evidence/p1.mjs (geometry) and evidence/p3.mjs block T6 (click→position map)
defects.proposedCure: One axis, expressed once. Either paint the ramp on the inset track (background-position: 11px 0; background-size: calc(100% - 22px) 100% — the pill caps then hold flat terminal colour, which is what a 0%/100% stop actually means), or put the handles on the full-width axis and inset the rail's silhouette instead. HANDLE_HALF must be read from the rendered handle box rather than re-declared as a JS literal (D-13).

defects.defect: The remove chip has ZERO reserved geometry: it is absolutely positioned 28px outside the component's own 40px layout box, consumes the parent's entire gap-5, and paints across (and visibly cuts) the next section's rule. Selecting a stop therefore repaints another section's boundary.
defects.evidence: evidence/p2.mjs T2 (desktop): `editorRoot y 200.7→240.7 (h=40)`, `chip y 244.7→268.7 (h=24, z-index 20)`, `hr (section) y 260.7→261.7`, `hrIsUnder "BUTTON.rail-remove-chip"` — the chip is what paints at the rule's own y. Screenshots evidence/D04-chip-crosses-section-rule.png and evidence/D05-twelve-stops-empty-rings.png. Violates PROPORTION-AUDIT.md §5.3: 'Renderer, icon or touch footprints may reserve collision space only on the axis where collision exists.' Source: GradientStopEditor.vue:288 (top-11, absolute), GradientVisualizer.vue:135 (flex flex-col gap-5 parent), :148 (the hr).
defects.mechanism: an absolutely-positioned affordance with no block-axis reservation inside a gapped flex column
defects.reproduction: node docs/tranches/V/megatranche/audit/components/wb-gradient-stopeditor/evidence/p2.mjs — block T2
defects.proposedCure: Same transposition as D-3 — the chip leaves the rail for the selected-stop inspector. If it stays, the editor root reserves its own footprint via padding-block-end; it never borrows the parent's gap.

defects.defect: The stop swatch is a tautology and therefore carries no information: at a stop's own position the ramp already IS that colour, so a colour-filled dot painted on the ramp has zero figure-ground separation and reads as an empty ring. At working density the instrument is a row of holes. Selected state differs only by scale 1.25 and border-white vs border-white/80.
defects.evidence: Shipped audit shot docs/tranches/V/megatranche/audit/visual/shots/safari-desktop-light/gradient.png (and the crop evidence/D05-rest-state-rings-desktop-light.png) — both terminal handles render as white rings with the rail showing through. evidence/D05-twelve-stops-empty-rings.png: twelve stops, twelve empty rings, no specimen anywhere; the selected 6th is findable only by measuring. Violates VISUAL-CONSTITUTION §4.1 'Selected, failed, pending, withdrawn and disabled states are never colour-only. Role, accessible name, state/value … are explicit.' Source: GradientStopEditor.vue:247 (background: linear-gradient(cssColor,cssColor) over the ramp), :236-240 (border-white vs border-white/80), :60-63 (scale ladder).
defects.mechanism: a specimen placed on a ground that is definitionally identical to it
defects.reproduction: Open docs/tranches/V/megatranche/audit/visual/shots/safari-desktop-light/gradient.png; or node evidence/p3.mjs block T6 which produces evidence/D05-twelve-stops-empty-rings.png
defects.proposedCure: The constitutional geometry: the stop rank moves OFF the meniscus onto a quiet seat rail beneath it. Each seat is a geometric button on a neutral well carrying a WatercolorDot face (D-6), so the face reads as a specimen, the meniscus stays the unbroken 'continuous liquid-color rail' of §2, and selection is expressed by the seat rather than by 5px of scale.

defects.defect: Species violation: the handle is a hand-rolled circular swatch (`background: linear-gradient(cssColor, cssColor), var(--alpha-checker)`) where the binding constitution names a WatercolorDot face inside an enclosing geometric seat, and names Gradient as an executor site for exactly that law.
defects.evidence: VISUAL-CONSTITUTION.md §7 Gradient: 'Each WatercolorDot stop is a face inside an enclosing geometric button/seat; that seat alone carries selection, focus, drag and accessible state.' §4.2 names the sites: '…Generate, Mix and Gradient sites.' Measured: `grep -rln "WatercolorDot" demo/ | wc -l` → 19 files (Mix, Picker, Dock, Generate, Extract, ColorSpaceSelector, palettes, EmptyState…); `grep -rn "WatercolorDot" demo/workbenches/gradient/` → no matches. Source: GradientStopEditor.vue:229-247. Also violates owner edict 4 (glass-ui is the design system; reuse existing component-type names).
defects.mechanism: local re-implementation of an available producer species
defects.reproduction: grep -rln "WatercolorDot" demo/ ; grep -rn "WatercolorDot" demo/workbenches/gradient/
defects.proposedCure: Consume the producer species. With D-5's seat rail the face is WatercolorDot and the seat is the named button that owns selection/focus/drag — exactly the shape §4.2 already ratified for this site.

defects.defect: The keyboard grammar implements a third of the specified one and the accessibility tree carries no state at all: Home, End, ArrowUp, ArrowDown, PageUp/Down and the Space-grab are no-ops; the handle has no role, no aria-valuenow/min/max, no aria-pressed, and its accessible name carries no ordinal. A screen-reader user can move a stop but can never learn which one is selected or how many exist.
defects.evidence: evidence/p2.mjs T4 (focus handle 0, press each key, read aria-labels): Home → no change; End → no change; ArrowUp → no change; ArrowDown → no change; PageUp → no change; Space → no change; ArrowRight → 'Gradient stop at 1%'; Shift+ArrowRight → 'Gradient stop at 11%'. evidence/p1.mjs attribute dump: `attrs: data-stop-id, type=button, aria-label="Gradient stop at 0%", class, style`, `role: null`. VISUAL-CONSTITUTION §5.2 mandates 'Home=0%, End=100%; announce stop identity, percentage, ordinal' and Up/Down at the same signed step. Source: GradientStopEditor.vue:173-187 (only ArrowLeft/ArrowRight/Delete/Backspace/Escape), :234 (aria-label without ordinal).
defects.mechanism: a bespoke button impersonating a value control

result.axis: CHALLENGE-L — library structure (module boundaries, ownership, dependency direction, public surface) for demo/workbenches/generate/GenerateControls.vue
result.modelObserved: Claude Opus 5 (1M context) — exact model ID claude-opus-5[1m]. Matches the explicit Opus 5 declaration this seat was spawned with; the seat is declared, not inherited.
result.strongestDefect: L-0 — `<Button variant="…">` is a dead prop against glass-ui 7.0.0, whose Button has no `variant` prop at all (its axis is `emphasis` ∈ primary|secondary|quiet|text, orthogonal to `tone`). The prop falls through to $attrs as an inert DOM attribute, so all three Buttons in this file render at DEFAULT emphasis — the declared "deliberate-primary register" (line 153-155) is never applied, and it is visible in the shipped screenshot as three buttons of identical pale weight. Repo-wide: 51 Button call sites on the dead API vs 2 on the live one. The Glass 6→7 rename landed in the producer and never landed in the consumer; vue-tsc is green over it because fallthrough attrs are not a type error. Compounding cause: glass-ui 7 is internally inconsistent — Slider and Badge KEPT `variant` (so this file's `Slider variant="spectrum"` and `Badge variant="secondary"` are correct, sitting lines away from three that are not), which is why no author could infer the difference and no tool told them.
result.negativeProof: Not applicable to the overall verdict (DEFECTIVE), but recorded so the next seat does not re-run it — the following were interrogated and found SOUND: (1) value.js consumption in the cone is genuinely correct — zero `@src/*` and zero `../src/` reaching across all nine files in the transitive closure; the only specifiers used are `@mkbabb/value.js/color` and `@mkbabb/value.js/css`, both real `package.json#exports` keys, both `RESOLVED` under bare `node --input-type=module -e "await import(…)"`. A real consumer could write them verbatim; the T.W1 dogfood keystone holds on this axis. (2) `verbatimModuleSyntax` is clean — all three type-only imports are `import type` (lines 21, 32, 33). (3) `Slider variant="spectrum"` and `Badge variant="secondary"` ARE valid glass-ui 7 props (`SliderVariant = "standard" | "spectrum"`; Badge VARIANT keys `default|secondary|outline`) — a blanket variant→emphasis sweep would break both, so L-0's cure must be surgical. (4) `WatercolorDot`'s deep subpath import is necessary, not gratuitous — it is genuinely absent from the root barrel (`grep -c WatercolorDot dist/index.d.ts` → 0). (5) The route is runtime-clean: `/#/generate` across all four Safari matrices shows 0 page errors, 0 console errors, 0 horizontal overflow, main count 1, no blank/near-blank (REPORT.md rows 124/139/154/169). (6) `useColorGeneration` (43 lines) is genuinely focused and correctly layered — the U-F47 relocation of the pure math down to the shared color layer was the right call, honestly documented. (7) The pinned SHA-256 4f95c57c… still MATCHES — no coordination-boundary drift, and no source edit landed from this seat.

defects.defect: `<Button variant="…">` is inert against glass-ui 7 — the component's declared visual hierarchy never renders. glass-ui 7.0.0's ButtonProps has NO `variant` prop; its axis is `emphasis` (primary|secondary|quiet|text) plus `tone`. Undeclared props fall through to $attrs as inert DOM attributes, so GenerateControls' three Buttons all render at default emphasis. Repo-wide epidemic: 51 dead-prop Button sites vs 2 on the live API.
defects.evidence: node_modules/@mkbabb/glass-ui/dist/components/button/Button.vue.d.ts:4 `export type ButtonEmphasis = "primary"|"secondary"|"quiet"|"text"` with no `variant` member in ButtonProps. `grep -o 'variant' dist/button-Bu9F4uU6.js | wc -l` → 0; `grep -o 'emphasis' …` → 6. `grep -o 'data-emphasis[^ {,]*' dist/components/button/styles.css | sort -u` → only the 4 emphasis values. `grep -c 'audacious' dist/components/button/styles.css` → 0. Call sites: GenerateControls.vue:158 variant="primary-audacious", :166 variant="ghost", :176 variant="ghost". Census: `grep -rn '<Button' -A4 demo/ | grep 'variant=' | wc -l` → 51 (16 ghost, 15 outline, 2 primary-audacious); `grep -rln 'emphasis=' demo/ | wc -l` → 2. `npx vue-tsc -p tsconfig.demo.json --noEmit` → exit 0, no output (green with all 51 sites present).
defects.mechanism: A design-system prop contract enforced by neither the type system nor the runtime. The producer may rename any prop and every consumer keeps compiling and keeps rendering something — worse than breaking, because it is invisible. Aggravated by glass-ui 7's own internal inconsistency: Slider and Badge kept `variant`, only Button moved to `emphasis`.
defects.reproduction: Read docs/tranches/V/megatranche/audit/visual/shots/safari-desktop-light/generate.png: "Regenerate" and the two icon buttons beside it render at IDENTICAL pale weight — three default-emphasis buttons, not one saturated primary flanked by two ghosts. Confirm the cause with the four greps above against glass-ui 7.0.0 in node_modules.
defects.proposedCure: Producer-first, and it belongs in the Glass 8 release gate (G-3), not a 51-site consumer sweep that rots on the next rename: glass-ui closes ButtonProps to unknown attributes, or asserts in dev when a `variant` attr reaches a Button root. Acceptance: `<Button variant="ghost">` FAILS at typecheck or first render, reproducibly in CI. Secondarily reconcile the axis naming across Button/Slider/Badge, since the inconsistency is what made 51 sites wrong by default. Only then sweep the consumers (variant="primary-audacious" → emphasis="primary", variant="ghost" → emphasis="quiet"), leaving Slider/Badge `variant` untouched.

defects.defect: The save seam silently discards the palette name the user types. GenerateControls emits `save: [colors, name]` and passes paletteName, but its sole consumer GeneratePane declares a one-parameter handler and hardcodes the literal "Generated Palette". The editable plate title has no effect on the saved palette.
defects.evidence: GenerateControls.vue:48-50 `defineEmits<{ save: [colors: string[], name: string] }>()`; :102-104 `emit("save", [...palette.value], paletteName.value)`. GeneratePane.vue:14-20 `function onSave(colors: string[])` — `name` never bound — then `pm.createPalette("Generated Palette", paletteColors)`. TypeScript permits a narrower handler arity, so nothing fails at build. The in-file comment at GenerateControls.vue:44-47 asserts the wire exists ("this emit is already truthful") — the emit is truthful; the wire was never landed.
defects.mechanism: The concept "the name of the thing being saved" has two homes — a ref inside the child and a string literal inside the parent — joined by a Vue emit whose payload the parent is free to ignore silently.
defects.reproduction: Prior seat's live run against http://localhost:9000/#/generate: typed PROBE-NAME-XYZ into the plate title, clicked Save, read localStorage → {"hasProbeName": false, "hasHardcoded": true, sample name:"Generated Palette", slug:"generated-palette-5fd9d37c"}. Static confirmation needs no browser: GeneratePane.vue:14 never destructures the second emit parameter. My own independent re-probe was abandoned — the shared Playwright MCP browser was concurrently driven by parallel seats (my tab was navigated to #/mix mid-evaluation), and I discarded the run rather than report contaminated telemetry.
defects.proposedCure: CURABLE NOW (lands in GeneratePane.vue, outside the pin): bind the second parameter. The idiomatic cure is the L-6 transposition — the name belongs in a provided generate-session where there is no seam to drop it across, making the defect unrepresentable.

defects.defect: `demo/ui/` is a nineteen-directory pure re-export alias layer over @mkbabb/glass-ui — the forbidden legacy shim surface. GenerateControls crosses it four times, and the file simultaneously uses three different specifier registers for one package.
defects.evidence: All 19 of 19 subdirs are shim-only: `for f in demo/ui/*/index.ts; do [ -z "$(ls $(dirname $f) | grep -v '^index.ts$')' ] && echo SHIM-ONLY; done` lists all nineteen. `cat demo/ui/button/index.ts` → `export { Button } from "@mkbabb/glass-ui";` (entire file); select/slider/badge/card identical in form. GenerateControls.vue:3-12 imports via the shims, :14 via the glass-ui root barrel directly, :15 via the granular subpath — three registers in twelve lines. glass-ui publishes 74 subpaths; this file uses one.
defects.mechanism: A migration that stopped one step short of the root: the shadcn tree was kept alive as an alias surface. Violates edict 2 (no aliases/shims/dual paths) and edict 3 (no wrapper layers that need not exist), at directory scale. It also actively hides which design system and which version a call site binds to — the proximate reason L-0 went unnoticed.
defects.reproduction: The classification loop above; `cat demo/ui/*/index.ts`. Honest scoping: glass-ui declares sideEffects:["*.css"] and its root barrel imports no CSS, so Rollup can tree-shake it — I measured no production bundle penalty and do not claim one. The defect is structural and legibility, not perf.
defects.proposedCure: Delete demo/ui/ entirely; import each component from its granular glass-ui subpath (@mkbabb/glass-ui/button, /select, /slider, /badge, /card). One specifier form, one hop, the version and prop vocabulary visible at every call site. CURABLE NOW for the ten other consumers; BLOCKED-ON-GLASS-V8 for this file's four lines.

defects.defect: Feature → feature-internal edge: the generate workbench reaches into the palette BROWSER feature's card cluster for PaletteColorStrip, and into palettes/types for PaletteColor. The component states the layering law it then breaks, five lines apart.
defects.evidence: GenerateControls.vue:16 `import { PaletteColorStrip } from "../../palettes/browser/card"` — whose own barrel header (card/index.ts:1) calls it "palette-browser · card cluster — hardened public surface". Three workbenches cross it: `grep -rn 'palettes/browser/card' demo/ | grep -v '^demo/palettes/'` → generate:16, mix/MixSourceSelector.vue:8, extract/ExtractWorkbench.vue:200. palettes/types is consumed by 6 files across 3 workbenches. GenerateControls.vue:23-24 documents the correct edge ("the feature consumes it UP-from-shared (feature → shared, correct)") seven lines below the violation. The adapter at :55-57 fabricates a `position` field the strip never reads (PaletteColorStrip.vue reads only .css and .weight) — pure boundary tax.
defects.mechanism: Unique semantic ownership violated. "Render an ordered set of colors as adjacent bands" has two homes — PaletteColorStrip (weighted, full-bleed, filed under a feature) and PreviewStrip (capped, chip-sized, filed under the shared layer) — and this component imports BOTH. A primitive consumed by two workbenches plus the palettes catalog is a shared primitive misfiled inside one feature.
defects.reproduction: The two greps above; read demo/palettes/browser/card/PaletteColorStrip.vue and confirm `position` is never referenced.
defects.proposedCure: Move PaletteColorStrip.vue to demo/color-session/color-chips/ beside PreviewStrip (the module whose header already declares itself "ONE focused common module for the multi-feature chip grammar, never a per-pane copy"), retype it on `readonly string[]` + optional `weights?: number[]`, and let the palettes feature do the PaletteColor[]→string[] adaptation at its own edge — it is the only consumer holding a PaletteColor[]. The stripColors adapter and the palettes/types import then vanish from this file. Also lift PaletteColor/Palette to the shared domain layer.

defects.defect: Library-shaped code stranded in the demo: the library owns palette EXTRACTION (quantize) but not palette SYNTHESIS. demo/color-session/generate-color.ts is 243 lines of pure, Vue-free, DOM-free, seeded color math whose only outside calls are three published value.js primitives — structurally indistinguishable from src/quantize.ts, which IS published.
defects.evidence: demo/color-session/generate-color.ts:33-34 imports only `@mkbabb/value.js/color` and `@mkbabb/value.js/css`; ships 10 OKLCh presets, 6 harmony algorithms, a hue-range clamp, seeded palette + single-color generators. src/quantize.ts is 139 lines of the same shape and is published via src/subpaths/quantize.ts as @mkbabb/value.js/quantize. `grep -rli 'harmony|generatePalette|mulberry' src/` → no output. package.json keywords already advertise "palette". Consequence is measurable: `grep -rl '\.\./demo/' test/*.ts | wc -l` → 10 of 22 library test files reach across into demo internals. generate-color.ts itself has NO unit test — only e2e/smoke/oracles/o20-generate-plate.spec.ts — so clampHueToRanges (:156-184, with a non-obvious wrapping-range branch and a proportional remap) is covered only through a browser.
defects.mechanism: Wrong direction of ownership. The demo exists to dogfood the library; instead it privately owns a capability the library should publish, so no consumer can reach it and no published type describes it. Nearly half the library test suite is testing demo modules because those modules are unpromoted library code.
defects.reproduction: The greps above; compare src/quantize.ts against demo/color-session/generate-color.ts for Vue/DOM dependencies (both have none).
defects.proposedCure: Promote to src/palette/{presets,harmony,generate}.ts and publish @mkbabb/value.js/palette alongside /quantize, returning Result in the house failure-explicit idiom (generatedCss currently converts three Results into exceptions, inverting the library's own contract). mulberry32 moves to src/math. demo/color-session/generate-color.ts and prng.ts then delete, and useColorGeneration becomes what its docstring already claims: a ~25-line reactive wrapper over a published subpath.

defects.defect: The demo's proof of the published subpath surface is not a proof. tsconfig.demo.json's hand-rolled `paths` block has drifted from package.json#exports in BOTH directions — 3 phantom entries pointing at nonexistent .d.ts files and rejected by Node, and 2 real published subpaths left unmapped — and where they overlap, `paths` substitution means TypeScript never consults the exports map at all.
defects.evidence: exports keys (7, no `.` root): ./color ./value ./css ./easing ./math ./transform ./quantize. tsconfig paths (8): @mkbabb/value.js, /color, /parsing, /math, /easing, /units, /transform, /quantize. In tsconfig but NOT exported: /parsing, /units, and the bare root. Exported but NOT in tsconfig: /value, /css. `node --input-type=module -e "await import(…)"` → `@mkbabb/value.js` ERR_PACKAGE_PATH_NOT_EXPORTED, `/parsing` ERR_PACKAGE_PATH_NOT_EXPORTED, `/units` ERR_PACKAGE_PATH_NOT_EXPORTED, `/css` RESOLVED, `/color` RESOLVED. `test -f dist/index.d.ts || echo MISSING` → MISSING; same for dist/subpaths/parsing.d.ts and units.d.ts. The comment at tsconfig.demo.json:37-41 is false three ways: it claims a bare `.` root (absent), a "CLOSED 8-key set" (it is 7), and that it "Mirrors the vite.config.ts runtime self-alias generated from the same map" (it does not).
defects.mechanism: Two sources of truth for one map — one generated, one hand-kept — with no test holding them equal. vite.config.ts:41-50 generates its alias set from package.json#exports and says so ("GENERATED (not hand-rolled) so the alias set can never drift"); the typecheck half is the hand-written copy that drifted. Delete "./color" from exports and the demo typecheck stays GREEN while every real consumer breaks at install — the demo's 25 /color imports are therefore not a proof of the published surface.
defects.reproduction: The node import probe and the three `test -f` checks above. Prior seat additionally captured `tsc --traceResolution` showing two imports in the SAME file (generate-color.ts) resolving by two different mechanisms: /color via paths substitution with no Package ID, /css via "Entering conditional exports" with Package ID @mkbabb/value.js@4.0.0.
defects.proposedCure: CURABLE NOW: delete the @mkbabb/value.js* paths block entirely. Self-reference resolution already works (the /css trace proves it, with a real Package ID), so all seven subpaths would resolve through the genuine exports map and removing a subpath would turn the demo typecheck RED — which is what a dogfood is for. If a paths block must survive, generate it from package.json#exports the way Vite does. Add one test/dist/ gate asserting Object.keys(exports) ≡ the resolvable specifier set.

defects.defect: The shell→feature action seam is five hops of `any` and double optional-chain masking: the dock action bar reaches into this component's instance by name to invoke Regenerate/Save/Copy.
defects.evidence: Chain: demo/color-picker/App.vue:317 `const generatePaneRef = ref<any>(null)` → demo/shell/usePaneRouter.ts:106-110 `interface PaneActionRefs { generate: Ref<any>; gradient: Ref<any>; mix: Ref<any> }` → usePaneRouter.ts:196-198 `handler: () => paneRefs.generate.value?.regenerate?.()` → GeneratePane.vue:23-25 `regenerate: () => controlsRef.value?.regenerate?.()` → GenerateControls.vue:115 `defineExpose({ regenerate, save, copyColors })`. Those three Ref<any> are the ONLY `any` in usePaneRouter.ts (`grep -n 'any' demo/shell/usePaneRouter.ts` → lines 108, 109, 110 only).
defects.mechanism: Ownership, not typing. useColorGeneration() is instantiated INSIDE GenerateControls (:35-42), so generation state is owned by a component instance and the shell has no way to reach it except by grabbing the instance. The `any` is the symptom; the state's home is the disease. The `?.` on the METHOD (as distinct from the instance) exists only to swallow a contract mismatch — a masking fallback in the sense edict 2 forbids: rename `regenerate` anywhere in the chain and the dock button silently no-ops with no type error, no runtime error, no console warning.
defects.reproduction: Read the five sites above. The same three verbs are ALSO rendered declaratively on the plate (:157-184), so one concept has both a declarative and an imperative path and only the imperative one can break silently.
defects.proposedCure: Invert it. useColorGeneration becomes a pane-scoped session provided by GeneratePane under a typed InjectionKey — the pattern already used in this very tree (CSS_COLOR_KEY, LIBRARY_PORT_KEY, EDIT_TARGET_KEY). The pane declares its action descriptors as typed DATA ({key, icon, title, handler}[]) and hands them to the router, which injects rather than reaches. PaneActionRefs, both defineExpose blocks, controlsRef, App.vue's three ref<any>, and all six ?. masks delete. Pays three times: elegance, correctness (L-1 becomes unrepresentable — save reads the name from the same session the input writes), and performance (session computeds replace per-render template calls, L-9).
