defects.reproduction: Read REPORT.json and filter rows where route == "/#/generate"; the entry appears in all four matrices. Prior seat confirmed live, scoped to the plate subtree at 1440×900: [{tag:"span", role:"slider", w:12, h:24, aria:"Color count"}].
defects.proposedCure: BLOCKED-ON-GLASS-V8 (G-1): glass-ui expands the Slider thumb hit-area to ≥24×24 via a pseudo-element hit box, preserving the 12px visual. Nothing changes in this file.

defects.defect: The plate chrome row wraps at full desktop width, while the in-file comment documents the wrap as a 390px small-screen behaviour — misleading the next author who tunes the row.
defects.evidence: GenerateControls.vue:138-142 claims "at 390 the verbs settle onto their own right-aligned line". Prior seat measured live at 1440×900: chromeRow width 460, height 97, kids = [input top:10 w:398, badge top:12 w:30, verb-cluster top:47 w:233] — the verb cluster sits 35px BELOW the name row at full desktop width, because the pane's inner width is 460px, not the viewport's 1440. Visible in shots/safari-desktop-light/generate.png as a two-line plate with dead space right of the title.
defects.mechanism: A prose assertion documenting a state that does not hold — the same decay class as L-5's stale paths comment and L-12's stale alias citation. The wrap is graceful as designed; only the comment is wrong. Note this reads worse than it should because L-0 leaves the verb cluster with no visual weight to anchor it.
defects.reproduction: Read shots/safari-desktop-light/generate.png and observe the two-line plate at desktop; re-measure the chrome row's child offsets at 1440×900.
defects.proposedCure: BLOCKED-ON-GLASS-V8 (the fix is inside the pinned file): correct the comment to the measured default behaviour, or retune basis-[10rem] so the row genuinely holds one line at pane widths ≥460px.

defects.defect: The dropdown preview cost claim ("10 rows × 5-12 library generations is sub-millisecond") holds at the default count 5 and fails by 2.8× at count 12; the two truth functions are plain template calls, not computeds, so every re-render of the mounted SelectContent recomputes all sixteen strips.
defects.evidence: GenerateControls.vue:88-93 carries the claim. Prior seat measured the bundled core on node/V8: one generatePalette(count=5) 0.097ms; count=12 0.362ms; preset dropdown open 10 strips @count=5 = 0.871ms (claim HOLDS); preset dropdown open 10 strips @count=12 = 2.80ms (claim FAILS). presetStops/harmonyStops at :94-100 are plain function calls — Vue memoizes neither. PreviewStrip caps at 7 segments (STRIP_SEGMENT_CAP, a PRIVATE constant in PreviewStrip.vue), so at count 12 the host pays to generate five colors the chip discards; the sibling RAMP form does publish its budget (RAMP_SAMPLE_COUNT is exported from color-chips/sample.ts and re-exported from the barrel).
defects.mechanism: Asymmetric public surface in the chip module — the ramp tells hosts its sampling budget, the strip hides it — so the host cannot size its truth function honestly. Desktop-V8 numbers; WebKit on the mobile matrix would be materially slower, putting a count-12 dropdown open into multi-frame territory.
defects.reproduction: Bundle demo/color-session/generate-color.ts with esbuild and time generatePalette across counts; read PreviewStrip.vue for the private cap and color-chips/sample.ts for the exported RAMP_SAMPLE_COUNT.
defects.proposedCure: NOT "generate only 7" — generateHues for `analogous` derives its step from count, so a 7-generation is not the prefix of a 12-generation and truncating would break the seed-exactness law the file rightly insists on. Instead: export STRIP_SEGMENT_CAP so the host can decide honestly, and wrap the two truth functions in computeds keyed on (count, preset, harmony, seed) — which the L-6 session transposition delivers for free.

defects.defect: "Palette stops → CSS rail" is hand-rolled in four places with no owner, the markup sandwich is duplicated verbatim across two workbenches, and the mechanism violates the shared chip module's own SAMPLING LAW — visibly, in the same card.
defects.evidence: GenerateControls.vue:65-73 and demo/workbenches/extract/composables/useExtractSession.ts:101-112 are near-byte twins: same `length===0 → "var(--muted)"` guard, same `length===1?50:(i/(len-1))*100`, same `.toFixed(0)`, same `linear-gradient(to right, ${stops.join(", ")})`. Two more copies at demo/workbenches/mix/MixResultDisplay.vue:112 and demo/picker/controls/ComponentSliders/ComponentSliders.vue:195. The MARKUP is duplicated too: GenerateControls.vue:292-307 vs ExtractControls.vue:18-33 are character-identical on the structural lines (`relative flex-1 h-6 flex items-center` wrapper, `absolute inset-0 rounded-full overflow-hidden h-6` rail div, `Slider variant="spectrum" class="relative w-full"`, `:style="{ '--slider-track-bg': 'transparent' }"`). That last line is a per-instance override of a design-system token, which edict 5 forbids by name; `grep -rn -- '--slider-track-bg' demo/` finds 4 override sites. demo/color-session/color-chips/sample.ts:5-12 legislates the opposite: "ramps are k-sample discrete stops built from THE LIBRARY's mixColors interpolation — NEVER CSS `in <space>` gradient interpolation, because the preview must show what THE APP computes, not what the browser's engine would … One mechanism for all rows, no engine divergence."
defects.mechanism: The concept "a slider whose track IS a color ramp" has no home, so it lives four times in demo features and zero times in the design system that owns Slider. The component then runs TWO contradictory mechanisms for "show a color sequence" — the law-abiding library-sampled PreviewStrip in its dropdowns (:245, :274) and the forbidden raw CSS gradient in its slider track (:72), eleven lines above the import of the module that forbids it.
defects.reproduction: Visible in shots/safari-desktop-light/generate.png: the plate strip shows five clean hard segments (green·lavender·gold·cyan·pink) while the count slider directly below shows the browser's sRGB interpolation between them — the muddy grey-green between green and lavender is a color the app never computed. The instrument and its readout disagree in the same card. Confirm the duplication with `grep -rn 'linear-gradient(to right' demo/`.
defects.proposedCure: BLOCKED-ON-GLASS-V8 (G-2): the rail belongs in glass-ui as a first-class affordance on the existing Slider — a `trackStops: readonly string[]` prop or a `track` slot — with sampling routed through color-chips/sample.ts so the slider obeys the same SAMPLING LAW as the chips and the visible engine divergence disappears. Both workbenches then delete their rail div, their --slider-track-bg override, and their gradient computed; the whole idiom collapses to `<Slider :track-stops="stops" />`.

defects.defect: `.generate-swatch` is a per-component class hook whose only rules are hand-added to two global selector lists that already carry the general seam `[data-color-surface]`.
defects.evidence: GenerateControls.vue:205 sets class="generate-swatch …"; the file has no <style> block (`grep -c '<style' GenerateControls.vue` → 0). Its only rules live in demo/styles/foundation.css:689 and :834, inside @media (forced-colors: active) and @media print, enumerated alongside `.swatch-row > *`, `.shadow-swatch`, `.watercolor-swatch` and — crucially — `[data-color-surface]`, the attribute hook that already expresses the concept.
defects.mechanism: Cross-cutting media rules do belong in a global sheet (edict 6 is not violated — nothing was deleted); the defect is shape. Because the component's swatches do not carry the existing general attribute, two more class names had to be appended to two separate hand-maintained lists, and the next color-painting component will require a third append.
defects.reproduction: `grep -rn 'generate-swatch' demo/` → 1 consumer (GenerateControls.vue:205), 2 global rule lists (foundation.css:689, :834); read both blocks and observe [data-color-surface] already present in each.
defects.proposedCure: BLOCKED-ON-GLASS-V8 (G-4): have WatercolorDot carry data-color-surface — a producer one-liner, since the dot is a glass-ui primitive. Both global lists then shrink to the attribute selector alone, and .generate-swatch deletes along with .shadow-swatch and .watercolor-swatch.

defects.defect: The composable's docstring cites `@composables/color/generate-color`, a path alias W43 (RF-15) deleted.
defects.evidence: demo/workbenches/generate/composables/useColorGeneration.ts:8 cites `@composables/color/generate-color`. tsconfig.demo.json:32-34 records the kill: "the demo `@…` path aliases were killed … No @styles/@components/@utils/@lib/@composables/@assets project alias survives." The real import two lines below is `../../../color-session/generate-color`.
defects.mechanism: Comment decay. Trivial in isolation, but it is the third stale prose assertion in this component's closure — with L-5's "CLOSED 8-key set" comment and L-8's "at 390" wrap comment. The component is heavily commented and those comments are load-bearing for the next author, so their decay rate is itself a structural risk here.
defects.reproduction: Read useColorGeneration.ts:8 against its own import at :17, and against tsconfig.demo.json:32-34.
defects.proposedCure: CURABLE NOW (outside the pin — the file is composables/useColorGeneration.ts, not GenerateControls.vue): cite the real relative path. More durably, prefer structural expression over prose: the layering claims these comments make should be enforced by an import-boundary lint rule, not asserted in text that no tool checks.

result.axis: CHALLENGE-C — implementation defects in demo/workbenches/generate/GenerateControls.vue (glass BJ W4 pinned consumer; no source edits authorized)
result.modelObserved: Opus 5 (1M context) — exact model id claude-opus-5[1m]. Spawned with an explicit Opus 5 declaration; served tier matches. Not an inherited or undeclared seat.
result.strongestDefect: C-1 — the per-swatch copy verb does not exist in the shipped build. GenerateControls.vue:199-208 passes tag="button", :aria-label and @click to glass-ui 7.0.0's WatercolorDot, which declares 6 props (no `tag`), no emits, sets inheritAttrs:false and hand-forwards ONLY class/style, then renders a hardcoded <span aria-hidden="true"> with inline pointer-events:none that wins the style merge. Live DOM: tag=SPAN, ariaHidden=true, ariaLabel=null, tabIndex=-1, pointerEvents=none; the plate has exactly 4 tabbables and the 5 swatches contribute zero. copyColor() is unreachable dead code, and the code comment at :190-197 asserts the opposite in writing. An API break absorbed silently at the W44 Glass-7 adoption because unknown attrs are legal Vue fallthrough and invisible to every gate.
result.negativeProof: Not applicable to the verdict (DEFECTIVE), but recorded as the audited-and-clean surface so no seat invents these: (1) NO ungated rAF — WatercolorDot is mounted without `animate` (default false) and the compiled useWatercolorBlob returns before registering its rAF (`if (l.value = …, !a) return {borderRadius,transform}` precedes `t(e=>g(e.now),…)`); even when armed the loop declares {pauseWhenHidden:true, respectReducedMotion:true}. (2) Nothing to clean up — no listeners, observers, timers, subscriptions or imperative DOM; only async is the two clipboard awaits; palette is a computed over four refs, no unbounded growth. (3) No defineModel stale-read hazard — the sole v-model is on a native <input> bound to a local ref, which is the prescribed synchronous-cache shape. (4) No ValueUnit nesting, no oklch→HSV/stableHue surface, no WebGL, no parseCssColor call — the component only emits strings the library serialized, and generatedCss checks .ok on all three of oklch/mapColorToGamut/serializeCssColor. (5) The T-17 seed-exactness law genuinely HOLDS: presetStops(c) === generatePalette(count,c,harmony,seed) and selecting c computes the identical call; mulberry32 is deterministic; the O-20 failure diff is numerically equal on all five rows (85.53637546394% ≡ 0.855364), i.e. a string-form artefact, not a lying preview. (6) The comment's "zero rest cost" half is TRUE — measured document.querySelectorAll('[data-stops]').length === 0 with both Selects closed. (7) verbatimModuleSyntax clean — all four type-only imports are `import type`. (8) No god module, no legacy shims/aliases/dual paths, no contrived shared dirs, no deleted animations. (9) Edict 5 NOT violated by `--slider-track-bg` — it is a producer-sanctioned token read with fallback in glass-ui.css (`--slider-track-bg,var(--muted-medium`), and the BJ W4 hold plans to rename that exact seam at v8. (10) Pin verified: shasum -a 256 → 4f95c57c7a6c46fa15a08b98b954a39529a12f71bda672423c7008c33ae324f6, matches CARRY-LEDGER §D exactly, no coordination-boundary drift.

defects.defect: The per-swatch copy verb is entirely dead: `tag="button"`, `:aria-label` and `@click` are all silently discarded by glass-ui 7.0.0's WatercolorDot, which renders a hardcoded aria-hidden span with pointer-events:none. The swatches are not buttons, have no accessible name, are not focusable, and cannot be clicked; copyColor() is unreachable.
defects.evidence: demo/workbenches/generate/GenerateControls.vue:199-208 (the four bindings) · node_modules/@mkbabb/glass-ui/dist/components/watercolor-dot/WatercolorDot.vue.d.ts:23-52 declares {color,variant?,animate?,cycleDuration?,range?,seed?} and no emits · `grep -o "tag" node_modules/@mkbabb/glass-ui/dist/watercolor-dot.js | wc -l` → 0 · watercolor-dot.js setup body: `inheritAttrs:!1` with `n=h(), c=i(()=>n.class), f=i(()=>n.style)` (class/style only) and root `<span aria-hidden="true" style=[attrs, {backgroundColor, borderRadius, pointerEvents:"none", …}]>` · LIVE DOM at http://localhost:9000/#/generate: {"tag":"SPAN","ariaHidden":"true","ariaLabel":null,"tabIndex":-1,"tagAttr":null,"pointerEvents":"none","cursor":"pointer","w":40,"h":40} and tabbablesInPlate = [INPUT "Palette name", BUTTON "Regenerate", BUTTON "Save palette", BUTTON "Copy all colors"] — the 5 swatches contribute 0
defects.mechanism: Producer/consumer contract break absorbed by Vue's legal-fallthrough semantics: a component with inheritAttrs:false that hand-forwards a whitelist of attrs silently swallows every unlisted attr AND every listener, and the type system treats unknown attributes on a component as valid fallthrough. The consumer's documented idiom (tag="button") was never a prop.
defects.reproduction: http://localhost:9000/#/generate → click any colour swatch inside [data-generate-plate] → nothing is copied, no focus moves, no state changes. Structurally: the DOM dump above (SPAN / aria-hidden=true / pointer-events:none / tabIndex -1 / aria-label null).
defects.proposedCure: The dot is a FACE, not a SEAT. Transpose rather than patch: a real <button> seat wraps the dot (dot stays the decorative aria-hidden child it was built to be; the button carries name, focus affordance, ≥24px target, listener). Better for a 9-consumer species: glass-ui grows the seat — a WatercolorDotButton, or an explicit as/tag + attr-forwarding contract on WatercolorDot. Relay R-1 to the glass BH inbox; the consumer half is BLOCKED-ON-GLASS-V8. Do NOT delete the three dead bindings — that retires the verb, not the defect.

defects.defect: Gate vacuity, three ways: the component's ONLY oracle (O-20) is currently RED for an unrelated serialization-form reason, CI never runs e2e at all, there are zero unit tests for the generation core, and `npm run typecheck` is green over every defect here.
defects.evidence: `npx playwright test e2e/smoke/oracles/o20-generate-plate.spec.ts --reporter=line` → "1 failed, 1 passed (39.2s)", failing at o20:105 with stamped "oklch(85.53637546394% 0.087179123785 49.783647190779deg)" vs live "oklch(0.855364 0.0871791 49.7836)" (numerically IDENTICAL — serializeCssColor vs getComputedStyle forms) · `grep -n "run:" .github/workflows/ci.yml` → npm ci / lint / vue-tsc lib / vue-tsc demo / build / npm test / verify-packed-surface / tsc / npm test — no playwright step in any of ci.yml, deploy-pages.yml, release.yml · `grep -rln "GenerateControls|useColorGeneration|generatePalette|generateSingleColor" test e2e` → only o20-generate-plate.spec.ts · `npx vue-tsc -p tsconfig.demo.json --noEmit; echo EXIT=$?` → EXIT=0 with --listFiles confirming both GenerateControls.vue and WatercolorDot.vue.d.ts in the program · o27-focus-affordance.spec.ts:33-41 pins its WCAG-2.5.8 BR-3 rule to openGradient() only
defects.mechanism: Oracles assert decorative properties (a forwarded class + computed backgroundColor) instead of the control contract (role, accessible name, operability), so they are indifferent to whether the control exists; and the one oracle that would fail is neither run by CI nor currently green.
defects.reproduction: MUTATION TEST — delete `tag="button"`, `:aria-label` and `@click` from GenerateControls.vue:199-208 and re-run O-20: the result is unchanged (test 1 still passes, test 2 still fails for its own serialization reason). o20:98-105 selects `.generate-swatch` (a class WatercolorDot DOES forward) and reads getComputedStyle(el).backgroundColor (painted by the producer regardless).
defects.proposedCure: Assert the contract, not the paint: O-20's swatch leg becomes role + accessible-name assertions; its byte-identity leg normalises both sides through one serializer. Generalise o27-focus-affordance.spec.ts from openGradient() to the route matrix so BR-3 (≥24px) and the focus-affordance rules cover every route. Put test:e2e in ci.yml or delete the suite — an unrun oracle manufactures the false confidence that let a 7.0.0 API break reach the shipped plate. All three land in e2e/ and touch no pinned consumer.

defects.defect: The plate's editable name is discarded on save — renaming the palette has no effect. GenerateControls emits `save: [colors, name]`; the only consumer declares a one-parameter handler and hardcodes the literal "Generated Palette".
defects.evidence: demo/workbenches/generate/GenerateControls.vue:48-50 (`defineEmits<{ save: [colors: string[], name: string] }>()`) and :102-104 (`emit("save", [...palette.value], paletteName.value)`) · demo/workbenches/generate/GeneratePane.vue:14 `function onSave(colors: string[])` and :19 `pm.createPalette("Generated Palette", paletteColors)` · demo/palettes/usePaletteStore.ts:66 `function createPalette(name: string, colors: PaletteColor[])` — the name parameter exists and is ignored · LIVE: {"inputValueAfter":"MY UNIQUE NAME 4711", "namesBefore":["Generated Palette","Sunset",…], "namesAfter":["Generated Palette","Generated Palette","Sunset",…]}
defects.mechanism: Positional emit payload silently dropped by handler arity — TypeScript accepts a narrower handler as assignable to a wider emit signature, so vue-tsc cannot see the drop. The same drop applies to the dock-driven save (GeneratePane.vue:22-26 re-exposes save through the same emit).
defects.reproduction: http://localhost:9000/#/generate → type any name into the plate title input → click the Save-palette button → read localStorage["color-palettes"]: the new entry is named "Generated Palette", not the typed name. Verified live with a native value setter + input event so v-model commits.
defects.proposedCure: Immediate: bind the payload — `onSave(colors: string[], name: string)` → `pm.createPalette(name, paletteColors)`. Structural cure that kills the class: emit a single object payload (`save: [{ colors, name }]`) so ignoring a field must be explicit rather than a consequence of arity. (GeneratePane.vue is not the pinned file, but no source edits land from this formation — authored as a wave item.)

defects.defect: The generated palette — the workbench's entire output — has zero accessible representation, and none of the three verbs announces anything.
defects.evidence: PaletteColorStrip.vue:2-10 aria-hidden="true" role="presentation" · the swatches are producer-hardcoded aria-hidden with the :aria-label discarded (C-1) · PreviewStrip.vue:43 aria-hidden="true" · GenerateControls.vue:293-296 the count ramp is an unlabelled decorative div · LIVE probe of every live region on the page while operating the plate: [{"role":"alert","live":null,"text":"dev misconfigured — run `npm run dev`"}] — that is the dev banner; there is no status seat
defects.mechanism: Every colour-bearing element is (correctly, individually) marked decorative, but no element ever supplies the text alternative at the level where the palette is the content — so a chain of locally-correct aria-hidden decisions sums to a workbench whose output does not exist for AT. Compounded by no aria-live for the async/replacing results.
defects.reproduction: http://localhost:9000/#/generate with VoiceOver or any AT: tab through the plate — exactly 4 stops (Palette name, Regenerate, Save palette, Copy all colors), none naming a colour; press Regenerate — the entire palette silently replaces itself with no announcement, the only changed announceable text being the seed hex. WCAG 1.1.1 and 4.1.3.
defects.proposedCure: Keep the strip and dots decorative — they are ornament. Give the PALETTE a text alternative once, at region level: the <section>'s accessible name carries count + ordered colours, or a visually-hidden <ul> of the css strings that doubles as the keyboard seat for C-1's copy verbs (one structure, both cures). Add exactly one role="status" in the plate that regenerate, save and both copies write to — which also discharges C-6 and C-12.

defects.defect: The count slider's thumb is 12.7 × 24.3 CSS px — below the WCAG 2.5.8 24×24 floor on the minor axis — and it is this component's contribution to the visual audit's small-tap-target census on all four matrices.
defects.evidence: LIVE: countSliderDescendants → {"tag":"SPAN","role":"slider","cls":"slider-thumb glass-specular-track","w":12.7,"h":24.3,"label":"Color count","ti":0} · docs/tranches/V/megatranche/audit/visual/REPORT.json /#/generate probe.a11y.smallTapTargets contains {"w":12,"h":24,"tag":"span","label":"Color count"} on safari-desktop-light/dark and safari-mobile-light/dark (4 of the 60 report-wide defects; the other 4 rows per matrix are the co-mounted Palettes pane's 160×23 input and the dock's three 22×22 slug buttons) · the same probe measured the picker's L/A/B/ALPHA channel thumbs at 12×24 each · e2e/smoke/oracles/o27-focus-affordance.spec.ts BR-3 encodes the ≥24px-fine / ≥44px-coarse rule but o27:33-41 pins the spec to openGradient()
defects.mechanism: Producer-owned .slider-thumb geometry (glass-ui) with no hit-inflation, combined with a target-size oracle whose scope is a single route — so a species-wide producer defect is invisible to the gate that was written to catch exactly it.
defects.reproduction: http://localhost:9000/#/generate → measure [role="slider"][aria-label="Color count"] → 12.7 × 24.3 CSS px. Already captured independently by the audit's own Safari matrix on all four cells.
defects.proposedCure: Producer-side always-on hit-inflation on .slider-thumb (the visual dot HELD, the effective target inflated) — relay R-2 to the glass BH inbox, since the BJ W4 hold forbids the consumer touching it. Demo-side and unblocked: generalise o27's BR-3 from openGradient() to the route matrix so this is born-RED rather than silent.

defects.defect: Both clipboard call sites await `writeClipboard` and discard the discriminated result the producer designed to be read, so a denied or hung copy is indistinguishable from a successful one.
defects.evidence: demo/workbenches/generate/GenerateControls.vue:106-113 — `await writeClipboard(palette.value.join(", "))` and `await writeClipboard(css)`, both results dropped · node_modules/@mkbabb/glass-ui/dist/composables/dom/useClipboard.d.ts:16-37 — `export type CopyResult = { ok: true } | { ok: false; reason: CopyFailureReason }` with the doc comment "Returns the discriminated result … rather than a lossy boolean, for identical call ergonomics: `const { ok } = await writeClipboard(text)`" · the producer also ships useClipboard({status, copy}) with scope-owned confirmation state
defects.mechanism: A result-typed API consumed as if it were void: the failure channel exists, is documented, and is thrown away — so the platform's known failure modes (Safari permission denial, insecure context, the producer-documented 'writeText pending forever') surface as silence.
defects.reproduction: NONE from the shipped happy path — the drop is source-dispositive (GenerateControls.vue:107 and :112 discard the return). Combined with C-3 (no live region) neither success nor failure produces any user-perceivable signal, so 'Copy all colors' is already indistinguishable from a no-op today.
defects.proposedCure: `const { ok } = await writeClipboard(…)` feeding the single role="status" seat the C-3 cure introduces — one status element serving regenerate, save and both copies, rather than per-call-site feedback.

defects.defect: The code comment's own performance claim is false by measurement: the preset dropdown's seed-exact previews cost 1.3 ms at count 5 and 3.6 ms at count 12, not 'sub-millisecond'.
defects.evidence: GenerateControls.vue:86-96 claims "…so zero rest cost; 10 rows × 5-12 library generations is sub-millisecond" · measured in-page against the live dev server (module imported off Vite at /@fs/…/demo/color-session/generate-color.ts, 20 warm-up iterations, performance.now()): {"onePalette5_ms":0.1,"presetDropdownOpen_count5_ms":1.3,"presetDropdownOpen_count12_ms":3.6}
defects.mechanism: An unverified performance assertion used as the justification for calling a generator from the template. The 'zero rest cost' half of the same comment is TRUE (verified: [data-stops].length === 0 with the menus closed — reka's SelectContent genuinely unmounts), so only the cost figure is wrong.
defects.reproduction: In-page: `const m = await import('/@fs/…/demo/color-session/generate-color.ts'); const t=performance.now(); for (let i=0;i<10;i++) m.generatePalette(12, m.PRESET_NAMES[i], 'golden', 12345); performance.now()-t` → 3.6 ms, landing synchronously in the frame that opens the preset menu, before the harmony menu's own 6 rows.
defects.proposedCure: Either correct the comment to the measured figure, or make the claim true by memoising per (count, harmony, seed) across the 10 preset rows — they share three of four arguments. Do not delete the previews: they are the T-17 truth law and it genuinely holds (§6).

defects.defect: The plate-chrome row wraps at the DEFAULT desktop pane width, not at 390 as the source comment documents — so the intended one-line composition (name — count — regenerate — actions) never renders at any viewport.
defects.evidence: GenerateControls.vue:138-142 claims "at 390 the verbs settle onto their own right-aligned line" · docs/tranches/V/megatranche/audit/visual/shots/safari-desktop-light/generate.png shows the verb cluster already on its own second line at desktop with a wide dead gap beside the title · flex base sizes at the measured pane (content ≈ 437 CSS px): input basis-[10rem]=160 + badge ≈34 + cluster (Regenerate 145 + Save 36 + Copy 36 + 2 inner gaps) = 233 + 2 row gaps = 443 > 437
defects.mechanism: Flex line-breaking uses base sizes, and the sum overshoots the primary desktop pane by roughly six pixels — so the wrap the comment reserves for 390px fires ~250px earlier, at the layout the composition was designed for.
defects.reproduction: Read shots/safari-desktop-light/generate.png (safari-desktop-light matrix, 1440-wide viewport) — the Regenerate/Save/Copy cluster is on line 2 with 'Generated Palette … 5' alone on line 1.
defects.proposedCure: Either shrink the cluster's base (icon-only Regenerate below a threshold, or drop the input's basis-[10rem] to basis-0 so it does not claim 160px of the line budget), or accept the two-line form and delete the false breakpoint claim from the comment. Nothing overflows (REPORT.json overflowX: 0 on all four matrices), so this is composition truth, not breakage.

defects.defect: The editable palette name's only affordance is `hover:underline`, which does not exist on touch — on mobile the field is visually indistinguishable from a heading, and there is no placeholder for the emptied state.
defects.evidence: GenerateControls.vue:144-149 — bg-transparent, borderless, `hover:underline decoration-dashed underline-offset-4` is the sole rest affordance; no placeholder attribute · docs/tranches/V/megatranche/audit/visual/shots/safari-mobile-dark/generate.png shows 'Generated Palette' rendering as plate title with zero field affordance · live: the input carries aria-label="Palette name" (so AT is fine) and measures 398 × 30.5
defects.mechanism: Discoverability gated behind a pointer capability the device does not have. Coarse pointers never enter :hover, so the only signal that the title is editable never fires.
defects.reproduction: Open http://localhost:9000/#/generate on a touch device or in Safari mobile emulation — the plate title shows no border, no underline, no field chrome at rest. Confirmed in the audit's own safari-mobile-dark capture.
defects.proposedCure: A rest-state affordance that is not hover-gated (show the card family's dashed underline at rest, or restore it under @media (hover: none)), plus a placeholder so an emptied name is not an invisible unlabelled control. Pairs with C-2 — an affordance for a field whose value is discarded is worse than no field.

defects.defect: `value as PresetName` / `as HarmonyName` launder reka-ui's nullable AcceptableValue; a null would make GENERATION_PRESETS[preset] undefined and throw a TypeError from inside the palette computed during render.
defects.evidence: GenerateControls.vue:75-81 — `preset.value = value as PresetName;` / `harmony.value = value as HarmonyName;` · node_modules/reka-ui/dist/index3.d.cts:231 — `type AcceptableValue = string | number | bigint | Record<string, any> | null` · demo/color-session/generate-color.ts:220 `const p = GENERATION_PRESETS[preset];` then :227 `p.l[0] + rng() * (p.l[1] - p.l[0])`
defects.mechanism: An unguarded narrowing cast on an untrusted boundary — the 'masking cast' idiom the owner edicts forbid. A throw inside a computed evaluated during render blanks the pane (the repo's known render-crash shape).
defects.reproduction: NONE — this is a HYPOTHESIS. I found no path in the shipped UI that makes reka emit null here (no clear affordance is wired to either Select). The mechanism is certain; the trigger is unreached.
defects.proposedCure: Replace the cast with a membership check against the arrays that already exist — `if (!PRESET_NAMES.includes(value as PresetName)) return;` — so the boundary validates rather than asserts.

defects.defect: generatePalette's count domain is undefended in the shared colour layer: 0/-1/NaN silently return [], Infinity throws RangeError, and 2.5 returns 3 colours; clampHueToRanges also carries a dead wrapping-range branch whose span arithmetic would go negative.
defects.evidence: Measured on the live module: {"zero":{"len":0},"one":{"len":1},"neg":{"len":0},"nan":{"len":0},"inf":{"threw":"RangeError: Invalid array length"},"frac":{"len":3}} · demo/color-session/generate-color.ts:156-184 clampHueToRanges — the lo>hi branch at :165-167 pairs with `ranges.reduce((sum,[lo,hi]) => sum + (hi - lo), 0)` at :171, which is negative for a wrapping range · no shipped preset wraps (warm is [[0,80],[330,360]], two ascending segments)
defects.mechanism: A pure primitive exported from the shared colour layer with no input contract and no unit test; today its only caller clamps the domain, so the gaps are latent rather than live.
defects.reproduction: NONE from the UI — the slider is :min="1" :max="12" :step="1" (GenerateControls.vue:301-303) and count is not on defineExpose. Reproduced only by calling the module directly (evidence above). Recorded because generatePalette/generateSingleColor are consumed elsewhere (demo/color-session/useColorParsing.ts).
defects.proposedCure: Give the pure core an explicit contract at its own boundary (clamp/validate count to a documented 1..50 as its JSDoc already claims) and unit-test it — there is currently ZERO unit coverage of generatePalette, generateHues or clampHueToRanges, so the dead wrapping branch's wrong arithmetic has never been exercised.

defects.defect: Repeated save silently mints duplicate palettes with no confirmation, no duplicate check and no undo.
defects.evidence: From the C-2 live reproduction: namesAfter = ["Generated Palette","Generated Palette","Sunset",…] — two identical rows after a single click · the only live region on the page is the dev-misconfig role="alert" (C-3), so nothing confirms the save landed
defects.mechanism: Silent write + absent feedback: because the user cannot tell whether the first click registered (C-3), the interface invites the second click that creates the duplicate.
defects.reproduction: http://localhost:9000/#/generate → click Save palette twice → localStorage["color-palettes"] gains two identically-named entries, with no visible change in the plate either time.
defects.proposedCure: The dedupe policy belongs to the store, but the missing feedback is this component's: route the save through the same role="status" seat the C-3 cure introduces, so one click is visibly acknowledged.

result.axis: CHALLENGE-L — library structure (module boundaries, ownership, dependency direction, public surface) under demo/workbenches/generate/GenerateControls.vue
result.modelObserved: Opus 5 (1M context) — exact model id `claude-opus-5[1m]`. Declared for this seat, not inherited.
result.strongestDefect: L2-1 — the five per-swatch copy verbs on the Generate plate DO NOT EXIST in the product. GenerateControls.vue:199-208 passes `tag="button"`, `:aria-label` and `@click` to `<WatercolorDot>`, but glass-ui 7.0.0's WatercolorDot declares only `color|variant|animate|cycleDuration|range|seed`, ships `inheritAttrs:false`, and hardcodes `aria-hidden="true"`. Measured live: the rendered element is a SPAN with no tag/aria-label/role/tabindex; `.focus()` leaves `document.activeElement===swatch` false; `.click()` produces ZERO clipboard writes while the positive control ("Copy all colors") produces one. Three gates are green over it — `vue-tsc -p tsconfig.demo.json` EXIT=0, the O-20 oracle asserts only `backgroundColor`, and the visual audit's interactive-element probe cannot see an aria-hidden span. This is the third member of the same producer-surface disease pass 1 found on `<Button variant>` (§L-0), and the first with a FUNCTIONAL rather than cosmetic consequence — which is why the Glass 8 gate G-3 must widen from Button-only to any-unknown-attr-on-any-glass-ui-root.

defects.defect: The per-swatch copy verb is dead: the component drives a WatercolorDot API glass-ui 7.0.0 does not declare (`tag="button"`), so five interactive swatches render as inert aria-hidden spans — not focusable, not clickable, invisible to AT. Copying a single generated colour is not a feature of the shipped product.
defects.evidence: CONSUMER: demo/workbenches/generate/GenerateControls.vue:199-208 (`tag="button"`, `:aria-label="`Copy ${css}`"`, `@click="copyColor(css)"`). PRODUCER: node_modules/@mkbabb/glass-ui/dist/components/watercolor-dot/WatercolorDot.vue.d.ts — props = {color, variant, animate, cycleDuration, range, seed}; no `tag`, no emits. `grep -o inheritAttrs .../dist/watercolor-dot.js` → present; `grep -o 'aria-hidden[^,]{0,20}'` → `aria-hidden": "true"` ×3. MEASURED DOM: {"tag":"SPAN","attrs":["data-v-292b9032=","aria-hidden=true","class=generate-swatch w-9 h-9 sm:w-10 sm:h-10 ","data-testid=watercolor-swatch","data-variant=solid","style=background-color: oklch(…"]}. MEASURED FOCUS: {"matchesFV":false,"isActiveEl":false}. MEASURED CLICK: {"afterSwatchClick":[],"afterCopyAllClick":["oklch(76.364581747912% …"]}. Plate focusable census: ["INPUT:Palette name","BUTTON:Regenerate","BUTTON:Save palette","BUTTON:Copy all colors"] — zero swatches. GATES: `time npx vue-tsc -p tsconfig.demo.json --noEmit` → EXIT=0 in 9.2s; e2e/smoke/oracles/o20-generate-plate.spec.ts:97-105 asserts only getComputedStyle().backgroundColor; docs/tranches/V/megatranche/audit/visual/capture.mjs:88-98 selects only a,button,input,…,[tabindex] so an aria-hidden span is unobservable (REPORT.json generate rows: namelessButtons 0).
defects.mechanism: Producer/consumer prop contract enforced by neither the type system (Vue fallthrough attrs always type-check) nor the runtime (inheritAttrs:false silently eats them). Identical mechanism to pass-1 §L-0 (`<Button variant>`, 51 sites) — but a structural prop rather than a style prop, so the element is the wrong element and the behaviour never attaches.
defects.reproduction: Playwright/WebKit against http://localhost:9000/#/generate (self-healing hash idiom, §8.6 of the report): (1) `swatch.focus()` → document.activeElement !== swatch; (2) patch navigator.clipboard.writeText to record calls, `document.querySelector('.generate-swatch').click()` → [] writes; (3) control: `button[aria-label="Copy all colors"].click()` → 1 write.
defects.proposedCure: The dot is decorative by the producer's own design (aria-hidden hardcoded) and should stay so. Consumer owns the verb seat: `<button aria-label="Copy …" @click><WatercolorDot :color :seed/></button>` — which also honours T-28's outline law honestly (the button carries the ring at the silhouette; the dot never does). BLOCKED-ON-GLASS-V8: new gate G-4 requires glass-ui to DECIDE (a) decorative-only + documented, or (b) typed polymorphic root + declared click emit, before any consumer edit. Widen gate G-3 from 'Button variant fails' to 'any attribute reaching any glass-ui component root outside its declared prop surface fails at typecheck or first render, reproducibly in CI'. Add O-20 behavioural assertion: swatch click → clipboard receives that swatch's CSS string.

defects.defect: The ramp-track slider is implemented twice, and the two copies diverged exactly at the WCAG 1.4.11 contrast cure: the extract twin carries an inset contrast ring and an O-18 census hook, the generate twin carries neither.
defects.evidence: Copy A: demo/workbenches/extract/composables/useExtractSession.ts:101-112 (kSliderGradient) + ExtractControls.vue:20-33 with `boxShadow: inset 0 0 0 1.5px ${trackInk}` (:22) and data-o18="extract-k-rail". Copy B: GenerateControls.vue:65-73 (countSliderGradient) + :292-307, no ring, no hook. Same algorithm line for line (`pct = n===1?50:(i/(n-1))*100`, `.toFixed(0)`, `"var(--muted)"` fallback); GenerateControls.vue:284-285 says so — 'the extract k-slider pattern verbatim'. MEASURED live rail: {"railBoxShadow":"none","railRect":{"w":434,"h":24},"railInlineBg":"background: linear-gradient(to right, oklch(0.63947 0.110159 190.777) 0%, …)"}. ORACLE ASYMMETRY: e2e/smoke/oracles/o18-contrast-census.spec.ts:1106,1126,1133 census extract-kc and extract-k-rail only; the generate rail appears in no census row. The cure's own provenance: ExtractControls.vue:59-64 ('the track re-inks with the CONTRACT … at the WCAG 1.4.11 graphics floor').
defects.mechanism: A design-system capability ('a Slider whose track paints a supplied ramp') implemented as a per-pane absolutely-positioned div sandwich plus `--slider-track-bg: transparent`. Copied code does not diverge at random — it diverges wherever only one copy received the fix. Upgrades pass-1 §L-10 from INFO to MAJOR.
defects.reproduction: Playwright at /#/generate: read the rail div's computed boxShadow → "none"; compare ExtractControls.vue:22 which sets an inset 1.5px trackInk ring. `grep -rn 'data-o18' e2e/smoke/oracles/o18-contrast-census.spec.ts` → extract hooks only.
defects.proposedCure: Glass 8 gate G-2 (already filed) gains G-2′: the producer's ramp-track affordance MUST carry the WCAG 1.4.11 contrast ring, so a consumer cannot obtain the ramp without the ring. Both underlay divs, both `--slider-track-bg: transparent` overrides and both gradient builders then delete together. Independently of G-2′, add data-o18="generate-count-rail" plus its census row — that is the only mechanism that would have caught the divergence.

defects.defect: Two colour-harmony vocabularies live in one application: glass-ui 7 owns `ColorHarmony` (consumed by the Atmosphere pane) while the demo mints a rival `HARMONY_NAMES` with its own generator. The same concept ships under two spellings — 'Triadic' in Generate, 'triad' in Atmosphere.
defects.evidence: PRODUCER: node_modules/@mkbabb/glass-ui/dist/composables/color/index.d.ts:81 `export type ColorHarmony = "analogous"|"complementary"|"split-complementary"|"triad"|"tetradic"|"monochrome"`, :87 `deriveHue(anchorHue, harmony, hueSpread, t)`; documented at dist/components/aurora/composables/color.d.ts:29-34 as 'the PUBLIC alias of the shared ColorHarmony vocabulary … The blob and aurora derive from this ONE union.' DEMO RIVAL: demo/color-session/generate-color.ts:68-85 `HARMONY_NAMES = ["golden","analogous","complementary","triadic","split-complementary","random"]` with its own generateHues at :93-149. CONSUMERS: GenerateControls.vue:264-278 (+capitalize at :83-85) renders 'Triadic'; demo/scenes/atmosphere/AuroraPane.vue:121-127, typed AuroraHarmony=ColorHarmony via @mkbabb/glass-ui/aurora, renders the glass-ui union with 'triad'.
defects.mechanism: Unique semantic ownership violated twice: the concept is absent from @mkbabb/value.js (the constellation's colour library), present in @mkbabb/glass-ui (a UI library — itself an inversion of dependency direction), and privately re-implemented a third time in demo/.
defects.reproduction: NONE — static, but exhaustively enumerated: the two unions, their two generators, and their two rendered menus are all cited at file:line above. The user-visible 'Triadic' vs 'triad' divergence is derivable from the two type declarations plus the two capitalisation paths.
defects.proposedCure: One vocabulary, one home, and the home is the colour library, not the component library. Fold ColorHarmony into pass-1's proposed `@mkbabb/value.js/palette` subpath and have glass-ui CONSUME it (colour vocabulary flowing library → design system, not the reverse); retire the demo's rival. RF-17 library-evolution wave — 4.0.0 is immutable, so this is a next-cut row, not a megatranche edit.

defects.defect: The design system's `Select` publishes no typed model-value, so four demo files reach past glass-ui into its own transitive dependency (reka-ui) and launder the enum boundary through nine unchecked `as` casts.
defects.evidence: GenerateControls.vue:33 `import type { AcceptableValue } from "reka-ui"`; :75-81 `preset.value = value as PresetName` / `harmony.value = value as HarmonyName`. `grep -c AcceptableValue node_modules/@mkbabb/glass-ui/dist/index.d.ts` → 0 (glass-ui does not re-export it). Census: GenerateControls.vue:33 (casts :76,:80); MixConfigBar.vue:15 (casts :99,:122,:146); GradientVisualizer.vue:28 (casts :164,:181,:198); AuroraPane.vue:25 (casts :79,:81,:85,:92) = 4 files / 9 casts.
defects.mechanism: Wrong direction of dependency. The demo depends on the design system's PRIVATE choice of headless substrate; swap reka-ui in Glass 8 and four demo files break for a reason unrelated to their own concern. Pass 1 correctly noted reka-ui is a declared devDependency — declaredness is not the defect, direction is.
defects.reproduction: NONE — static; the grep census above is exhaustive over demo/.
defects.proposedCure: Producer ask alongside G-1/G-2/G-3: `Select<T extends string>` with `@update:model-value: (v: T) => void` (or a re-export of the value type from the glass-ui root). Nine casts and four reka-ui imports die and the preset/harmony boundary becomes type-checked instead of asserted. Same lesson as G-3 from the other side: a design-system prop OR event whose type the consumer must guess is not a contract.

defects.defect: The palette name the user types is silently discarded on save: the child emits `save: [colors, name]` but the pane's handler declares arity 1 and passes the literal "Generated Palette" to the persistence port. Data loss on user input.
defects.evidence: GenerateControls.vue:48-50 `defineEmits<{ save: [colors: string[], name: string] }>()`, :52 `paletteName = ref("Generated Palette")`, :102-104 `emit("save", [...palette.value], paletteName.value)`. GeneratePane.vue:14 `function onSave(colors: string[])` — name parameter never bound — and :19 `pm.createPalette("Generated Palette", paletteColors)`. LIVE REPRODUCTION (pass 2, which pass 1 had to abandon under shared-browser contention): {"url":"http://localhost:9000/#/generate","inputAfterSet":"ZZ-PROBE-NAME","nameMatches":[["color-palettes",["Generated Palette","Sunset","Empty Plate","Overflowing"]]]} — the v-model round-trip is verified and the persisted store contains zero occurrences of ZZ-PROBE-NAME. Comment at :44-47 asserts 'this emit is already truthful' — it is not.
defects.mechanism: Ownership split with an untyped joint: the NAME is owned by the leaf component, the PERSISTENCE PORT (LIBRARY_PORT_KEY) is injected by the parent, and the two are joined by a Vue emit. TypeScript cannot catch it — a handler is always assignable to an emit with more parameters. Second symptom of the same split: `string[] → PaletteColor[]` is synthesised twice (GenerateControls.vue:55-57 and GeneratePane.vue:15-18) because neither file owns 'the generated palette as a domain object'.
defects.reproduction: Playwright at /#/generate with the self-healing hash idiom: set input[aria-label="Palette name"] to ZZ-PROBE-NAME via the native value setter + input event (verified round-trip), click button[aria-label="Save palette"], read localStorage['color-palettes'] → names are ["Generated Palette","Sunset","Empty Plate","Overflowing"].
defects.proposedCure: ESCALATION RECOMMENDED — this is the highest-value action available before Glass 8. GeneratePane.vue is NOT in the hold's pinned receiver set (the four pinned files are ComponentSliders.vue, ConfigSliderPane.vue, ExtractControls.vue, GenerateControls.vue), so binding the second emit argument at GeneratePane.vue:14-19 cures the data loss WITHOUT touching any pinned file. The full cure is the session hoist: `useGenerateSession()` owning preset/harmony/count/seed/name/palette/regenerate/save, provided at the pane under a typed InjectionKey — one writer, one adapter, and the name-drop becomes unrepresentable.

defects.defect: Cross-feature edge: workbenches/generate imports PaletteColorStrip from the palettes feature's card cluster, dragging the palettes DOMAIN type into a feature that has no palette.
defects.evidence: GenerateControls.vue:16 `import { PaletteColorStrip } from "../../palettes/browser/card"`. CENSUS — 4 consumers, 3 of 4 outside palettes/: MixSourceSelector.vue:8,203; GenerateControls.vue:16,135; ExtractWorkbench.vue:200; only PaletteCard.vue:33,175 is in-feature. LAW: docs/tranches/V/audit/REFORMATION-2026-07-16.md:73 (RF-15) enumerates the surviving true-shared buckets and names this species as work owed ('Cross-feature violation to fix: ConsoleRail → palette api barrel'). TAX: `grep -rn 'css, i) => ({' demo` → 4 synthesis sites (GenerateControls.vue:56, GeneratePane.vue:15, CurrentPaletteEditor.vue:244, useGradientModel.ts:144) fabricating `{css, position}` to satisfy props typed on PaletteColor (PaletteColorStrip.vue:29,35-45, reading c.weight; demo/palettes/types.ts:1-11 shows the faked name?/weight? fields).
defects.mechanism: A presentational primitive filed inside a feature it does not belong to. 75% of its consumers are outside its home, so 3 features must cross a boundary and adapt to a domain type none of them own. Meanwhile the CORRECT shared home already exists and this same file already imports from it (demo/color-session/color-chips/index.ts:1-27 declares itself 'ONE focused common module for the multi-feature chip grammar, never a per-pane copy').
defects.reproduction: NONE — static; the consumer census above is exhaustive (`grep -rn 'PaletteColorStrip' demo`).
defects.proposedCure: Move the strip into the existing shared chip module as `demo/color-session/color-chips/ColorStrip.vue`, retyped domain-free: props { stops: readonly string[]; weights?: readonly number[]; orientation? }. PaletteCard maps PaletteColor[] → (stops, weights) at its own boundary, where the domain type belongs. Result: 3 cross-feature edges die, 2 synthesis adapters die, the domain type stops leaking, and all three strip forms sit under one declared grammar. No new directory minted (edict 3) — color-chips already exists and already claims this concept.

defects.defect: `demo/ui/` is a 19-directory alias-shim layer over the design system, and this single 312-line file consumes glass-ui through three different idioms at once.
defects.evidence: Measured: 19 demo/ui/*/index.ts barrels; 18 are one-line pure re-exports of @mkbabb/glass-ui (e.g. `demo/ui/button/index.ts` = `export { Button } from "@mkbabb/glass-ui";`), and the nineteenth (alert/) is also a pure re-export carrying only a comment. GenerateControls.vue:3-12 uses the shim (../../ui/select|slider|button|badge), :14 uses the root barrel (writeClipboard), :15 uses a subpath (@mkbabb/glass-ui/watercolor-dot). glass-ui 7.0.0 publishes ./badge ./button ./select ./slider among 74 exports and declares sideEffects: ["*.css"], so the root barrel tree-shakes as well as a subpath — the shim buys nothing, not even bundle size.
defects.mechanism: Survival of the pre-glass-ui shadcn era: an alias layer preserving old import paths. Edict 2 (no aliases / migration shims / dual paths) and edict 3 (no wrapper indirection).
defects.reproduction: NONE — static; `for d in demo/ui/*/; do …` shim census run in the report's command log.
defects.proposedCure: Delete demo/ui/ entirely; every call site imports the glass-ui subpath directly — the idiom this very file already uses for WatercolorDot. A clean measured down-metric for the RF-21 structure-settlement wave (19 directories, 19 files). Sequence after the Glass 8 unblock, since it touches the pinned file's import block.

defects.defect: The generation core is stranded in the demo while its sibling workbench's core is a published library subpath — the same tree, the same shape of pure colour math, opposite sides of the src/↔demo/ line.
defects.evidence: EXTRACT'S MATH IS THE LIBRARY: src/subpaths/quantize.ts exports dominantColor/quantizePixels, consumed at demo/workbenches/extract/quantize-worker.ts:6-7, useExtractSession.ts:14, useImageQuantize.ts:9 via `@mkbabb/value.js/quantize`. GENERATE'S IS NOT: demo/color-session/generate-color.ts (243 lines, pure, seeded, zero Vue) + demo/color-session/prng.ts (mulberry32), touching the library only for primitives at :33 (oklch, mapColorToGamut from /color) and :34 (serializeCssColor from /css).
defects.mechanism: Arbitrary placement of a library-shaped capability. `generatePalette(count, preset, harmony, seed) → string[]` is pure, deterministic, gamut-mapped and DOM-free — exactly the shape of a public subpath export. An external consumer of @mkbabb/value.js gets quantizePixels but must re-implement harmony generation from scratch; the demo cannot dogfood the public surface for its own headline feature.
defects.reproduction: NONE — static; the subpath census (`grep -rhno '@mkbabb/value\.js[a-z/.]*' demo` → 25 /color, 10 /css, 6 /math, 5 /easing, 4 /quantize, 0 bare) and the two file trees are cited above.
defects.proposedCure: Relocate generatePalette/generateSingleColor/GENERATION_PRESETS/the harmony union into a new `@mkbabb/value.js/palette` subpath (with mulberry32 to src/math/prng.ts), and have glass-ui's ColorHarmony re-point at it (see L2-3). RF-17 library-evolution wave — 4.0.0 is immutable.

defects.defect: Three-level ref forwarding with masking optional-calls on the METHOD, so a renamed verb silently no-ops the dock button with no type error, no runtime error and no warning.
defects.evidence: demo/shell/usePaneRouter.ts:196 `handler: () => paneRefs.generate.value?.regenerate?.()`, :198 `…?.copyColors?.()` → demo/workbenches/generate/GeneratePane.vue:22-26 `regenerate: () => controlsRef.value?.regenerate?.()` → GenerateControls.vue:115 `defineExpose({ regenerate, save, copyColors })`. Two expose layers and four `?.` method masks relay three verbs.
defects.mechanism: The `?.` on the method (as distinct from the instance) exists only to swallow a contract mismatch — a masking fallback in the sense edict 2 forbids. The pane's defineExpose is hand-written and untyped against the child's.
defects.reproduction: NONE — static.
defects.proposedCure: Folds into the L-1 session hoist: `useGenerateSession()` provided at GeneratePane under a typed InjectionKey; the dock injects it and calls the verbs directly. Both expose layers, the controlsRef and all four masks delete.

defects.reproduction: NONE — static.

result.negativeProof: Verdict is DEFECTIVE, but these were tested and found SOUND — recorded so no seat re-runs them. (1) LIBRARY-SPECIFIER DISCIPLINE IS CLEAN AT THE CALL SITES: `grep -rhno '@mkbabb/value\.js[a-z/.]*' demo` → 25 /color, 10 /css, 6 /math, 5 /easing, 4 /quantize, and ZERO bare-specifier or deep-path imports (the one bare match is prose at demo/shared/utils.ts:12). package.json#exports is a closed 7-key set with no "." root; this component's transitive library use (generate-color.ts:33-34) goes through /color and /css, both real exports keys a real consumer could write. result.axis: CHALLENGE-C — implementation defect hunt on demo/workbenches/gradient/GradientVisualizer/GradientStopEditor.vue (+ its composables, styles, and tests)
result.modelObserved: Opus 5 — exact model id `claude-opus-5[1m]` (1M context). Explicitly declared at spawn, not inherited.
result.strongestDefect: C1 — a drag inverts stop order (no ordering invariant anywhere on the update path), which makes the rail paint a clamped flat band, re-pairs the easing intervals across inverted stops, and emits CSS that the app's OWN parser rejects: live drag produced `linear-gradient(90deg, oklch(0.75 0.15 145) 74.9%, oklch(70% 0.165 205deg) 50%, oklch(0.65 0.18 265) 100%)`, and parseGradientCSS on that exact string returns `reject: stop positions must be non-decreasing`.

defects.defect: Dragging (or shift+arrow nudging) a handle past a neighbour leaves `stops` non-monotonic: the rail's ramp positions descend so CSS clamps them into a flat band, the easing intervals now straddle inverted pairs, and the serialized CSS is refused by the app's own parser — the atomic round-trip contract is one-way only.
defects.evidence: Live: after adding a stop at 50% and dragging the 0% handle right, DOM/model order = ["Gradient stop at 75%","Gradient stop at 50%","Gradient stop at 100%"]; editor text = `linear-gradient(90deg, oklch(0.75 0.15 145) 74.9%, oklch(70% 0.165 205deg) 50%, oklch(0.65 0.18 265) 100%)`; rail background-image head = `linear-gradient(90deg, oklch(0.75 0.15 145) 74.9%, oklch(0.746875 0.150937 148.75) 73.34%, oklch(0.74375 0.151875 152.5) 71.79%, …)` (descending). `npx vite-node docs/tranches/V/megatranche/audit/components/wb-gradient-stopeditor/evidence/parse-probe.ts` → `parseGradientCSS -> reject: stop positions must be non-decreasing (hard-stop reordering isn't modeled)` on that exact string. Code: demo/workbenches/gradient/composables/useGradientModel.ts:127-131 (updateStop never sorts) vs :118 (addStop does); emit sites GradientStopEditor.vue:145 and :179; guard-on-input at demo/workbenches/gradient/composables/gradientParse.ts:284-290.
defects.mechanism: Sortedness is enforced on insert and merely coincidental on update — the position write is a raw array map, so an invariant the rest of the system depends on has no owner.
defects.reproduction: http://localhost:9000 → dock → Gradient → click the rail at 50% → drag the 0% handle to ~75% → read the CSS box and the rail's computed background-image; paste that CSS back into the editor and the app rejects it.
defects.proposedCure: Make ordering a property of the operation, not of the array: one model action `setStopPosition(id, pos)` that maps then sorts, so sortedness is total by construction, paired with C2's identity-keyed intervals so the re-sort cannot scramble easing. Clamping the drag to (prev, next) is cheaper and strictly worse — it makes stops un-reorderable.

defects.defect: Easing intervals are keyed by array INDEX and synced by a length watcher that appends/truncates at the TAIL, while addStop inserts in sorted position — so inserting a stop silently moves the user's authored curve onto a different pair of stops and reverts the authored segment to linear.
defects.evidence: Live: stops [0,50,100] with `steps(4, jump-end)` authored on segment 50→100 → readouts ["cubic-bezier(0, 0, 1, 1)","steps(4, jump-end)"], heads ["1 → 2linear","2 → 3steps"]. After clicking the rail at 25%: labels [0%,25%,50%,100%], readouts ["cubic-bezier(0, 0, 1, 1)","steps(4, jump-end)","cubic-bezier(0, 0, 1, 1)"], heads ["1 → 2linear","2 → 3steps","3 → 4linear"] — steps now governs 25→50; the authored 50→100 curve is gone. Code: demo/workbenches/gradient/composables/useGradientModel.ts:89-100.
defects.mechanism: An adjacency relation (which pair of stops a curve belongs to) is modelled as a positional array, and the sync watcher observes only `stops.length`, so it cannot know where the stop landed and always guesses 'at the end'.
defects.reproduction: http://localhost:9000 → Gradient → click the rail at 50% → open interval row 2 → click the `steps` specimen → click the rail at 25% → read `.readout-rail code` and `.interval-head` text.
defects.proposedCure: Hang the interval on the stop that OPENS it — `GradientStop { id, cssColor, position, easing }` (last stop's easing ignored) — so the curve travels with its own stop through any insert/remove/sort. That deletes the parallel array, the sync watcher, and all three `Gradient interval N is missing` throws (useGradientCSS.ts:189/240, GradientVisualizer.vue:77). Alternative: a Map keyed by the ordered stop-id pair.

defects.defect: Every pointermove during a handle drag emits `update:position` TWICE — the bar's handler documents itself as a 'fallback path while a handle drag is live (capture sits on the handle)', but captured events still bubble to the bar, so both handlers always run.
defects.evidence: Live counters on a 20-step drag: {"barMovesOnHandle":21,"barMovesTotal":22} — the bar's draggingId branch fired on every move of the drag. Code: GradientStopEditor.vue:91-99 (bar) and :136-146 (handle); each calls getPosition → getBoundingClientRect (line 77), a forced layout. Downstream cost measured via evidence/serialize-cost.ts: `per invalidation (all three computeds): 0.223 ms` at 3 stops (coalesced 0.110 / rail 0.111 / simple 0.001 ms).
defects.mechanism: A false premise about pointer capture (it retargets, it does not stop propagation) left a live duplicate code path that the comment records as fact.
defects.reproduction: Attach a bubble-phase pointermove listener to [data-testid=gradient-stop-bar], drag a handle 20 steps, count events whose target matches [data-stop-id].
defects.proposedCure: Delete the branch: `if (draggingId.value) return;` at the top of onBarPointerMove — with capture on the handle the bar has no job during a drag — and cache the rail rect at pointerdown instead of measuring twice per move (the rail cannot resize mid-drag; touch-action:none is already set).

defects.defect: The gradient route's parse path THROWS instead of rejecting on the 8 empty-argument colour functions (MT-F001): the throw escapes parseGradientCSS → applyCSS → onParseCSS into a debounce timer, so the 'model-or-reject, fail LOUD' contract inverts into an uncaught TypeError with no verdict rendered.
defects.evidence: `npx vite-node .../evidence/parse-probe.ts` → `parseCssColor("oklch()") -> THROW TypeError: Cannot read properties of undefined (reading 'replace')` and identically for rgb()/hsl()/lab()/lch()/oklab()/hwb()/color(); `parseGradientCSS -> THROW TypeError … << linear-gradient(90deg, oklch(), blue)`. Root: src/css/grammar.ts:181 `splitTopLevel(slash[0]!.replace(/,/g, " "), "space")` where splitTopLevel (grammar.ts:63-87) returns [] for an empty body, so the non-null assertion is false. defects.proposedCure: Fix it in grammar.ts, not the pane: `const head = slash[0]; if (head === undefined) return failure(source, "css_syntax", ["CSS color"]);`. A try/catch in onParseCSS would be a masking fallback (edict 2) and would leave every other parseCssColor caller exposed.

defects.evidence: Live focusable census inside main on /#/gradient: ["Gradient stop at 0%","Gradient stop at 100%","Gradient type","Interpolation space","Hue interpolation","Gradient direction", …] — the rail div measures role:null, tabindex:null, so click-to-add is pointer-exclusive (WCAG 2.1.1). Raise the visible dot to 24px so the hit region and the target agree.

defects.defect: The handle track (inset 11px at each end) and the ramp paint (full border-box) do not share an axis — falsifying the file's own headline invariant that 'handles, add-ghost and ramp share one axis by construction'.
defects.evidence: Measured live: barRect {x:224,w:462}, border 1px, bgSize "100% 100%", bgOrigin "border-box" → ramp 0% at x=224, 100% at x=686; handle centres measured 235 and 675 (left: `calc(0% + 10px)` / `calc(100% - 10px)` resolved against the padding box). The ramp's own sample step is 3.13% (`oklch(0.75 0.15 145) 0%` → `oklch(0.746875 0.150937 148.75) 3.13%`), so the ghost fill vs the pixel beneath it differ by ≈2.9° of hue near the terminals. defects.defect: Dual write path for the selection plus an unbound public model: the same gesture both writes `selectedId` and emits `select`, the parent wires both, and nothing outside the stop editor ever reads the resulting state.

defects.defect: Hover is modelled in JavaScript — a `hoveredId` ref plus pointerenter/pointerleave on every handle — purely because the handle's scale rides an inline `transform` that shadows the `hover:` utility; the transform/transition strings are also re-authored per instance on every render.

Segment 0->1 C(a)=0.1831 C(b)=0.1617 C_painted_mid=0.0626 vs C_true_oklch_mid=0.1724 => 63.7% loss; 1->2 62.9%; 2->3 62.4%; 3->4 59.9%. Visible in docs/tranches/V/megatranche/audit/visual/shots/safari-mobile-light/generate.png: the strip's bands are saturated while the ramp 40px below passes through grey-brown. Component comment :62-64 claims 'the instrument shows its own state'. Canon: VISUAL-CONSTITUTION.md:143 'No path desaturates through gray'; §1 'value.js is a chromatic laboratory'.

defects.reproduction: node gc-probe4.mjs. Seed-independent — the loss is a property of the interpolation, not the palette.
defects.proposedCure: The ramp stops being a hand-rolled CSS gradient: either the producer Slider carries a colour-bearing track (the VISUAL-CONSTITUTION.md:104 'colour-bearing or neutral track chosen by semantics' arm), or the gradient is generated by this repo's own interpolation. A colour library emitting an un-hinted sRGB gradient is a contradiction in terms.

defects.defect: Three action species (Regenerate, Save, Copy) are rendered twice — once in the plate chrome and once in the Dock control set — when the constitution says they live in ONE Dock control set. The component exposes them specifically so the Dock can call them, then renders them inline as well.

Plate: GenerateControls.vue:157-164, :165-174, :175-184; and :115 `defineExpose({ regenerate, save, copyColors })`. One action/selection owner across Generate'. The comment :120-128 celebrates killing 'the orphan toolbar row' — but the Dock set is the duplicate that survived.

defects.defect: The editable plate title is inert — the typed name is discarded and every save is written as the literal 'Generated Palette', despite a source comment declaring the name to be load-bearing provenance FOR the save.

Consumer GeneratePane.vue:14 `function onSave(colors: string[])` never declares `name`; :19 `pm.createPalette("Generated Palette", paletteColors)` hardcodes it. defects.defect: The plate chrome row wraps at the primary desktop viewport and does NOT wrap at half-width, inverting its authored responsive intent and manufacturing a ~340px void between the title and the count badge. This falsifies the prior pass's hypothesis that 200% zoom would compound the wrap.

Mechanism at :148 `flex-1 basis-[10rem]` = flex: 1 1 10rem; flex line-breaking uses the flex BASE size, so 160px title + badge + shrink-0 cluster exceeds the 438px content box; after the break flex-grow:1 inflates the title to 398px. Comment :139-142 claims 'at 390 the verbs settle onto their own right-aligned line'. Cost: 40px of plate height (220 vs 180) = 22% of the plate.
