result.axis: CHALLENGE-L — library structure (module boundaries, ownership, direction of dependency, public surface)
result.modelObserved: Opus 5 (1M context) — exact model id `claude-opus-5[1m]`; the tier this seat was explicitly spawned with, declared not inherited.
result.strongestDefect: L-1 + L-2 read together: value.js has ceded ownership of its own easing vocabulary to its design system. At the package level `@mkbabb/glass-ui` (5.2M) and `@mkbabb/keyframes.js` (608K) are the ONLY entries in `package.json#dependencies` (lines 82-85) while `src/` and `dist/` reference them ZERO times and glass-ui peer-depends back on `@mkbabb/value.js@^4.0.0` — a declared package cycle costing every library consumer 5.8 MB. At the type level the same inversion appears as `useGradientModel.ts:49 export type GradientInterval = EasingPickerValue` — a Vue picker's v-model payload becomes the data contract of `gradientParse.ts`, a headless CSS parser with zero Vue in it. Both cures are one edit in two places: value.js `/easing` mints `AuthoredEasing` + `serializeTimingFunction`, glass-ui narrows to them, `dependencies` empties — and L-3, L-4 and the duplicated literal minters dissolve rather than get patched.
result.negativeProof: Not applicable to the verdict (DEFECTIVE), but recorded so the absences are not re-litigated: (1) the premise's most-predicted defect is ABSENT — `grep -rn "@src" demo/workbenches/gradient/ | wc -l` → 0; every library import in this component's chain is a published subpath (`@mkbabb/value.js/easing`, `/color`, `/css`) that a real consumer could write, so the demo is a true proof of the public API here. (2) `package.json#exports` has no `"."` entry and nothing in src/demo/test/e2e imports bare `@mkbabb/value.js` — consistent, not a gap. (3) verbatimModuleSyntax: all three type-only imports in the subject (lines 30, 34, 36-40) are `import type`. (4) Visual audit `/#/gradient` × 4 Safari matrices: pageErrors 0, consoleErrors 0, overflowX 0, main 1 (REPORT.md:125,140,155,170); the 12 `bleeding` rows are the FadingScroll `width:max-content` strip by design; the 6 smallTapTargets and 1 namelessButton belong to the slug bar / stop handles / shell, not this component — its `.rail-btn` is exactly 24x24 CSS px, clearing the probe's `<24` filter and sitting on the WCAG 2.5.8 floor. The screenshot renders correctly.

defects.defect: The published library declares its own demo's design system as a runtime dependency, forming a declared package cycle and forcing 5.8 MB of unused install weight on every consumer.
defects.evidence: package.json:82-85 `"dependencies": {"@mkbabb/glass-ui":"^7.0.0","@mkbabb/keyframes.js":"^6.0.0"}` — the ONLY two entries. Measured: `grep -rn "@mkbabb/glass-ui|@mkbabb/keyframes" src/ | wc -l` → 0; `grep -rn "@mkbabb/glass-ui" dist/subpaths/*.js dist/value.js | wc -l` → 0; `grep -rn "@mkbabb/keyframes" demo/ | wc -l` → 0 (referenced by NOTHING in the repo). `du -sh node_modules/@mkbabb/glass-ui node_modules/@mkbabb/keyframes.js` → 5.2M + 608K, against dist/subpaths at 132K. glass-ui/package.json peerDependencies includes `"@mkbabb/value.js":"^4.0.0"`.
defects.mechanism: wrong-direction dependency declared at the package manifest level: demo-only tooling placed in `dependencies` instead of `devDependencies`, creating value.js → glass-ui → value.js.
defects.reproduction: `npm i @mkbabb/value.js@4.0.0` in an empty non-Vue project: the install pulls a Vue design system plus a keyframes engine and glass-ui's own peer set (vue, reka-ui, embla-carousel, tailwindcss, @mkbabb/pencil-boil). `import { CubicBezier } from "@mkbabb/value.js/easing"` uses none of them.
defects.proposedCure: Move both entries to `devDependencies`. `dependencies` becomes `{}` — the honest shape for a zero-runtime-dependency value library. Nothing breaks: `"files": ["dist", "!dist/gh-pages", …]` (package.json:49-53) never ships the demo.

defects.defect: The gradient domain model — including a headless CSS parser with zero Vue in it — is typed by a Vue component's v-model payload imported from the design system.
defects.evidence: demo/workbenches/gradient/composables/useGradientModel.ts:49 `export type GradientInterval = EasingPickerValue;` (imported from `@mkbabb/glass-ui/easing` at line 12). glass-ui's own declaration calls it "The picker's v-model payload" (node_modules/@mkbabb/glass-ui/dist/components/easing/composables/useEasingPicker.d.ts). It propagates into UI-free code: gradientParse.ts:41 `interface ParsedGradientModel { …; intervals: GradientInterval[] }` (that module has zero Vue imports); useGradientCSS.ts:53-62,120-133,232-254; and the subject's own public contract GradientEasingEditor.vue:48-50 `"update-interval": [index: number, value: EasingPickerValue]`.
defects.mechanism: inverted semantic ownership: the concept 'an authored easing curve = mode + re-parseable CSS literal + resolved callable + raw params' is a value.js concept, but value.js publishes no such record, so its own demo borrows one from a package that depends on it.
defects.reproduction: NONE (latent). Failure scenario: glass-ui 8 renames `term`→`jump` or makes `points` optional for steps mode — a semver-legal design-system component change. That silently breaks value.js's headless gradient CSS parser, its serializers and its persisted model shape, none of which involve a picker.
defects.proposedCure: value.js `/easing` mints the record: `export interface AuthoredEasing { readonly mode: "bezier"|"steps"; readonly css: string; readonly fn: EasingFunction; readonly points: readonly [number,number,number,number]; readonly steps: number; readonly term: JumpPosition }`. Then `GradientInterval = AuthoredEasing` (no glass-ui import in the model at all) and glass-ui narrows to `export type EasingPickerValue = AuthoredEasing` — consuming the library's vocabulary, the direction its peerDeps already declare. The glass-ui type imports at useGradientModel.ts:12, easingCatalogue.ts:31-35 and GradientEasingEditor.vue:30 all collapse to `@mkbabb/value.js/easing`.

defects.defect: The public surface parses CSS timing functions but cannot serialize one, so the demo hand-mints the literal and must stay byte-identical with a private glass-ui implementation — held in agreement by a comment.
defects.evidence: `grep -rn "export function serialize|export const serialize" src/css/ src/easing.ts` → serializeCssColor, serializeKeyframeSelector, serializeCssValue, serializeTimelineOptions — no timing-function serializer, while `/css` exports `parseTimingFunction` (src/subpaths/css.ts). Consequence at easingCatalogue.ts:38-56: comment says "glass-ui `useEasingPicker.readout` mints … MUST be byte-identical", then `bezierLiteral` re-implements `+n.toFixed(3)` joined by `", "` and `stepsLiteral` re-implements `steps(${n}, ${term})`.
defects.mechanism: asymmetric public surface (parse without serialize) forces a duplicate implementation of one CSS serialization law into a consumer, coupled to the original only by prose.
defects.reproduction: Deterministic from source: change glass-ui's `readout` join from `", "` to `","`. `bezierLiteral` still emits `", "`. The identity match at easingCatalogue.ts:220 (`SPECIMEN_TILES.find(t => t.css === interval.css)`) is a string compare, so it returns undefined, `tileIdFor` returns null, `specimenNameFor` (line 229) returns "custom" — all 30 bezier tiles render unpressed and every closed specimen row's head reads `custom` for a named preset, with no error raised anywhere.
defects.proposedCure: Add `serializeTimingFunction(ast: CssTimingFunction): string` to `src/css/`, exported from `/css` as the exact inverse of `parseTimingFunction`, round-trip tested in the existing test/bbnf-equivalence idiom. `bezierLiteral`/`stepsLiteral` delete; glass-ui's private minter delegates. One law, one home, provable by round-trip instead of by comment.

defects.defect: value.js declares the jump-term union and the jump-term array independently; glass-ui derives its name from the array; the demo casts across them — and any divergence detonates as a module-scope throw that kills the whole gradient chunk.
defects.evidence: src/easing.ts:13 `export type JumpPosition = "jump-start"|"jump-end"|"jump-none"|"jump-both";` and src/easing.ts:68 `export const jumpTerms = ["jump-start","jump-end","jump-none","jump-both"] as const;` — no derivation between them. glass-ui: `export type JumpTerm = (typeof jumpTerms)[number]`. Bridge cast at easingCatalogue.ts:136 `const position = term as JumpPosition;`. Runtime guard at src/easing.ts:136 returns `err({code:"jump_position_invalid"})`; easingCatalogue.ts:98-104 `easingValue` converts an err Result to a `throw`. The catalogue is built at module scope: easingCatalogue.ts:198 `export const SPECIMEN_FAMILIES = buildFamilies();`.
defects.mechanism: two hand-written declarations of one enum with no structural link, bridged by an unchecked cast at the consumer, guarding an eager module-scope evaluation.
defects.reproduction: Add "jump-middle" to `jumpTerms` (src/easing.ts:68) and forget `JumpPosition` (line 13). glass-ui's `JumpTerm` widens automatically and the picker offers the term; a `stepsTile` receives it; `steppedEase` returns err; `easingValue` throws during import evaluation of easingCatalogue.ts — a static import of GradientEasingEditor.vue → GradientVisualizer.vue → the async GradientPane chunk (demo/shell/usePaneRouter.ts:74). The entire gradient workbench fails to load from a one-line library edit.
defects.proposedCure: Delete the hand-written union: `export type JumpPosition = (typeof jumpTerms)[number];`. One declaration, mechanically derived; the cast at easingCatalogue.ts:136 deletes; divergence becomes impossible.

defects.defect: Interval identity is positional while stop identity is id-based, and the two are synced across modules by a length-only watcher that appends/truncates at the end — so inserting or removing a stop silently reassigns authored curves to the wrong stop pairs.
defects.evidence: useGradientModel.ts:33-37 (GradientStop has `id`); intervals have none. useGradientModel.ts:89-100 `watch(() => stops.value.length, len => { …intervals.value.push(linearInterval()); … intervals.value.length = needed })` — told only THAT the length changed, never WHERE. `removeStop` (122-125) removes by id from anywhere. `addStop` (116-120) sorts by position so an inserted stop can land first. The subject cements the ordinal contract: GradientEasingEditor.vue:48-50 `"update-interval": [index: number, …]` → useGradientModel.ts:134-140 `updateInterval(index, value)`.
defects.mechanism: a shadow array with no modelled identity, kept in size by a length signal that carries no positional information, in a different module from the identity-bearing collection it shadows.
defects.reproduction: Source-derived (all three sites quoted in the report). 1) initial `stops=[A@0%,B@100%]`, `intervals=[linear]` (useGradientModel.ts:79-83). 2) press `ease-out-back` on row `1 → 2` → `updateInterval(0,…)` → `intervals=[back]`. 3) click the rail near 0% → GradientVisualizer.vue:91 `addStop(...)` → sorted, new stop lands FIRST. 4) watcher sees len 2→3 and pushes `linearInterval()` at the END → `intervals=[back, linear]`. 5) `back`, authored for A→B, is now interval 0 = N→A; A→B is linear. Symmetrically `removeStop(firstStopId)` drops the LAST interval, shifting every curve one pair left; the specimen rows relabel (useSpecimenRows.ts:61) and report the wrong assignment as truth. Live confirmation was ABANDONED — the shared dev browser at :9000 is under concurrent control by other seats (the page self-navigated /#/gradient → /#/extract → /#/atmosphere mid-evaluate; other seats' ?probe=4 / ?probe=6 params observed) and the probe-parsimony edict applies.
defects.proposedCure: Architectural transposition: the easing belongs to the LEADING STOP, not a parallel array — `interface GradientStop { id; cssColor; position; easing: AuthoredEasing }` (the last stop's easing is simply unused). The length watcher DELETES; add/remove become identity-correct by construction; `updateInterval(index,…)` becomes `updateStop(id, { easing })` — the same id-addressed door every other mutation already uses; the subject's emit becomes `"update-easing": [stopId: string, value: AuthoredEasing]`; useSpecimenRows derives rows by a pairwise walk over one array instead of zipping two.

defects.defect: Dead re-export shims that exist only to preserve import paths — 7 of 9 re-exported names have zero consumers, and the 2 live ones form a three-hop alias chain the sibling workbench crosses in one hop.
defects.evidence: useGradientModel.ts:19-29, header verbatim "Re-exports (preserve public API surface)", re-exports 9 names. Measured outside the owning composables/ dir: `grep -rn "serializeCoalescedGradient|serializeRailRamp|linearInterval|parseGradientCSS|serializeGradient" demo/ … | grep -v composables/` → only two COMMENT hits (GradientStopEditor.vue:9, easingCatalogue.ts:44); `grep -rn "GradientParseResult|ParsedGradientModel" demo/ … | grep -v composables/` → no output. useGradientInterpolation.ts:13-17 re-exports INTERPOLATION_SPACES/HUE_INTERPOLATION_METHODS from color-session/color-space-meta with the comment "Re-exported here so the gradient tree's own consumers keep their import path". Chain: color-space-meta → useGradientInterpolation → useGradientModel → GradientVisualizer.vue:17-21. Sibling: demo/workbenches/mix/MixConfigBar.vue:18 imports the same constants from color-session/color-space-meta directly.
defects.mechanism: back-compat alias / dual path (owner edict 2: no aliases, migration shims, dual paths) — a re-export layer preserved for consumers that no longer exist.
defects.reproduction: Delete useGradientModel.ts:19-29 and useGradientInterpolation.ts:17, then repoint GradientVisualizer.vue:17-21 at ../../../color-session/color-space-meta. `npm run typecheck` passes — the greps above prove no other consumer exists.
defects.proposedCure: Delete both re-export blocks; import each concept from its single canonical home, as MixConfigBar.vue already does. Net −11 lines, one path per concept.

defects.defect: A leaf composable is imported from glass-ui's root barrel when a dedicated subpath publishes it, entering 21x more module graph; systemic across the demo, with three competing clipboard idioms alive.
defects.evidence: GradientEasingEditor.vue:29 `import { useClipboard } from "@mkbabb/glass-ui";` while it lives at dist/composables/dom/useClipboard.d.ts behind `"./dom"`. Measured first-hop weight: glass-ui.js imports 43 chunks / 168,303 bytes; dom.js imports 6 chunks / 7,876 bytes. Systemic: 37 root-barrel vs 82 subpath imports across demo/; all 15 clipboard import sites use the barrel and 0 use ./dom (greps in report). Three idioms: useClipboard at GradientEasingEditor.vue:94; writeClipboard with the CopyResult discarded at GradientVisualizer.vue:12,128 (same pane); raw `navigator.clipboard.writeText` at demo/picker/visual/PointerDebugOverlay.vue:112.
defects.mechanism: public-surface misuse — reaching a leaf through a package's aggregate entry, plus duplicate concept implementations for 'copy text with feedback'.
defects.reproduction: `grep -oE 'from *"\./[^"]+"' node_modules/@mkbabb/glass-ui/dist/glass-ui.js | sort -u | wc -l` → 43; same over dom.js → 6. Byte sums 168,303 vs 7,876.
defects.proposedCure: `import { useClipboard } from "@mkbabb/glass-ui/dom";` here, and one idiom per repo — `useClipboard` wherever a tick is shown, `writeClipboard` only where nothing is shown, never raw `navigator.clipboard`. Retire the 37 barrel imports to their subpaths.

defects.defect: The component re-implements two glass-ui 7.0.0 primitives that the demo already uses elsewhere — the disclosure accordion and the quiet icon button — and its child per-instance-overrides a design-system variant it is simultaneously requesting.
defects.evidence: Accordion hand-rolled at GradientEasingEditor.vue:61-71 + 117-147 (ref<number|null>, toggleInterval, hand-wired aria-expanded/aria-controls/id, v-show panel, manually rotated ChevronDown) vs glass-ui `Collapsible`/`CollapsibleTrigger`/`CollapsibleContent` (dist/components/collapsible/index.d.ts), already used at demo/workbenches/mix/MixSourceSelector.vue:181-226 with tokenized data-[state=open]:animate-collapsible-down transitions. Ghost icon buttons: 23 lines of scoped CSS at GradientEasingEditor.vue:269-291 vs glass-ui Button `emphasis?: "primary"|"secondary"|"quiet"|"text"`, `iconOnly?: boolean` (dist/components/button/Button.vue.d.ts:4-16), reachable via demo/ui/button and used by 22 demo files. Child: EasingSpecimenStrip.vue:163-170 re-declares display:flex/flex-direction:column/align-items/gap/padding on .specimen-tile — the exact geometry `shape="cell"` already applies (chipVariants.d.ts SHAPE.cell = "glass-chip--cell flex-col gap-1.5 px-2 py-2.5 text-micro").
defects.mechanism: second implementation of a concept that already has a home in the design system (owner edicts 4 and 5: glass-ui owns variants/primitives; style at the root component level, never per-instance).
defects.reproduction: NONE (structural). Verified by presence: `grep -rn "Collapsible" demo/` → MixSourceSelector.vue uses it; `grep -rl "/ui/button" demo/` → 22 files use glass-ui Button; this component uses neither.
defects.proposedCure: `<Collapsible v-model:open>` per specimen row; `<Button emphasis="quiet" icon-only size="xs">` for the two rail controls; delete .rail-btn/.rail-btn--on and the accordion state. If the --motion-accent tinted 'on' state has no `tone` that expresses it, that is a glass-ui Button variant request — it belongs there, not in demo scoped CSS. Drop the .specimen-tile geometry block and let shape="cell" own it.

defects.defect: `easingValue` — the Result-unwrap-or-throw helper — exists twice, byte-identical but for its error string, in two modules already inside one import tree.
defects.evidence: easingCatalogue.ts:98-104 and useGradientCSS.ts:71-77: identical signature `(result: ReturnType<typeof CubicBezier>, source: string): EasingFunction` and identical body `if (result.ok) return result.value; throw new Error(...)` — only the message text differs. Both are also called with `steppedEase(...)` results (easingCatalogue.ts:137, useGradientCSS.ts:113), which only type-checks because the two Result shapes coincide.
defects.mechanism: duplicated ownership of one concept across two private homes.
defects.reproduction: NONE (structural). `grep -n -A7 "function easingValue" <both files>` shows the duplication verbatim.
defects.proposedCure: One `unwrapEasing(result, source)` beside the model — or better, export `unwrapOrThrow` from src/easing.ts, since throw-on-err is a library Result ergonomic, not a gradient fact.

defects.defect: Two placement conventions for composables inside one workbench: gradient composables at gradient/composables/*, easing composable+catalogue three levels deeper under a component-named directory — producing the tree's only four-level cross-feature reach.
defects.evidence: demo/workbenches/gradient/composables/{gradientParse,useGradientCSS,useGradientInterpolation,useGradientModel}.ts vs demo/workbenches/gradient/GradientVisualizer/easing/{easingCatalogue.ts,useSpecimenRows.ts}. Consequence: useSpecimenRows.ts:13 `import { useSafeAccentFn } from "../../../../color-session/useContrastSafeColor";` — the only `../../../../` in the workbench. The sibling `extract/` already follows the other rule (ImageEyedropper/{ImageEyedropper.vue,composables/}).
defects.mechanism: inconsistent module lattice — a component-named container directory used as a namespace, so co-located composables sit at a different depth than the feature's other composables.
defects.reproduction: NONE (structural). `grep -rn 'from "../../../..' demo/workbenches/gradient/` → one hit, useSpecimenRows.ts:13.
defects.proposedCure: Greenfield lattice, one rule — a feature directory owns its components AND its composables at the same depth: gradient/{model/, easing/, stops/, code/, GradientVisualizer.vue, GradientPane.vue}. GradientVisualizer/ as a container disappears; the deepest cross-feature reach becomes ../../color-session/… matching MixConfigBar.vue:18.

defects.defect: demo/ui/ is 18 one-line pass-through alias directories re-exporting glass-ui from its ROOT barrel, when each component publishes a dedicated subpath — and the paths are genuinely dual.
defects.evidence: `cat demo/ui/button/index.ts` → `export { Button } from "@mkbabb/glass-ui";`; `cat demo/ui/collapsible/index.ts` → `export { Collapsible, CollapsibleTrigger, CollapsibleContent } from "@mkbabb/glass-ui";`. 18 such dirs measured (1 line, 1 glass-ui line each). Dual path measured: `dialog` imported via demo/ui/dialog by 3 files and via @mkbabb/glass-ui/dialog by 2. The subject's parent straddles both in one block: GradientVisualizer.vue:9-13 imports Select/Slider from ../../../ui/* and DockControl from @mkbabb/glass-ui/dock.
defects.mechanism: contrivance directory (edict 3) + alias/dual path (edict 2) + root-barrel reach (L-7), stacked.
defects.reproduction: NONE (structural). `for d in demo/ui/*/; do wc -l $d/index.ts; done` → 18 files at 1 line each, all `from "@mkbabb/glass-ui"`.
defects.proposedCure: Delete demo/ui/*/index.ts; import every glass-ui component from its own subpath. The memory note 'shadcn-vue components in demo/ui — DO NOT modify' is stale for these 18: they hold no shadcn source, only a re-export line.

defects.defect: The specimen catalogue is built as a module-scope side effect, so 1,617 curve evaluations and 22.6 KB of retained SVG path strings are paid on gradient-pane open whether or not any easing row is ever expanded.
defects.evidence: easingCatalogue.ts:198 `export const SPECIMEN_FAMILIES: SpecimenFamily[] = buildFamilies();` — top level. Static import chain: easingCatalogue → GradientEasingEditor.vue:35 → GradientVisualizer.vue:16 → async GradientPane (demo/shell/usePaneRouter.ts:74). Measured against this repo's dist/subpaths/easing.js: tiles 33, build 3.02 ms cold / 1.77 ms avg warm, 22,651 bytes of path strings retained. glyphPath samples 49 points per curve (samples=48, i<=samples) with two toFixed(3) formats each → 1,617 evaluations, ~3,234 string formats.
defects.mechanism: eager module-scope evaluation of derived data in a leaf module — the catalogue is a pure function of the frozen library constant bezierPresets but is neither lazy nor build-time generated.
defects.reproduction: `node scratchpad/cat-bench.mjs` (the exact catalogue arithmetic against dist/subpaths/easing.js) → `tiles: 33 / build ms (cold): 3.02 / path-string bytes retained: 22651 / avg ms over 10 warm builds: 1.77`.
defects.proposedCure: Make SPECIMEN_FAMILIES a lazily-built module singleton (getter memoized on first strip mount), or generate it at build time as static data — it is a pure function of a frozen library constant, so both are free.

result.axis: CHALLENGE-L — library structure (module boundaries, ownership, direction of dependency, public surface) for demo/workbenches/generate/GenerateControls.vue
result.modelObserved: Opus 5 (1M context) — exact model id `claude-opus-5[1m]`, matching the explicit Opus 5 declaration this seat was spawned with. Declared, not inherited.

defects.defect: `test/` — the only region of the repo that crosses the src/↔demo/ boundary — is type-checked by no TypeScript program, and already contains 27 latent type errors. The demo's own tests ARE checked (3 files in the demo program); the library's 19 are not.
defects.evidence: tsconfig.lib.json include = 13 enumerated src patterns; tsconfig.demo.json include = ["demo/","src/vite-env.d.ts"]; tsconfig.json = {files:[],references:[…]}. `npx tsc -p tsconfig.lib.json --noEmit --listFilesOnly | grep -c "/value.js/test/"` → 0; same for tsconfig.demo.json → 0; `grep -c "/value.js/demo/test/"` → 3. package.json: typecheck = vue-tsc -p tsconfig.lib.json --noEmit && vue-tsc -p tsconfig.demo.json --noEmit. vitest.config.ts has no `typecheck` block (esbuild transpile-only). Probe program over test/+demo/: 27 errors, 27 under test/, 0 under demo/. Sample: test/value-domain-clamp.test.ts(35,26) TS2339 Property 'hue' does not exist on type '… | { key: string; min: number; max: number; unit: "K"; }'; test/status-lamp.test.ts(149,15) TS2488; test/math.test.ts(318,40) TS2345.
defects.mechanism: A boundary enforced by a two-program tsconfig split is left unenforced at the single place it is actually crossed. The lib program is genuinely clean (0 of 88 files match glass-ui|/demo/) partly BECAUSE the boundary-crossing files were placed outside every program.
defects.reproduction: Create tsconfig.probe-test.json extending tsconfig.base.json with include:["test/","demo/","src/vite-env.d.ts"] and the compilerOptions of tsconfig.demo.json (drop composite/references); run `npx vue-tsc -p tsconfig.probe-test.json --noEmit`; observe 27 errors, all under test/. (Probe file was deleted; git status clean.)
defects.proposedCure: Add a third leaf tsconfig.test.json (include:["test/"], references both leaves) and append it to the `typecheck` script; fix the 27 errors rather than suppress them. This is the prerequisite for every other test-side cure — until test/ is in a program, new tests inherit the same blindness.

defects.defect: The `@src/*` deep-path alias — declared RETIRED by the T.W1 dogfood keystone and correctly proven absent from demo/ by pass 1 — is alive in `test/`: 6 imports across 4 files reaching library internals directly, each with an exact published-subpath equivalent. It resolves at runtime (vitest alias) and fails at typecheck (no tsconfig counterpart), so it has survived only because no type program has ever read those files.
defects.evidence: `grep -rn "@src/" test/` → test/gradient-v4-consume.test.ts ← "@src/subpaths/css"; test/parsing/timeline/parsing-easing.test.ts ← "@src/subpaths/css" and "@src/subpaths/easing"; test/transform/path-geometry.test.ts ← "@src/transform/path"; test/transform/decompose-targeted.test.ts ← "@src/transform/decompose" (×2). src/subpaths/transform.ts re-exports the entirety of both reached internals (decomposeMatrix2D/3D, recompose*, slerp, interpolateDecomposed, PathGeometry, getTotalLength, getPointAtLength + types). Alias defined at vitest.config.ts:11 (`"@src": path.resolve(…, "src")`); tsconfig.demo.json:6 records the `@src/*` path was RETIRED. 6 of the 27 probe errors are TS2307 'Cannot find module @src/…'.
defects.mechanism: Pass 1's §L-5 inverted: there, a hand-written `paths` mirror shadowed `exports`; here a bundler alias has NO type-program counterpart at all, so the weaker resolver is the only one consulted. Both are the same disease — a boundary asserted in one tool and unenforced in another. The two `@src/subpaths/*` cases are sharpest: they reach the subpath entry file by filesystem path, deliberately stepping around the exports map that exists to serve exactly that module.
defects.reproduction: `grep -rn "@src/" test/` (6 hits); then run the L3-1 probe program and observe six TS2307 'Cannot find module @src/…' errors — the imports resolve under vitest but not under tsc.
defects.proposedCure: Rewrite the 6 imports onto @mkbabb/value.js/{css,easing,transform}; delete the `@src` alias from vitest.config.ts:11; narrow vite.config.ts's `@src` to the sourceExportPlugin `?source` use only (one of its two documented justifications dies with these six lines).

defects.defect: Inverted dependency: the library's unit suite imports demo code (10 of 19 test files), so the library suite cannot run without demo/ on disk. And coverage is inverted exactly where it matters — generate-color.ts (243 lines, the largest and most nearly-pure module in demo/color-session/) has ZERO unit coverage, while six smaller siblings in the same directory ARE covered by the LIBRARY suite. Its only automated coverage anywhere is an e2e browser oracle.
defects.evidence: `grep -rl "\.\./demo/" test/*.ts | wc -l` → 10 (of 19). Annexed areas: demo/picker/…/sliderAnnouncement, demo/platform/transport/availability, demo/shell/dock/status-lamp, demo/shell/viewSchema, demo/palettes/mix, demo/workbenches/gradient/composables/{gradientParse,useGradientCSS,useGradientInterpolation,useGradientModel}, demo/workbenches/extract/…/useImageSampler, 5× demo/color-session/*. Per-module coverage in demo/color-session/: picker-color.ts 217ln yes(2), ink.ts 174ln yes(2), palettes-ramp.ts 120ln yes, color-chips/sample.ts 91ln yes, view-accent.ts 47ln yes, color-utils.ts 25ln yes(2) — vs generate-color.ts 243ln NO, prng.ts 11ln NO. `grep -rln "generate-color\|generatePalette" test/ e2e/` → e2e/smoke/oracles/o20-generate-plate.spec.ts only.
defects.mechanism: The repo's own test infrastructure cannot tell where the library ends — independent corroboration of pass 1's §L-4 from a direction §L-4 never used ('the library's test suite already treats this as library code', not 'it looks library-shaped'). The e2e-only coverage is an inverted test pyramid: a pure, seeded, total, sub-millisecond numeric function whose sole test drives Safari. Pass 2's §8.2 showed what that regime misses — O-20 asserted backgroundColor and stayed green through the entire life of a dead verb.
defects.reproduction: `grep -rl "\.\./demo/" test/*.ts | wc -l` → 10; `grep -rln "generate-color\|generatePalette" test/ e2e/` → e2e oracle only; per-module loop over demo/color-session/*.ts checking `grep -rl "color-session/.*<basename>\"" test/`.
defects.proposedCure: Write test/generate-color.test.ts against the current demo module — seed-exactness (same (count,preset,harmony,seed) ⇒ identical output), preset-range containment in OKLCh, harmony hue geometry, and the count-dependence of generateHues that forbids truncation. These tests ARE the specification the src/palette/ promotion needs and they move with the code; promoting 243 untested lines into a published subpath first would ship an unspecified public API. Sequence this BEFORE pass 1's move 1.

defects.defect: CORRECTION to pass 1's proposed cure: promoting demo/color-session/generate-color.ts to src/palette/ as written would ship 16 user-facing English UI strings inside the published colour library, making @mkbabb/value.js permanently un-internationalisable behind a semver contract.
defects.evidence: `grep -cn "label:\|description:" demo/color-session/generate-color.ts` → 18. generate-color.ts:47-56 — vibrant description:"High chroma, bold tones"; pastel "Soft, light, airy"; earth "Muted clay and soil"; …; :79-84 — "split-complementary": {description:"Base + two flanking complements"}, etc. Rendered verbatim by the subject component at GenerateControls.vue:246 ({{ GENERATION_PRESETS[p].description }}) and :275 ({{ HARMONY_DEFS[h].description }}).
defects.mechanism: The module pass 1 correctly identified as library-shaped is not in fact pure: it fuses numeric ranges/algorithms (reusable, library-owned) with application voice (this app's copy deck). Promoting the fused artefact would hand every future consumer of the numeric ranges a copy deck they did not ask for, and would create a new, harder-to-reverse defect inside src/.
defects.reproduction: `grep -n "description:" demo/color-session/generate-color.ts` → 16 prose strings at :47-56 and :79-84.
defects.proposedCure: Split at the promotion, not after it: src/palette/presets.ts publishes PRESET_RANGES: Record<PresetName,{l,c,h}> (numbers only); src/palette/harmony.ts publishes the six generators and HarmonyName (algorithms only); the description strings stay in demo/ as a Record<PresetName,string> copy table keyed by the published union, so a missing entry is a type error. Preserves the whole of pass 1's argument while keeping the published surface free of application voice.

defects.defect: Seeded randomness has two independent live implementations — demo/color-session/prng.ts and glass-ui's own mulberry32 compiled into watercolor-dot.js — and GenerateControls.vue invokes BOTH on the same visual element (one decides each swatch's colour, the other its shape), while @mkbabb/value.js/math, the package that exists to publish numeric primitives, ships neither.
defects.evidence: `grep -rn "mulberry32" demo src test` → demo/color-session/prng.ts:2 (definition), generate-color.ts:35 (import), :219 (`const rng = seed != null ? mulberry32(seed) : Math.random`), GenerateControls.vue:89 (comment). `grep -o "mulberry[A-Za-z0-9]*" node_modules/@mkbabb/glass-ui/dist/watercolor-dot.js | sort -u` → mulberry32. Same element, both paths: GenerateControls.vue:95,99 → generatePalette(…, seed:number) → demo mulberry32 → swatch COLOUR; GenerateControls.vue:204 → :seed="`gen-${css}-${i}`" (string) → glass-ui mulberry32 → same swatch's SHAPE. `cat src/subpaths/math.ts` publishes clamp, scale, lerp, lerpArray, logerp, deCasteljau, cubicBezier, interpBezier, cubicBezierToString; `grep -rn "mulberry32\|seedrandom" src/` → no output.
defects.mechanism: Wrong home for a shared primitive, with the strongest possible empirical signature: the concept has already been independently re-derived twice by two separate packages. One dot, two PRNGs, two seed registers (number vs string), no shared definition of 'deterministic given a seed'; the seed bench note at :212-214 reports only one of the two.
defects.reproduction: `grep -rn "mulberry32" demo src test` (1 demo definition) + `grep -o "mulberry[A-Za-z0-9]*" node_modules/@mkbabb/glass-ui/dist/watercolor-dot.js | sort -u` (glass-ui's own) + `grep -rn "mulberry32\|seedrandom" src/` (empty).
defects.proposedCure: src/math/prng.ts → mulberry32 plus hashSeed(string): number so the string and numeric seed registers become one register; publish from @mkbabb/value.js/math; delete demo/color-session/prng.ts. File the glass-ui-consumes-it half together with pass 2's §L2-3 ColorHarmony ask as ONE RF-17 row — both are the same direction of dependency (colour/numeric primitives flow from the colour library into the design system, not the reverse).

defects.defect: Evidence-base gap: the two specialised visual matrices that could falsify this component's two open accessibility-structural findings (§L-11 forced-colors class list, §L2-1 zero-focusable swatches) do not cover the /generate route at all.
defects.evidence: `ls docs/tranches/V/megatranche/audit/visual/shots/` → 10 matrices. `ls forced-colors-desktop/` → adminusers.png blob.png browse.png gradient.png picker.png. `ls keyboard-focus-desktop/` → identical 5. `ls */generate.png` → only the four safari-* matrices. forced-colors-desktop is the only probe that would exercise foundation.css:689's @media (forced-colors: active) selector list that had to grow a .generate-swatch entry; keyboard-focus-desktop is the only probe that would exhibit five swatches with zero focus reachability — which is why pass 2 had to obtain it by hand-driven Playwright.
defects.mechanism: Not a defect in the component: a gap in the evidence base the formation reasons from. Two of this file's three most serious open items sit in the matrices' blind spot, so the audit apparatus cannot independently confirm or refute them.
defects.reproduction: `ls docs/tranches/V/megatranche/audit/visual/shots/forced-colors-desktop/ docs/tranches/V/megatranche/audit/visual/shots/keyboard-focus-desktop/` — 5 routes each, no generate.png.
defects.proposedCure: Extend both matrices to /#/generate (and to the other routes they omit) before the mega-tranche seals its visual evidence.

defects.defect: EVIDENCE UPGRADE (not a new defect) to §L-10/§L2-2: the hand-rolled CSS rail's engine interpolation diverges from the app's own computed path by a measured 25.5% chroma and 16.8deg hue per stop pair — the SAMPLING LAW violation quantified, and visible in the shipped screenshot.
defects.evidence: GenerateControls.vue:65-73 builds `linear-gradient(to right, …)` from raw stops with no `in <space>`. Computed against the shipped library (dist/subpaths/{color,css}.js) for the adjacent teal/magenta pair of the dark-matrix palette: APP midpoint (OKLCh lerp, what color-chips/sample.ts legislates) = oklch(0.640, 0.215, 262.5deg); ENGINE midpoint (sRGB lerp, a raw CSS gradient stop pair) = oklch(0.522, 0.160, 279.3deg) → 25.5% chroma loss, 16.8deg hue drift. Corroborated visually in docs/tranches/V/megatranche/audit/visual/shots/safari-desktop-dark/generate.png: a washed low-chroma band between the teal and magenta stops that appears nowhere in the palette or in the specimen strip above it.
defects.mechanism: Because the gradient carries no interpolation space, WHICH midpoint the user sees is the rendering engine's choice, not the application's — exactly the 'engine divergence' the chips module's SAMPLING LAW names in prose. Pass 1 rated this INFO reasoning the law was 'scoped to the chip family'; the number removes the remaining reason to treat it as advisory.
defects.reproduction: node --input-type=module: import ./dist/subpaths/{color,css}.js; parse oklch(0.6 0.13 195) and oklch(0.68 0.30 330); lerp channels directly for the OKLCh path; convertColor both to 'rgb', average channels, convertColor back to 'oklch' for the engine path; compare channel[1] (chroma) and channel[2] (hue).
defects.proposedCure: No change to pass 2's MAJOR rating or its cure (glass-ui Slider owns a first-class ramp track carrying the WCAG 1.4.11 contrast ring, per gate G-2'). This finding only removes the grounds for treating the SAMPLING LAW as advisory on this instrument.

result.strongestDefect: L3-1 — `test/` is type-checked by no TypeScript program (0 of 19 files in either leaf, proven by `tsc --listFilesOnly`), while `demo/test/` IS checked (3 files). It is simultaneously the ONLY region of the repo that crosses the src/↔demo/ boundary (10 of 19 files import demo code, L3-3) and the only region no gate reads. It already holds 27 real type errors, 0 of which are in demo/. It is strongest because it is the enabling defect: L3-2's six retired-alias `@src/*` deep paths have survived solely because nothing type-checks them (they fail TS2307 the instant a program looks), and L3-3's proposed generation-core spec would land in the same blind region. result.negativeProof: Verdict is DEFECTIVE, so no global negative is claimed. The measured negatives that DID hold, recorded so a fourth seat need not re-run them: (1) `demo/` is type-clean — my probe checked test/ AND demo/ together and produced 27 errors, 0 under demo/. (2) inv-K-1 holds structurally — `tsc -p tsconfig.lib.json --listFilesOnly` lists 88 files, `grep -c "glass-ui\|/value.js/demo/"` → 0. This CONFIRMS BY MEASUREMENT passes 1–2's "direction correct" verdict on GenerateControls.vue lines 20 and 25–31 — the one boundary in this component's import block that is unambiguously right. (5) The absent root `.` export is deliberate and documented, not a defect: package.json#exports has 7 keys and no `.`, main/module/types are all undefined, README.md:15-21 lists exactly those 7 subpaths and every example imports one (:30 /css, :52 /color, :75 /easing, :89 /quantize), and no source file anywhere imports the bare specifier. (6) `files: ["dist","!dist/gh-pages","!dist/gh-pages/**"]` — demo never ships in the tarball, so L3-3 is a development-graph defect, not a published-package one. (7) PIN INTACT at a third HEAD: shasum -a 256 of GenerateControls.vue = 4f95c57c7a6c46fa15a08b98b954a39529a12f71bda672423c7008c33ae324f6 at HEAD 7cae8bd0, with `git log c654824e..HEAD -- demo/workbenches/generate/` empty. result.axis: CHALLENGE-C — implementation defects in demo/workbenches/gradient/GradientVisualizer/GradientStopEditor.vue (pass 2: independent re-verification + 4 new findings + 1 mechanism correction)
result.modelObserved: Opus 5 — model id claude-opus-5[1m] (1M context), the tier explicitly declared by the orchestrator for this seat. Not inherited, not undeclared.

defects.defect: Drag (and shift+arrow) inverts stop order — the model has no ordering invariant, so the app emits CSS that its own parser rejects and the rail/tile paint a CSS-clamped lie
defects.evidence: Live, my own run: afterDrag labels ["Gradient stop at 77%","…50%","…63%","…100%"] (DOM order == model order); rail computed background-image head = linear-gradient(90deg, oklch(0.65 0.18 265) 76.6%, oklch(0.657192 0.177842 256.369) 74.18%, oklch(0.664384 0.175685 247.739) 71.76%, …) — positions DESCEND. Round-trip: `npx vite-node evidence/parse-probe.ts` → parseGradientCSS -> reject: stop positions must be non-decreasing. Source: demo/workbenches/gradient/composables/useGradientModel.ts:127-131 vs the sorting addStop at :118; guard on the way IN at gradientParse.ts:284-290.
defects.mechanism: No invariant owner for the ordered-stop model: updateStop is a primitive map() that never re-sorts, while the parser enforces monotonicity on input only. Sortedness is an invariant on insert and a coincidence on drag.
defects.reproduction: http://localhost:9000/ → set location.hash='#/gradient' in-page → click the rail at 50% → drag the leftmost handle right to ~75%. Read the handle aria-labels in DOM order and getComputedStyle(bar).backgroundImage.
defects.proposedCure: Replace updateStop with one model action that owns ordering totally — setStopPosition(id, position) that maps then .sort((a,b)=>a.position-b.position) — landed together with C2's identity-keyed intervals so the re-sort cannot scramble easing. Sort, do not clamp: clamping to (prev,next) would make a stop un-reorderable.

defects.defect: Grab-offset teleport: pressing anywhere but a handle's exact pixel centre and moving the pointer 1 px relocates the stop by the whole grab offset
defects.evidence: Live, pasted: RESULT_grab_offset = { grabbed_px_right_of_centre: 8, pointer_travelled_px: 1, handle_travelled_px: 10.12, label_before: "Gradient stop at 0%", label_after: "Gradient stop at 2%" } on a 462px rail. Source: GradientStopEditor.vue:136-146 — emit("update:position", id, getPosition(e)) is absolute and ungated; the hit pseudo that invites the off-centre grab is .rail-handle::before at :374-391 (24px fine / var(--touch-target)=44px coarse).
defects.mechanism: onHandlePointerDown records no grab offset, so the first pointermove snaps the stop centre to the raw pointer. The 4px dead-zone the function already computes (handleGesture.moved) is wired only to the re-tap-to-deselect decision, never to the position emit.
defects.reproduction: Fresh /#/gradient, 2-stop seed. page.mouse.move(handleCentreX + 8, barCentreY); mouse.down(); mouse.move(handleCentreX + 9, barCentreY). Read the handle's aria-label and bounding-box centre before/after.
defects.proposedCure: Capture grabDx = e.clientX - handleCentreX at pointerdown (together with a cached bar rect, which also kills C3's per-move forced layout), gate the first emit on the dead-zone the file already computes (`if (!handleGesture.moved) return;`), and emit positionAt(e.clientX - grabDx). One change retires the teleport, the accidental-nudge class, and half of C3's cost.

defects.defect: Adding a stop silently re-attaches every authored easing curve to a different pair of stops; removing one does the mirror
defects.evidence: Live (pass 1, retained): before insert heads ["1 → 2linear","2 → 3steps"]; after clicking the rail at 25% heads ["1 → 2linear","2 → 3steps","3 → 4linear"] — steps(4, jump-end) moved from 50%→100% onto 25%→50%. Source: useGradientModel.ts:89-100 (length watcher pushes/truncates at the TAIL) vs addStop at :118 (inserts in SORTED position).
defects.mechanism: Intervals are an index-keyed parallel array; the watcher observes only stops.length so it cannot know where the stop landed and always guesses 'at the end'. An adjacency relation modelled as a positional array.
defects.reproduction: /#/gradient with stops [0,50,100]; open easing interval row 2, pick the steps specimen; click the rail at 25%; read the interval readouts and row heads.
defects.proposedCure: Hang the interval on the stop that OPENS it — GradientStop { id, cssColor, position, easing }, last stop's easing ignored — so the curve travels with its own stop through any insert/remove/sort. That deletes the intervals array, its sync watcher, and the three 'Gradient interval N is missing' throws (useGradientCSS.ts:189/240, GradientVisualizer.vue:77) outright.

defects.defect: Pointer selection never focuses the handle, so the entire documented keyboard contract (±1/±10 nudge, Delete, Escape) is dead after a mouse select
defects.evidence: Live, pasted mechanism proof: PROBE_A = { pointerdown:1, mousedown:0, mouseup:0, click:1, focus:0, defaultPrevented:true, activeElement:"BODY/" }. Live consequence with selection PROVED by the transform ladder: D = { selection_proved_by_scale:["1.25","1"], activeElement_after_click:"BODY/", labels_after_click == labels_after_2x_ArrowRight, keyboard_had_effect:false }. Source: e.preventDefault() at GradientStopEditor.vue:120; keyboard handler at :173-187; docstring claim 'Escape clears selection while the handle keeps focus' at :169-172.
defects.mechanism: preventDefault on pointerdown suppresses the compatibility mouse events; focus is the default action of mousedown, so the button never becomes document.activeElement. Selection state and focus state are two different objects, and every line of the keyboard handler assumes they are one.
defects.reproduction: Fresh /#/gradient. Install capture listeners for pointerdown/mousedown/focus on a handle; real mouse press+release on its centre; read the counters and document.activeElement; then press ArrowRight twice and compare aria-labels.
defects.proposedCure: Drop e.preventDefault() from pointerdown (text selection is already prevented by `select-none touch-none` on the rail at :203 and by pointer capture at :133) and, if a native drag image still appears, kill exactly that default with @dragstart.prevent on the handle. The :focus-visible ring system the file already builds at :328-359 then finally serves the pointer path.

defects.defect: Every drag pointermove emits update:position twice — the bar's 'fallback path while a handle drag is live' is a duplicate, not a fallback
defects.evidence: Live, my own run: E = { barMoves:21, barMovesTargetIsHandle:21, handleMoves:21, capture:"got" } over a 20-step drag — bar and handle handler counts are equal and every bar-level move targeted a handle. Pass 1 independently measured 21/22. Cost: evidence/serialize-cost.ts → 0.223 ms per invalidation at 3 stops. Source: GradientStopEditor.vue:91-99 with the false comment at :93.
defects.mechanism: Pointer capture retargets the event to the handle but the event still bubbles to the bar, so both handlers run; each calls getPosition (a getBoundingClientRect forced layout) and emits, causing two whole-array rebuilds per move.
defects.reproduction: Fresh /#/gradient; addEventListener('pointermove') on the bar and on a handle; real mouse drag of 20 steps; read the counters.
defects.proposedCure: Delete the branch — `if (draggingId.value) return;` — because with capture on the handle the bar has no job during a drag; and cache the bar rect at pointerdown (supplied by C11's cure) so the drag stops forcing layout at all.

defects.defect: The component's only behavioural gate is RED at HEAD, asserts DOM that no longer exists, and Playwright is not wired to CI at all — so the whole defect set above is unobservable
defects.evidence: Pass-1 run: `npx playwright test e2e/smoke/views/gradient.spec.ts e2e/smoke/oracles/o21-gradient-rail.spec.ts --project=smoke` → 5 failed / 8 passed, including views/gradient.spec.ts:144 'stop add … drag, and touch-true remove'. My own greps: `grep -rln playwright .github/workflows/` → no matches (ci.yml, deploy-pages.yml, release.yml only); `grep -rn 'gradient-ruler-cap|gradient-rung' e2e/` → o21-gradient-rail.spec.ts:135,163, and the same grep over demo/ src/ → no matches. Vacuous assertion at e2e/smoke/views/gradient.spec.ts:157-175.
defects.mechanism: Gate vacuity: the single drag assertion is `expect(pct).toBeGreaterThan(60)` on one handle after `mid.hover()` (which grabs the exact centre, so C11 can never fire), and nothing anywhere asserts stop ORDER.
defects.reproduction: Run the two spec files as above; then run the two greps.
defects.proposedCure: Add a vitest gate on the MODEL (useGradientModel) asserting the ordering invariant across drag/keyboard/add/remove, plus an interval↔segment identity assertion; wire the Playwright smoke project into ci.yml; delete the two oracles that assert retired test-ids. Exact mutation proving today's vacuity: delete the .sort() from useGradientModel.ts:118 — every assertion in the repo stays green while the model goes non-monotonic. Equally green-preserving: HANDLE_HALF = 0, deleting onHandleKeydown, and deleting the duplicate emit.

defects.defect: The route's parse path THROWS instead of rejecting on the 8 empty-argument colour functions (MT-F001 live), inverting the 'failure is LOUD' contract into an uncaught TypeError inside a debounce timer with no verdict rendered
defects.evidence: `npx vite-node evidence/parse-probe.ts` → parseCssColor("oklch()") -> THROW TypeError: Cannot read properties of undefined (reading 'replace'), same for rgb/hsl/hwb/lab/lch/oklab/color; parseGradientCSS -> THROW on `linear-gradient(90deg, oklch(), blue)`. Source: src/css/grammar.ts:181 `splitTopLevel(slash[0]!.replace(/,/g," "), "space")`.
defects.mechanism: splitTopLevel pushes its tail only when non-empty, so an empty body yields [] and the non-null assertion on slash[0] is false. gradientParse.ts:92 treats parseCssColor as a TOTAL validity oracle, so the throw escapes parseGradientCSS → applyCSS → GradientVisualizer.onParseCSS (:102-108, no try) → the code editor's debounce timer callback, where nothing can catch it.
defects.reproduction: Type `linear-gradient(90deg, oklch(), blue)` into the gradient CSS editor on /#/gradient; or run evidence/parse-probe.ts.
defects.proposedCure: Fix it in the library, not the pane: in grammar.ts, `const head = slash[0]; if (head === undefined) return failure(source, "css_syntax", ["CSS color"]);`. A try/catch in onParseCSS would be a masking fallback (edict 2) and would leave every other parseCssColor caller exposed.

defects.defect: Accessibility implemented as decoration: no keyboard path to ADD a stop, slider semantics on a bare <button> with no aria-value*, no aria-live, no focus restoration after remove, and 20×20 visible targets
defects.evidence: REPORT.json /#/gradient, identical in all 4 Safari matrices: smallTapTargets includes {"w":20,"h":20,"tag":"button","label":"Gradient stop at 0%"} and {"…100%"} — 2 of the route's 6, ×4 matrices = 8 rows. Measured live: rail div has role null / tabindex null; handles have role null and no aria-valuenow/min/max/valuetext despite the arrow-key pattern at GradientStopEditor.vue:173-187. removeStop at :158-162 restores no focus.
defects.mechanism: The component implements a slider's behaviour on a button's semantics and a pointer-only creation gesture, so AT is told 'button' and keyboard users cannot create a stop at all (WCAG 2.1.1 A; 2.4.3; 2.5.8 met only by an invisible 24px pseudo).
defects.reproduction: Tab through /#/gradient and enumerate focusables inside main; inspect a handle's computed role and aria-* ; read REPORT.json results[].probe.a11y.smallTapTargets for the four gradient rows.
defects.proposedCure: Give the handle role="slider" with aria-valuemin/max/now/valuetext and aria-orientation, add Home/End/PageUp/PageDown, make the rail itself focusable with Enter/'+' to mint a stop at the selected position, announce add/remove through one aria-live=polite region, move focus to the neighbouring handle after a remove, and raise the visible dot to 24px so the hit target and the seen target agree.

defects.defect: One axis, two denominators: getPosition measures a 304px border-box track while handleLeft places handles on a 302px padding-box track
defects.evidence: Live, pasted: F_axis = { borderLeftWidth:"1px", borderBoxWidth:324, paddingBoxWidth:322, pointerTrackLen_getPosition:304, handleCentreTrackLen_handleLeft:302 }. Confirmed at the other viewport: at w=462, handleLeft(0) centres at x+11 while getPosition maps pointer x+10 to 0%. Source: GradientStopEditor.vue:55-57 (handleLeft, percentages resolve against the padding box) vs :75-81 (getPosition, getBoundingClientRect = border box).
defects.mechanism: The rail carries a 1px border (.gradient-rail :319), so the two mappings of 'position along the rail' differ by 1px in origin and 2px in length. HANDLE_HALF is a bare JS literal the stylesheet knows nothing about.
defects.reproduction: On /#/gradient evaluate getComputedStyle(bar).borderLeftWidth and getBoundingClientRect().width, then compare handleLeft's calc() against getPosition's arithmetic at p=0 and p=100.
defects.proposedCure: Declare the inset ONCE as a --rail-inset custom property consumed by the paint contract, by handleLeft, and by getPosition; this also supplies C7's cure (ramp inset to the same track) and C9's cure (geometry back in the stylesheet).

defects.defect: The handle track (inset 11px) and the ramp paint (full border-box) do not share an axis — the file's own headline invariant is false
defects.evidence: Live: barRect {x:224,w:462}, borderTopWidth 1px, bgSize "100% 100%, 16px 16px", bgOrigin border-box; handle centres at 235 and 675 → 11px inside each ramp end = 2.38% of the ramp. Visible in shots/safari-mobile-light/gradient.png (terminal green painted left of the 0% handle centre). Claim at GradientStopEditor.vue:8-13, repeated :211-213, :262-265.
defects.mechanism: The ramp is painted across the whole border box while handle centres ride an inset track, so the hover ghost is drawn at the pointer but filled with colorAt(p_inset) while the ramp beneath shows p_full — Δhue ≈ 2.9° on the shipped seed near the terminals.
defects.reproduction: On /#/gradient read the bar's rect and computed background-* plus both handle centres; compare against the 0%/100% of the painted ramp.
defects.proposedCure: Inset the ramp to the handle track inside the owned paint contract: background-position: var(--rail-inset) 0, 0 0; background-size: calc(100% - 2*var(--rail-inset)) 100%, 16px 16px — with --rail-inset as the single number C13 also names.

defects.defect: Dual write path for the selection plus an unbound public model; and the defineModel stale-read hazard is ARMED (pass-1's mechanism justification was wrong)
defects.evidence: GradientStopEditor.vue:129-130 writes selectedId AND emits 'select'; GradientVisualizer.vue:140,144 wires both; grep for selectedStopId finds only 3 lines and GradientPane.vue never binds it. Mechanism correction from node_modules/@vue/runtime-core/dist/runtime-core.cjs.js:4321-4332 (vue 3.5.35, verified via require('vue/package.json').version): `localValue = value` runs ONLY when the parent has NOT passed v-model.
defects.mechanism: The parent DOES bind v-model:selected-id, so a write to selectedId.value is invisible to a subsequent read until the parent's ref updates, the parent re-renders and the prop reaches the child's watchSyncEffect — exactly the repo-recorded hazard standing law #7 prescribes a local shallowRef for. No current call site reads after write in the same tick (wasSelected at :123 is captured before the write at :129), so the verdict is a checked negative — but by luck of ordering, not by a synchronous model, and selectedId is written from four sites (:129,:152,:160,:178).
defects.reproduction: NONE — latent hazard, plus a source-level dual path. Read the Vue useModel setter and the two parent bindings.
defects.proposedCure: Make selection a plain local ref in the stop editor, delete the 'select' emit and its handler, and delete GradientVisualizer's unbound selectedStopId defineModel. That removes the dual path, the dead public surface, and the armed stale-read in one move.

defects.defect: Hover is modelled as reactive JS state because the inline transform shadows the hover: utility — a reactive tick and re-render per hover, and per-instance style strings
defects.evidence: GradientStopEditor.vue:30-33 and :255-261 document the defect in prose; hoveredId ref at :33, handleScale at :60-63, @pointerenter/@pointerleave on every handle at :269-270, transform+transition re-authored per instance at :262-263.
defects.mechanism: An inline style always outranks a class, so hover:scale-110 was dead and hover was re-implemented in the reactivity system — style authored per instance rather than at the root (edicts 5 and 7).
defects.reproduction: NONE needed — source-visible; the file states it itself.
defects.proposedCure: Pass per-stop DATA as custom properties (--stop-pos, --stop-color) and own the geometry in the scoped sheet: .rail-handle { --handle-scale:1; transform: translate(-50%,-50%) scale(var(--handle-scale)) } with :hover and [data-selected] overrides. Deletes hoveredId, handleScale and two listeners per handle.

defects.defect: No e.button guard: the bar's add gesture is armed by any pointer button, and pendingAdd can survive a context menu to be consumed by a later unrelated pointerup
defects.evidence: Source CONFIRMED: GradientStopEditor.vue:85-89 (and :119) inspect e.target and e.clientX/Y but never e.button/e.buttons; pendingAdd is disarmed only at :101-115 (pointerup/pointerleave). Live: clean-state right-click and middle-click on the bare rail did NOT mint a stop (B1/B2 before==after, 2 handles), but an earlier session where a right-press preceded it DID mint one (2→3 handles, new stop at 63%).
defects.mechanism: pendingAdd is a bare module-level latch with no button predicate and no contextmenu/pointercancel disarm, so its lifetime can straddle gestures.
defects.reproduction: HYPOTHESIS for the observed add — not reproducible on demand. The missing guard itself is source-confirmed at :85-89.
defects.proposedCure: `if (e.button !== 0) return;` at the top of both pointerdown handlers, and disarm pendingAdd on pointercancel and contextmenu — one owner for the latch and no path that leaves it armed across gestures.

defects.defect: Masking fallbacks, a dead inject, a no-op prop default, and a null guard that would silently warp a stop to 0%

result.strongestDefect: C1 — the drag gesture leaves the stop array non-monotonic (updateStop at useGradientModel.ts:127-131 never re-sorts, while addStop at :118 does), so the rail and render tile paint a CSS-clamped lie and the app emits CSS its own parser refuses ("stop positions must be non-decreasing", gradientParse.ts:284-290). result.strongestDefect: L-1 — the stop-ordering invariant has no owner: three write paths into stops[] carry three contradictory policies (addStop sorts, parseGradientCSS rejects, updateStop — the path this component drives — enforces nothing), so the model's own serializer emits CSS that the model's own parser rejects. Proven live, keyboard-only, on the two-stop default gradient.
result.negativeProof: Not applicable to the verdict (DEFECTIVE), but the following were checked and found SOUND, each with measurement: (1) No deep-import defect — all 49 value.js import sites in demo/ go through published subpaths; `npx tsc --noEmit -p tsconfig.demo.json --traceResolution` resolves `@mkbabb/value.js/css` to `/Users/mkbabb/Programming/value.js/dist/subpaths/css.d.ts` via the repo's own package.json#exports, with no node_modules segment — a real external consumer could write every demo import. (3) The visual audit's "20x20 smallTapTargets" rows for the stop handles are a measurement artifact, not a defect: elementFromPoint from the handle centre gives center→HANDLE, +11px→HANDLE, +13px→rail, i.e. a real 24x24 pointer target (WCAG 2.5.8 met) that getBoundingClientRect cannot see. (4) verbatimModuleSyntax satisfied — the sole type import is `import type` at line 4. (5) Vue 3.5 idioms present and correct — useTemplateRef (:28), reactive props destructure (:6), defineModel (:26); no stale-read hazard since :129's write is read back synchronously by handleScale (:60-63). defects.defect: The stop-ordering invariant is homeless: three write paths into stops[] with three contradictory policies. addStop sorts (useGradientModel.ts:118); parseGradientCSS rejects violations (gradientParse.ts:284-290); updateStop — the path this component drives from drag (:94,:145) and keyboard (:179) — enforces nothing (useGradientModel.ts:127-131). The model's serializer therefore emits CSS its own parser calls unmodelable, and intervals[i], defined as the span between stops[i] and stops[i+1], ends up attached to an inverted span.
defects.evidence: Live at http://localhost:9000/#/gradient, fresh mount, keyboard only — 10x shift+ArrowRight on stops[0] then 10x shift+ArrowLeft on stops[1] yields labels ["Gradient stop at 100%","Gradient stop at 0%"] and CSS readout `linear-gradient(90deg, oklch(0.75 0.15 145) 100%, oklch(0.65 0.18 265) 0%)` with errs: []. Feeding that exact string to the app's own parser in-page: `import('/@fs/…/gradientParse.ts').parseGradientCSS(...)` → "REJECT: stop positions must be non-decreasing (hard-stop reordering isn't modeled)"; the ordered control case returns OK. Computed --rail-ramp came out with DECREASING positions (100.00%, 96.88%, …, 3.13%, 0.00%), which CSS Images 3 §3.4.3 colour-stop fixup silently repairs. Coverage: `grep -rn "non-decreasing|monotonic" e2e test` finds the invariant only in the parser and its unit test; e2e/smoke/views/gradient.spec.ts:144 drags but never asserts order.
defects.mechanism: Unique semantic ownership violated — position semantics live in the leaf component (pixels/keys → number), array identity lives in the model, the ordering law lives in the parser. One concept, three homes; the invariant died in the seam. Root structural cause is L-3: hand-rolling a multi-thumb slider instead of consuming one.
defects.reproduction: http://localhost:9000/#/gradient → focus the 0% stop handle → shift+ArrowRight x10 → focus the other handle → shift+ArrowLeft x10 → read the CSS box. Positions descend. Retype that string into the CSS box and the destructive parse verdict appears.
defects.proposedCure: Do NOT add .sort() to updateStop — that makes a fourth policy holder. Transpose the instrument: bind stop positions to a multi-thumb glass-ui Slider (variant="stops"), where the invariant is already solved, shipped and installed one import line away — node_modules/reka-ui/dist/Slider/SliderRoot.js:124 calls getNextSortedValues on every commit, utils.js:8 sorts. Ordering becomes structurally unrepresentable rather than guarded.

defects.defect: parseGradientCSS is documented total ("model-or-reject … never a partial", gradientParse.ts:5-6) and is not: it delegates validity to a non-total library oracle. gradientParse.ts:16-17 explicitly names parseCssColor/parseCssScalar "the validity oracles; the demo never hand-validates a color". parseCssColor throws instead of returning {ok:false} for 8 empty-argument colour functions, so isColorToken (gradientParse.ts:92-94) is a crash site and the throw escapes the whole model-or-reject contract. The /css subpath publishes a ParseResult-typed API — a type-level promise of totality — and breaks it.
defects.evidence: In-page, against the real module: `parseGradientCSS('linear-gradient(90deg, oklch(), red)')` → THROW: TypeError: Cannot read properties of undefined (reading 'replace'); same for rgb() and color-mix(). Library site confirmed by `grep -n "replace(/,/g" src/css/grammar.ts` → line 181: `const components = splitTopLevel(slash[0]!.replace(/,/g, " "), "space");` — a `!` non-null assertion over splitTopLevel("", "/") which returns [].
defects.mechanism: A published boundary whose type says ParseResult<CssColor> and whose runtime says "or I throw". The consumer built its own totality guarantee on a guarantee never given, and no structural check exists that would catch the gap.
defects.reproduction: Type `linear-gradient(90deg, oklch(), red)` into the gradient CSS editor at http://localhost:9000/#/gradient. Chain: GradientCodeEditor.onInput → debouncedParse (GradientCodeEditor.vue:55) → emit("parse") → GradientVisualizer.onParseCSS (:102) → applyCSS → parseGradientCSS. The parseVerdict UI that e2e/smoke/views/gradient.spec.ts:222 certifies ("garbage input fails LOUD") never runs — these 8 inputs fail silently and wrongly.
defects.proposedCure: Totality is the library's contract and belongs in the library: parseFunctionalColor must return failure(source) on an empty body, plus a property test over {fn} × {"", " ", "/", ",,"} so the surface cannot regress to partiality. Explicitly do NOT wrap isColorToken in a try/catch — that is a masking fallback (edict 2) and moves the library's contract into its consumer.

defects.defect: CORRECTION TO THE PRIOR SEAT'S REPORT: challenge-L-library.md:434-449 (finding L-8(b), "two value.js's in one build — the demo type-resolves against the installed package while it runtime-resolves against the working tree") is a FALSE POSITIVE and must not survive into the tranche. Both types and runtime resolve to the repo's own dist/. The prior seat misread TypeScript's packageId label as a node_modules provenance marker; it is the package identity (name/path@version) of whichever package owns the file, and the repo's own package.json declares @mkbabb/value.js@4.0.0.
defects.evidence: `npx tsc --noEmit -p tsconfig.demo.json --traceResolution | grep -A3 value.js/css` → "Found 'package.json' at '/Users/mkbabb/Programming/value.js/package.json'" … "successfully resolved to '/Users/mkbabb/Programming/value.js/dist/subpaths/css.d.ts' with Package ID '@mkbabb/value.js/dist/subpaths/css.d.ts@4.0.0'" — no node_modules segment anywhere. `npx tsc -p tsconfig.demo.json --noEmit --explainFiles | grep -A3 subpaths/css` prints the repo-relative path `dist/subpaths/css.d.ts` (not node_modules/@mkbabb/value.js/dist/...) for all 11 import sites. The installed copy is a transitive artifact: node_modules/@mkbabb/keyframes.js@6.0.0 declares "@mkbabb/value.js": "4.0.0" as a hard dependency; nothing in the demo graph consults it. The prior seat's `cmp` DIFFERENT result is true (6dfbff9f vs 0cd5611e) but irrelevant.
defects.mechanism: Misattributed causation in a peer audit artifact. The prior report uses L-8(b) as the causal explanation for L-2 ("exactly the crack through which §L-2 shipped"). It is not the crack — L-2 ships through the `!` at src/css/grammar.ts:181, in the working tree, in the published 4.0.0, in every build.
defects.reproduction: Run the two tsc commands above at HEAD c654824e and read the resolved paths.
defects.proposedCure: Withdraw L-8(b). Keep L-8(a) (three dead paths entries) and enlarge it: delete the tsconfig.demo.json paths block for @mkbabb/value.js entirely rather than repairing it — the two subpaths with NO paths entry (/css, /value) already resolve correctly via package.json#exports, which is exactly what a real external consumer does, and vite.config.ts:38-47 already generates the runtime aliases from the same map. No workspace link is needed; adopting the prior cure would do work that fixes nothing.

defects.defect: Wrong owner for the whole instrument: a bespoke multi-thumb slider (inset-track geometry, pointer capture, drag lifecycle, keyboard model, hit-target inflation, dual-contrast focus-ring composition, pill silhouette, owned paint stack) is hand-rolled in demo/workbenches, while glass-ui already publishes the primitive and the component's own parent already imports it.
defects.evidence: GradientStopEditor.vue:53-81 (HANDLE_HALF/handleLeft/getPosition), :119-156 (pointer capture + drag), :173-187 (keyboard), :338-359 (focus ring), :374-391 (hit inflation), :317-326 (paint stack). Against: node_modules/@mkbabb/glass-ui/dist/components/slider/types.d.ts declares `modelValue?: number[] | null` and `minStepsBetweenThumbs?: number` (already N-thumb) and `variant?: SliderVariant`. demo/ui/slider/index.ts is the entire file: `export { Slider } from "@mkbabb/glass-ui";` and GradientVisualizer.vue:10 already imports it — 126 lines above the rail that does not use it. The file's own comments concede the point: :198 "the glass-ui slider-track rounding register (T-46)", :316 "--radius-pill".
defects.mechanism: Design-system ownership inversion (edict 4). The component imitates the design system instead of being it, which is why every recipe (focus ring, hit inflation, paint stack, ordering) had to be re-derived locally and each was fixed by a separate ruling (U-F25, U-F27, T.W6-2) instead of once at the root.
defects.reproduction: Structural — read the cited lines against the glass-ui and reka type declarations.
defects.proposedCure: Land `variant="stops"` on the existing glass-ui Slider (edict 4: reuse the existing component-type name; relay to the glass-ui BH inbox per the standing formation invariant), with slots #thumb (per-stop colour fill) and #ghost (add preview) and events add(position)/remove(index). GradientStopEditor.vue then collapses to ~40 lines with no HANDLE_HALF, no getBoundingClientRect, no setPointerCapture, no keydown handler, no scoped focus-ring or hit-inflation CSS, no .gradient-rail paint stack — and L-1, L-6(min-2-stops), L-7 and the paint-stack duplication die with it.

defects.defect: Dead re-export barrels kept explicitly as back-compat shims (edict 2: no aliases, no migration shims, no dual paths). useGradientModel.ts:19-29 is headed "── Re-exports (preserve public API surface) ──"; useGradientInterpolation.ts:13-17 says the re-export exists "so the gradient tree's own consumers … keep their import path".
defects.evidence: I enumerated every consumer of all seven re-exported names across demo/, test/, e2e/. serializeRailRamp, GradientParseResult and ParsedGradientModel have ZERO consumers through any door. serializeGradient, serializeCoalescedGradient, linearInterval and parseGradientCSS are imported from their real homes directly (test/gradient-parse.test.ts:10,11; test/gradient-v4-consume.test.ts:5,7). The ONLY live pass-through is INTERPOLATION_SPACES/HUE_INTERPOLATION_METHODS at GradientVisualizer.vue:19-20 — and those travel two stacked re-exports from demo/color-session/color-space-meta.ts, while the sibling workbench MixConfigBar.vue:18 imports the same two constants from the real home in one hop.

defects.reproduction: grep -rn over demo/ test/ e2e/ for each of the seven names, excluding the four gradient composables themselves.
defects.proposedCure: Delete both re-export blocks; point GradientVisualizer.vue:19-20 at ../../../color-session/color-space-meta, matching MixConfigBar.vue:18. Strictly smaller graph, zero behaviour delta, one line changed.

defects.defect: Selection state is transported twice on one gesture — a dual path in the component's own public contract. The component writes v-model AND emits an event carrying the identical fact in the same tick, and the parent consumes both.
defects.evidence: GradientStopEditor.vue:129-130 — `selectedId.value = id;` immediately followed by `emit("select", id);`. GradientVisualizer.vue:140 `v-model:selected-id="selectedStopId"` AND :144 `@select="(id) => selectedStopId = id"` — the same ref written twice. The two channels are already not equivalent: removeStop (:158-162) and onHandlePointerUp (:148-156) write selectedId with no matching select emit.
defects.mechanism: Redundant notification channel for one piece of state; the channels have already begun to diverge, which is how dual paths rot.
defects.reproduction: Structural — read GradientStopEditor.vue:129-130 against GradientVisualizer.vue:140,144.
defects.proposedCure: Delete the `select` emit (:22, :130) and the @select handler (GradientVisualizer.vue:144). v-model:selectedId is the whole contract.

defects.defect: demo/ui/ is a 19-module, content-free alias barrel over glass-ui — edict 2 (no aliases) and edict 4 (variants/primitives belong in glass-ui, not demo/ui/). The component's parent then imports the design system through three different doors in one file.
defects.evidence: Every directory under demo/ui/ is a single index.ts; 18 of 19 are one line. demo/ui/slider/index.ts is the entire file: `export { Slider } from "@mkbabb/glass-ui";`. GradientVisualizer.vue:9 imports Select via the shim, :10 imports Slider via the shim, :12 imports writeClipboard from the package root, :13 imports DockControl from the @mkbabb/glass-ui/dock subpath. Related: GradientVisualizer.vue:12 uses writeClipboard while its sibling GradientEasingEditor.vue:29 uses useClipboard — two clipboard idioms in one feature.

defects.reproduction: ls demo/ui/*/index.ts; cat demo/ui/slider/index.ts.
defects.proposedCure: Delete demo/ui/. Import @mkbabb/glass-ui/<subpath> everywhere — glass-ui 7.0.0 publishes 60+ subpaths including ./select, ./slider, ./button, so the tree-shakeable door already exists. Settle on one clipboard idiom.

defects.defect: Direction of dependency inverted: the leaf presentational component imports the orchestrating composable to obtain a pure data type. GradientStop is {id, cssColor, position} — three fields, no reactivity, no behaviour — declared inside the module that also constructs Vue refs, owns every mutation, and re-exports the serializers and the parser.
defects.evidence: GradientStopEditor.vue:4 `import type { GradientStop } from "../composables/useGradientModel";`. The type is declared at useGradientModel.ts:33-37, in a module that imports @mkbabb/value.js/color, @mkbabb/glass-ui/easing, ../../../color-session/picker-color and three sibling composables. useGradientModel has 5 importers, all of which are dragged onto its type graph.
defects.mechanism: Types owned by the state factory rather than by a leaf, so every presentational component hangs off the orchestrator. Runtime-erased under verbatimModuleSyntax, but the declaration graph is what the module lattice is made of.
defects.reproduction: Structural — read GradientStopEditor.vue:4 and useGradientModel.ts:33-62.
defects.proposedCure: A leaf model/types.ts with zero intra-tree imports (only @mkbabb/value.js/color and @mkbabb/glass-ui/easing types). Everything depends on the leaf; nothing depends on the factory except the Vue layer. Disappears entirely once L-3 lands.

defects.defect: tsconfig.demo.json's hand-written paths block has drifted from the generated package.json#exports map: three dead mappings, two of them pointing at files that do not exist, plus a self-description that contradicts the map it claims to mirror.

defects.defect: The "minimum 2 stops" policy is implemented twice, in the component and in the model.

defects.defect: The rail's "owned paint stack" — self-described in-file as "a MATERIAL CONTRACT, not a shorthand assembly" — is copy-pasted four times rather than owned once, against edict 5 (style at the root component level).

result.axis: CHALLENGE-D — design (pass 3) · demo/workbenches/generate/GenerateControls.vue

result.strongestDefect: D3-1 — The preview that justifies the entire instrument is painted on a veil that amplifies and transmits the specimen it is drawn over. Every seed-exact preview chip is therefore composited over an arbitrary band of the live palette, with that band's chroma boosted 60% by the veil's own saturate. The component's stated thesis (:87-93, "a preview that lies is worse than none") is defeated by the material it renders on. Pass 2 declared this same mechanism "the best-designed thing in the file" — while never once rendering the open dropdown; frames-D3/desktop-preset-open.png and mobile-harmony-open-count12.png are the first frames of that state in any pass.
