result.axis: CHALLENGE-C — implementation audit of demo/workbenches/generate/GenerateControls.vue (r3 pass)
result.modelObserved: Opus 5 (1M context) — exact model id `claude-opus-5[1m]`. Declared seat and served tier agree; not inherited, not undeclared.
result.strongestDefect: C-1 — the per-swatch copy verb does not exist. `WatercolorDot` at glass-ui 7.0.0 sets `defineOptions({ inheritAttrs: false })` (glass-ui src WatercolorDot.vue:6), hard-codes `aria-hidden="true"` (:99) and inline `pointerEvents: 'none'` (:115) on its root, and declares no emits. So `tag="button"`, `:aria-label="Copy ${css}"` and `@click="copyColor(css)"` at GenerateControls.vue:199–208 are all silently discarded — no Vue warning, because `inheritAttrs:false` suppresses the extraneous-attrs warning. Live: the element is a SPAN with `tagAttr null`, `ariaLabel null`, `tabIndex -1`, `pointer-events: none`, `cursor: pointer` (a false affordance); a synthetic MouseEvent dispatched straight at it produces ZERO clipboard writes while the Copy-all button in the same page writes fine. Twelve visible 40px controls that cannot be clicked, focused, or perceived by AT.
result.negativeProof: Measured-sound surfaces, so the DEFECTIVE verdict is not a blanket one: (1) the generation core is pure and its seed-exact law holds at the FUNCTION level — `generatePalette(count,preset,harmony,seed)` builds a fresh `mulberry32(seed)` per call and `presetStops`/`harmonyStops` pass exactly the args selecting the row installs (generate-color.ts:213–233; GenerateControls.vue:94–100). (2) Both domain boundaries are safe, driven live: count=1 → 1 swatch, 1 strip segment, gradient `linear-gradient(to right, oklch(0.666617 0.190188 133.655) 50%)`; count=12 → 12/12. No throw, no NaN, no blank. (3) ZERO rAF exposure — `animate` defaults false so glass-ui's `useRAFLoop` is never entered; `PerformanceObserver({entryTypes:["longtask"]})` over 10 consecutive Regenerate clicks returned `longTasksMs: []`. (4) HYPOTHESIS KILLED BY MEASUREMENT: the `absolute inset-0` gradient overlay does NOT steal the slider's pointer events — `document.elementFromPoint` across the track mid-line returns `SPAN.slider-track` / `SPAN.slider-range`, never the overlay. (5) None of the repo's known local hazards are present: no `defineModel` (so no stale-read), no oklch→HSV roundtrip / `stableHue` dependency, no `ValueUnit` wrapping, no WebGL or any drawing context. (6) `verbatimModuleSyntax` honoured — all three type imports are `import type`; `vue-tsc -p tsconfig.demo.json --noEmit` exits 0. (7) `SelectContent` genuinely unmounts when closed (`[data-stops]` count 0 closed vs 10 open), so the preview generators cost nothing at rest. (8) `pageErrors: []`, no component console errors; the Safari matrix records `pageErr 0 / consoleErr 0` for `/#/generate` on all four captures. (9) REFUTATION of the r2 pass's C-10 hypothesis: `null` cannot reach the `as PresetName` cast, because glass-ui's Select emits `SelectionValue = string | number` (glass-ui/dist/components/_shared/selection.d.ts:2), not reka-ui's nullable `AcceptableValue`.

defects.defect: The per-swatch copy verb is not wired, not focusable, and not hit-testable. Three of four bindings on <WatercolorDot> are silently discarded and the root is pointer-events:none + aria-hidden.
defects.evidence: demo/workbenches/generate/GenerateControls.vue:199-208 (tag="button", :aria-label, @click). /Users/mkbabb/Programming/glass-ui/src/components/watercolor-dot/WatercolorDot.vue:6 `defineOptions({ inheritAttrs: false })`, :99 `aria-hidden="true"`, :115 `pointerEvents: 'none'`. dts declares 6 props, no emits. LIVE probe §1: {"tagName":"SPAN","tagAttr":null,"ariaHidden":"true","ariaLabel":null,"tabIndex":-1,"pointerEvents":"none","cursor":"pointer"}. §2b synthetic click → writes []. §2c Playwright click → "TimeoutError: locator.click: Timeout 4000ms exceeded". §2d control (Copy-all button) → 1 writeText.
defects.mechanism: inheritAttrs:false on a library primitive silently swallows consumer listeners/aria/tag; the primitive additionally forces aria-hidden and pointer-events:none on its only root. Vue emits no warning precisely because inheritAttrs is false. Family: DEAD-CONTROL-BY-SILENT-PROP-DISCARD.
defects.reproduction: npx vite --port 9000; node docs/tranches/V/megatranche/audit/components/wb-generate-controls/probe-C-impl-r3.mjs → blocks 1-swatches, 2b, 2c, 2d. By hand: open http://localhost:9000/#/generate, click any swatch, paste — clipboard unchanged.
defects.proposedCure: BLOCKED-ON-GLASS-V8 (wave W-1). Architectural, not a patch: glass-ui 8 gives WatercolorDot an interactive register — a tag/as prop PLUS attrs+listener forwarding, with aria-hidden and pointer-events:none moved onto the decorative blob layer instead of the component root. The consumer then mounts the dot as the FACE of a real <button>. Relay R-1 to the glass-ui BH inbox. Gate: new e2e — click swatch n ⇒ writeText receives palette[n]; Tab reaches each swatch and Enter copies.

defects.defect: The editable plate name is discarded on save; every saved palette is named "Generated Palette".

LIVE probe §3: {"swatchCount":5,"swatchesReachableByAT":0,"liveRegionsInDocument":0,"liveRegionsInPlate":0,"plateAccessibleText":"5 Regenerate seed: 83d35f90","focusablesInPlate":["INPUT:Palette name","BUTTON:Regenerate","BUTTON:Save palette","BUTTON:Copy all colors"]}. grep -rn 'aria-live|role="status"' demo/workbenches/generate/ → NONE.

Safari matrix REPORT.json, /#/generate, all four captures: safari-desktop-light/dark {"w":12,"h":24,"tag":"span","label":"Color count"}; safari-mobile-light/dark {"w":12,"h":44,...}. defects.defect: The component's only automated oracle cannot pass by construction, CI never runs it, and every gate that does run is green over every defect here.
defects.evidence: e2e/smoke/oracles/o20-generate-plate.spec.ts:96-107 asserts expect(live).toEqual(stamped) where live=getComputedStyle().backgroundColor and stamped=data-stops (the library's raw strings). Both sides measured in one page state (probe-C-menu-r3.mjs §3): stamped_first "oklch(55.373499433044% 0.134321687222 305.139642180875deg)" vs live_first "oklch(0.553735 0.134322 305.14)", equal:false — numerically identical, textually never equal. Run at HEAD: `npx playwright test e2e/smoke/oracles/o20-generate-plate.spec.ts --project=smoke` → 2 failed. CI: `grep -n "run:" .github/workflows/ci.yml` = npm ci / lint / vue-tsc lib / vue-tsc demo / build / npm test / verify-packed-surface; `grep -n "playwright|e2e" .github/workflows/*.yml` → no output. Executed: VUE_TSC_EXIT=0, ESLINT_EXIT=0. No vitest file references the component, useColorGeneration, or generatePalette.
defects.mechanism: A serialization-form assertion masquerading as a byte-identity law: the spec's own comment says 'the same rgb() strings', so it was written when serializeCssColor emitted rgb(); the serialization moved to oklch(%/deg) and the oracle did not. Family: VACUOUS-GATE + STALE-ORACLE.
defects.reproduction: THE VACUOUS-GATE MUTATION: delete GenerateControls.vue:199-209 (the whole swatch grid + copyColor + its import). lint green, both vue-tsc green, npm test green (no vitest file touches it), build green, visual namelessButtons/smallTapTargets unchanged. Only o20 would notice, and o20 is red before it gets there and is not run in CI.
defects.proposedCure: Wave W-5 (not blocked, e2e/ is not pinned): rewrite o20 test 2 to compare PARSED colours — parseCssColor both sides, per-channel equality within 1e-9 — and add the count-12 leg that exposes C-13. Wave W-6: add the `smoke` playwright project to .github/workflows/ci.yml so W-5 is load-bearing.

defects.defect: The preset/harmony preview strips LIE at count 8-12: 12 stops are stamped on data-stops while only 7 segments are painted.
defects.evidence: GenerateControls.vue:86-96 asserts 'each option row previews the EXACT palette selecting it yields… A preview that lies is worse than none.' PreviewStrip.vue:25 STRIP_SEGMENT_CAP = 7, with a mask fade on the last segment. LIVE at count 12, harmony menu open (probe-C-menu-r3.mjs §5): {"count":"12","options":6,"stopsPerChip":[12,12,12,12,12,12],"segmentsPerChip":[7,7,7,7,7,7]}. At count 5 the two agree (§2: 5 and 5) — which is why no oracle written at the default can see it.
defects.mechanism: A library-level segment cap (7) collides with a consumer-level domain (1..12) that nobody reconciled; the stamped contract surface and the painted surface diverge above the cap. Family: PREVIEW-TRUNCATION-BREAKS-TRUTH-LAW. It also splits the O-14 chain sample.ts:15-20 documents ('the painted gradient must embed exactly those stops in the live DOM').
defects.reproduction: node docs/tranches/V/megatranche/audit/components/wb-generate-controls/probe-C-menu-r3.mjs → block 5-harmony@count12. By hand: /#/generate → focus the count slider → ArrowRight to 12 → open Harmony → each row shows 7 of 12 colours, 42% missing.
defects.proposedCure: Wave W-7 (not blocked, PreviewStrip.vue is not pinned): reconcile the two domains at the root — either lift PreviewStrip's cap to 12 (the strip is 2.618rem wide; 12 segments is ~3.5px each, still legible as a ramp) or narrow the count slider's max to the cap. Gate: stopsPerChip === segmentsPerChip at every reachable count.

defects.defect: Generated colours carry 12-15 significant decimals into the clipboard, into localStorage, and onward to the API.
defects.evidence: demo/color-session/generate-color.ts:235-243 `generatedCss` serializes with no rounding. Clipboard, intercepted writeText from the plate's Copy-all button (probe §2d): "oklch(57.075309213251% 0.165883022438 44.052828429267deg), oklch(71.53…" (~293 chars for five colours). localStorage after Save (probe-C-save-r3.mjs §2): "colors":[{"css":"oklch(79.838149605785% 0.170167350601 150.3761107…". The browser's own serialization of the identical colour is oklch(0.570753 0.165883 44.0528) — six figures.
defects.mechanism: No display-precision rounding at the serialization boundary of a generator whose output is a user-facing payload (copy) and a persisted record (save → createPalette → API). Family: UNROUNDED-FLOAT-ESCAPES-TO-PRODUCT.
defects.reproduction: node probe-C-impl-r3.mjs → 2d-after-copy-all; node probe-C-save-r3.mjs → 2-storage-after-save.
defects.proposedCure: Wave W-3 (not blocked — the fix lives one layer down in the shared color layer, not in the pinned file): round in generatedCss to display precision (4 dp on L%, 4 on C, 2 on H). Gate: vitest — every generatePalette string matches /^oklch\(\d+\.\d{1,4}% \d\.\d{1,4} \d+(\.\d{1,2})?deg\)$/ and a round-trip parse stays within 1/255 per sRGB channel.

defects.defect: Both clipboard call sites discard the discriminated {ok, reason} result the producer deliberately designed to be read; there is no success or failure feedback of any kind.
defects.evidence: GenerateControls.vue:106-113 `await writeClipboard(...)` with the result dropped at both sites. glass-ui useClipboard.d.ts:31-37: 'Returns the discriminated result ({ ok } / { ok, reason }) rather than a lossy boolean, for identical call ergonomics: const { ok } = await writeClipboard(text)'. CopyFailureReason = 'clipboard-api' | 'no-api'. No toast (vue-sonner removed repo-wide), no aria-live (C-3), no icon state. `git show f2c8f565 -- .../GenerateControls.vue`: the ONLY change to this file in the whole Glass 5→7 adoption was copyToClipboard → writeClipboard — name swapped, result still discarded.
defects.mechanism: An explicitly widened error channel discarded at the consumer in the same commit that adopted it. Family: IGNORED-ERROR-CHANNEL.
defects.reproduction: NONE for a user-visible failure on this machine (the happy path works — probe §2d). The discard itself is a code fact at GenerateControls.vue:106-113; the failure modes (non-secure origin, denied permission, unfocused document) are the producer's documented reasons.
defects.proposedCure: BLOCKED-ON-GLASS-V8 (pinned file). Use glass-ui's own useClipboard({resetMs}) — the reactive form whose `status` ref exists precisely for the confirmation UI this plate lacks — and route failure into the W-8 aria-live region. Idiomatic, no new wrapper, no new shared/ dir.

defects.defect: The plate chrome row wraps at the default desktop width — and it is a sub-pixel tie, not the 390-only behaviour the source comment documents.
defects.evidence: GenerateControls.vue:139-142 claims 'at 390 the verbs settle onto their own right-aligned line'. Measured with offsetTop+height/2 centres (probe §5): 1440 → 65.5 vs 107 (wrapped); 1280 → 65.5 vs 107 (wrapped); 768 → 70.5 vs 70 (one line); 390 → 65.5 vs 107 (wrapped). Independently visible in Safari: audit/visual/shots/safari-desktop-light/generate.png shows the verb cluster dropped below the title. Parts (probe-C-menu-r3.mjs §1 + probe §5): 430 → content 338 vs demand 425; 1440 → content 438 vs demand 438; 768 → content 438 vs demand 429.
defects.mechanism: flex-wrap line-breaking on flex-basis: input basis 10rem + badge + a verb cluster whose width steps up 9px at the desktop type scale, landing demand exactly at the available width and losing on the sub-pixel residue. Family: SUB-PIXEL-LAYOUT-TIE.
defects.reproduction: node probe-C-impl-r3.mjs → 5-geometry@1440 / @1280 / @768 / @390; compare offsetTop+h/2 of the name input vs the Regenerate button.
defects.proposedCure: BLOCKED-ON-GLASS-V8 (pinned file). Root-level, not a magic-number nudge: give the row a stated minimum — either reduce the input's flex-basis below the cluster's true demand, or let the verb cluster wrap as a unit only under a container query at a named breakpoint, so the composition's line count is a declared design decision rather than a sub-pixel accident. Correct the comment to match whatever is chosen.

defects.defect: The Select handlers' parameter type is imported from reka-ui, a seam glass-ui 7 no longer exposes — a stale pre-Glass-7 type shim that also over-widens the contract.
defects.evidence: GenerateControls.vue:33 `import type { AcceptableValue } from "reka-ui";`, :75-81 `function onPresetChange(value: AcceptableValue) { preset.value = value as PresetName; }`. glass-ui/dist/components/select/Select.vue.d.ts: `SelectEmits { "update:modelValue": [value: SelectionValue] }`; glass-ui/dist/components/_shared/selection.d.ts:2 `export type SelectionValue = string | number;`. reka-ui/dist/index3.d.ts:231 `type AcceptableValue = string | number | bigint | Record<string, any> | null;` — strictly wider, which is why vue-tsc stays green.
defects.mechanism: The demo reaches past its declared design system into that system's transitive dependency for a type the system exports itself. Edict 2 (no legacy/dual paths) + edict 4 (glass-ui is the design system). Family: STALE-BOUNDARY-TYPE-IMPORT. Load-bearing: it is also what made r2's C-10 null-crash hypothesis look plausible.
defects.reproduction: grep -rn 'from "reka-ui"' demo/workbenches/generate/GenerateControls.vue → line 33; cat node_modules/@mkbabb/glass-ui/dist/components/_shared/selection.d.ts.
defects.proposedCure: BLOCKED-ON-GLASS-V8 (wave W-9, pinned file): import SelectionValue from glass-ui and narrow by membership (PRESET_NAMES.includes / HARMONY_NAMES.includes) instead of casting — glass-ui even ships isSelectionValue() for the runtime half. Subsumes and closes r2's C-10. Gate: grep 'from "reka-ui"' in demo/workbenches/generate/ → 0.

defects.defect: A single aria-label lands on two nested elements: the role-less glass-slider root and the role=slider thumb.
defects.evidence: GenerateControls.vue:298 `aria-label="Color count"` on <Slider>. Playwright strict-mode violation is the direct evidence: locator("span[aria-label='Color count']") resolved to 2 elements — 1) <span data-slot="slider" ... aria-label="Color count" class="glass-slider relative w-full"> and 2) <span tabindex="0" role="slider" aria-valuemin="1" aria-valuenow="5" aria-valuemax="12" aria-label="Color count" class="slider-thumb …">.
defects.mechanism: glass-ui's Slider both lets aria-label fall through to its root and binds it explicitly on the thumb; the root has no role, so it is role=generic, on which ARIA 1.2 prohibits aria-label. Family: DUPLICATE-ACCESSIBLE-NAME.
defects.reproduction: node -e with playwright: page.locator("span[aria-label='Color count']") on http://localhost:9000/#/generate throws the strict-mode violation quoted above.
defects.proposedCure: Producer-owned — relay R-2 to the glass-ui BH inbox alongside the tap-target item: Slider should emit aria-label on the role=slider thumb only. No consumer edit (the pin forbids it, and a per-instance override would violate edict 5).

defects.defect: GeneratePane boundary defects: a dead injection, a non-3.5 template ref, a doubly-dead `save` export, and optional-call shims.
defects.evidence: demo/workbenches/generate/GeneratePane.vue:10 `const cssColorOpaque = inject(CSS_COLOR_KEY)!;` — never referenced in the file, and non-null-asserted. :12 `const controlsRef = ref<InstanceType<typeof GenerateControls> | null>(null)` where useTemplateRef is the Vue 3.5 form (edict 7). :22-26 exposes save/regenerate/copyColors; demo/shell/usePaneRouter.ts:196,198 wires only regenerate and copy — `grep -rn "copyColors" demo/ | grep -v workbenches/generate` returns exactly one line and there is no .save() caller, so GenerateControls.save → GeneratePane.save is a dead two-level path. :23-25 `controlsRef.value?.regenerate?.()` optional-chains a defineExpose'd member.
defects.mechanism: Accumulated boundary drift at the component's only consumer; the `?.()` shim is a masking fallback (edict 2) that turns a rename into a silent no-op instead of a throw. Family: CONSUMER-BOUNDARY-ROT.
defects.reproduction: grep -n 'cssColorOpaque' demo/workbenches/generate/GeneratePane.vue → one declaration, zero uses. grep -rn 'copyColors' demo/ | grep -v workbenches/generate → 1 line (usePaneRouter.ts:198).
defects.proposedCure: Wave W-10 (not blocked — GeneratePane.vue is not pinned): delete the CSS_COLOR_KEY injection, switch to useTemplateRef, delete the dead save expose at both levels, and drop the `?.()` from the exposed-method calls in usePaneRouter so a rename fails loudly.

defects.defect: WatercolorDot reads its `seed` prop once at setup, so the consumer's colour-derived `:seed="gen-${css}-${i}"` only ever applies its mount-time value — the 'seeded stable per (color,i)' claim decays after the first regenerate.
defects.evidence: GenerateControls.vue:196 comment 'seeded stable per (color,i)'; :204 :seed binding. node_modules/@mkbabb/glass-ui/dist/watercolor-dot.js: useWatercolorBlob destructures `{ …, seed: c = "" }` once from the options object, and its colour watcher recomputes `hashString(newColor + c)` using that closed-over mount-time `c`; only the feTurbulence seed is a computed on (color + seed). The two halves of one dot therefore disagree about their seed after a regenerate.
defects.mechanism: A by-value option passed to a composable that treats it as static, while the consumer passes a value it expects to be reactive. Family: NON-REACTIVE-OPTION-READ-ONCE.
defects.reproduction: NONE — I did not capture a before/after silhouette diff, and the dots are unreachable for interaction anyway (C-1). Labelled a hypothesis on the observable effect; the code path itself is quoted above and is not in doubt.
defects.proposedCure: Consumer side (BLOCKED-ON-GLASS-V8): pass a stable `gen-${i}` seed, since a colour-derived seed is a category error against that contract and buys nothing. Producer side (relay, optional): make useWatercolorBlob take seed as a getter/ref so the silhouette and the wet edge stay in agreement.

result.axis: CHALLENGE-D — design (visual truth, state coverage, motion, design-system boundary, proportion/seat law) of `demo/workbenches/gradient/GradientVisualizer/GradientStopEditor.vue`
result.modelObserved: Opus 5 — exact model id `claude-opus-5[1m]` (1M context). Explicitly declared at spawn, not inherited.
result.strongestDefect: D2-01 — typing `linear-gradient(90deg, oklch() 0%, red 100%)` into the route's own CSS field annihilates the entire application (stop bar gone, render tile gone, dock gone, body text 649→142 chars, one unlabelled "Try again" pill) with ZERO pageError and ZERO console error. Root cause is MT-F001 (`src/css/grammar.ts:181` asserts `slash[0]!` on an empty body) consumed as a total predicate at `gradientParse.ts:93`; the design defect belonging to this seat is that the instrument has no error state and no independent survival — the workbench's entire error grammar is one sibling-owned `{ok:false}` verdict line, bypassed by any throw.
result.negativeProof: Not SOUND, but these axes were probed and are provably clean, recorded as §18 of the report so no later seat re-opens them: (1) FOCUS RING — settled computed value on a focused handle is `rgba(0,0,0,0.85) 0 0 0 1px, rgba(255,255,255,0.92) 0 0 0 3px, --shadow-sm`: the dual-contrast recipe works and composes with the material lift (a first read at t≈6ms showed 0.0117px — that was the 200ms transition mid-flight; re-measured before publishing). (2) REDUCED MOTION — under `reducedMotion:"reduce"` the computed transition-property is `opacity, color, background-color, border-color, box-shadow`: `transform` is absent, i.e. the global guard at `demo/styles/animations.css:184-192` neutralises the inline spring; no spatial motion. (3) MOTION TOKENISATION — `:263` uses `var(--duration-fast) var(--ease-standard)` + `var(--spring-snappy-duration) var(--spring-snappy)`; animated properties are transform/box-shadow (composited), never a layout property; no keyframes deleted. (4) RTL — `shots/rtl-desktop/gradient.png` shows the rail unmirrored with handles on the physical ends, exactly as `VISUAL-CONSTITUTION.md:127` requires. (5) HIT-INFLATION BLEED on fine pointers — `elementFromPoint` at handle-centre +0,-14 returns `div.gradient-rail` and at +0,-21 returns the outer flex: the 24px pseudo steals nothing from neighbouring content. (6) VUE 3.5 / verbatimModuleSyntax — `useTemplateRef` (:28), reactive props destructure (:6), `import type` (:4); no stale defineModel read-after-write (`wasSelected` is captured before the write). (7) `overflowX: 0` on `/#/gradient` in all four shipped Safari matrices.

defects.defect: Eight characters typed into the route's own CSS field destroy the whole application, silently: the stop editor, render tile and dock are unmounted and replaced by a bare 'Try again' pill with no diagnosis. The component has no error state and no independent survival; the workbench's only error affordance is a sibling-owned one-line `{ok:false}` verdict that a throw bypasses entirely.
defects.evidence: `node evidence/WBGSE-D-probe7.mjs` → `== p7-oklch-empty ==  before: {"stops":2,"bar":true,"bodyLen":649}  after: {"stops":0,"bar":false,"tile":false,"verdict":null,"editorText":"","bodyLen":142}  errs: []`. Same for `rgb()`. Control: `notacolor` → `verdict:"unparseable color \"notacolor\""`, model unchanged. Screenshot `evidence/D-01-route-annihilated.png`. Root cause src/css/grammar.ts:181 (`slash[0]!` on an empty body); consumed as a total predicate at demo/workbenches/gradient/composables/gradientParse.ts:93; atomic contract claimed at useGradientModel.ts:152-156. Telemetry blindness: docs/tranches/V/megatranche/audit/visual/REPORT.md:140 records /#/gradient pageErr 0 consoleErr 0.
defects.mechanism: a throwing dependency consumed as a total function, behind an error grammar that models only the {ok:false} arm, in a component with no failure face
defects.reproduction: Live at http://localhost:9000/#/gradient: click the CSS block, select all, type `linear-gradient(90deg, oklch() 0%, red 100%)`, wait 500ms. Or `node docs/tranches/V/megatranche/audit/components/wb-gradient-stopeditor/evidence/WBGSE-D-probe7.mjs`.
defects.proposedCure: Make the parse boundary total at the one seam that owns it — `applyCSS` is the only place this workbench calls the library parser and it must be result-typed and throw-free — and give the rail a real `model-unavailable` face so a bad parse degrades the instrument, never the shell.

defects.defect: The ramp and the handles ride two different axes, so a handle's own colour is never the colour painted under it (except at 50%). The file's docblock asserts the opposite ('handles, add-ghost and ramp share one axis by construction').
defects.evidence: Pixel table from the committed element screenshot `evidence/D-03-ten-hue-rings.png` (924x82 device = 462x41 CSS): err (CSS px) between a stop's handle centre and the x where the ramp paints that stop's percentage = -10.5, -8.0, -6.0, -3.5, -1.0, +1.0, +3.5, +6.0, +8.0, +10.0 across p=0..100 — exactly linear, zero at 50%. At p=0 the handle fill is (232,49,49) while the ramp directly above it is (235,85,36). Source: `.gradient-rail` background-origin/clip border-box + size 100% 100% (GradientStopEditor.vue:317-326) vs `handleLeft()` inset track calc(10px + (100% - 20px)*p/100) (:55-57). Mobile railW measured 324 → the same 10.5px = 3.24%.
defects.mechanism: one domain quantity expressed in two coordinate systems, with a comment asserting they are one
defects.reproduction: `node .../evidence/WBGSE-D-probe4.mjs` (writes D-03-ten-hue-rings.png), then sample the PNG: pixel at each handle centre y=41 (fill) vs y=10 (ramp at the same x).
defects.proposedCure: Express the axis once: inset the ramp to the handle track (`background-position: 10px 0; background-size: calc(100% - 20px) 100%`) so the pill caps hold flat terminal colour — which is what a 0%/100% stop means — and derive the half-handle from the rendered box instead of re-declaring it in JS.

defects.defect: The drag gesture has no ordering law. Dragging a stop across a neighbour leaves the model non-monotonic; the serializer emits a descending stop list, CSS clamps it, and the rail, the render tile and the copied CSS all disagree with the handles.
defects.evidence: `node evidence/WBGSE-D-probe2.mjs` → `== 2 after drag-past == ["…at 84%","…at 50%","…at 100%"]` and `css: linear-gradient(90deg, oklch(0.75 0.15 145) 83.8%, oklch(70% 0.165 205deg) 50%, oklch(0.65 0.18 265) 100%)`; DOM left offsets `["calc(83.8% - 6.76px)","calc(50% + 0px)","calc(100% - 10px)"]`. Screenshot `evidence/D-02-unsorted-drag.png`: 84% of the rail is flat green with a hard cut, a cyan handle sits on solid green. Cause: useGradientModel.ts:118 `addStop` sorts; :127-131 `updateStop` does not. Canon: OPTICAL-BENCH-COMPOSITIONS.md:44 names 'order' as a W27 close criterion.
defects.mechanism: an aggregate invariant enforced on one write path only, with the gesture owner disclaiming it
defects.reproduction: Live: click mid-rail to add a stop, then drag the left handle past it; read the CSS block. Or `node .../evidence/WBGSE-D-probe2.mjs` block 2.
defects.proposedCure: Ordering belongs to the collection, not the call site: every `stops` mutation returns a normalised sorted list with recomputed ordinals and re-derived `intervals`, and the editor preserves handle identity across a crossing so the grabbed handle stays grabbed (also the precondition for §5.2's 'position of total' reorder announcement).

defects.defect: The stop swatch paints the ramp colour it sits on, so the fill can never contrast with its ground; the only boundary is a hardcoded 2px white ring at 80% alpha, in both schemes. Measured contrast reaches 1.00:1 — the control is literally invisible on a light ramp — and 6 of 10 rainbow hues fall below the 3:1 non-text floor.
defects.evidence: WCAG contrast computed from committed pixel buffers: `#ffffff → #fafafa` ramp gives ring:fill 1.00:1 and 1.03:1 (`evidence/D-03-white-ramp-handles.png` — the handles are gone, only the --shadow-sm smudge remains). Ten-hue ramp ring:fill = 3.19, 1.93, 1.31, 1.44, 1.44, 1.37, 3.22, 5.07, 3.22, 2.96. Computed border colour `oklab(0.999994 … / 0.8)` (probe 1). Source :235 `border-2 border-white/80`, :247 fill. The file already owns the cure for focus only (:342-349, measured `rgba(0,0,0,0.85) 0 0 0 1px, rgba(255,255,255,0.92) 0 0 0 3px`).
defects.mechanism: a specimen whose fill is definitionally equal to its ground, defended by a single one-sided hairline with no scheme arm
defects.reproduction: `node .../evidence/WBGSE-D-probe4.mjs`; or live: paste `linear-gradient(90deg, #ffffff 0%, #fafafa 100%)` into the CSS block and look at the rail.
defects.proposedCure: Apply the dual-contrast recipe the focus ring already proves to the resting/selected boundary — or, per OPTICAL-BENCH-COMPOSITIONS.md:44, make the dot a WatercolorDot face inside a named geometric seat and let the seat carry a scheme-aware boundary.

defects.defect: On coarse pointers the selected handle's 44px hit zone and the remove chip's 44px hit zone overlap by 8px inside the rail, and the chip wins. A touch aimed at the selected handle but landing ~16px low destroys the stop.
defects.evidence: Measured (probe 2 block 3): rail bottom 240.7, handle centre 220.7, chip box y 244.7..268.7 (centre 256.7); coarse pseudo measured `beforeSize: "44pxx44px"` (probe 2 block 4). Handle zone 198.7..242.7, chip zone 234.7..278.7 → overlap 234.7..242.7. `chipHitAtHrY: "Remove selected stop"` shows the chip already winning hit-tests outside its visual box. Source :385-391 (--touch-target on both), :288 (chip at top-11, z-20, later in DOM).
defects.mechanism: two invisible 44px targets stacked 36px apart on a 40px rail, inflated per element with no arbitration
defects.reproduction: iPhone-14 context, select a stop with >=3 stops present, tap ~16px below the handle centre (still on the rail). Geometry printed by `node .../evidence/WBGSE-D-probe2.mjs` block 3.
defects.proposedCure: The destructive action leaves the rail's physical neighbourhood: remove lives in a stop inspector row alongside numeric position and colour, so nothing destructive shares a fingertip with the drag surface.

defects.defect: The keyboard grammar implements a third of the binding row and the handle exposes no accessible state: Home, End, ArrowUp, ArrowDown, Enter and Space are all dead, and a screen reader cannot tell which stop is selected or hear a value change.
defects.evidence: probe `== C keys ==`: `End ["…at 11%"] -> ["…at 11%"]`, `Home` unchanged, `ArrowUp`/`ArrowDown` unchanged, `Enter`/`Space` unchanged with stop count still 2. Probe 5 `== C ==` shows each handle's full attribute set is `["aria-label=Gradient stop at N%"]` — no role, no aria-valuenow/min/max/text, no aria-pressed|current|selected, no ordinal. Binding text VISUAL-CONSTITUTION.md:127 requires Home=0%, End=100%, Up/Down and 'announce stop identity, percentage, ordinal'.
defects.mechanism: a bespoke <button> impersonating a value control
defects.reproduction: Focus a stop handle and press Home, End, Up, Down, Enter, Space — nothing happens. `node .../evidence/WBGSE-D-probe2.mjs`.
defects.proposedCure: Adopt the producer axis composition over BI `Slider` that VISUAL-CONSTITUTION.md:104 already binds Gradient to ('not new slider mechanics'); role, value, Home/End, RTL law and announcement arrive with it and this file stops owning slider physics.

defects.defect: The add gesture is hover-only, unnamed, keyboard-unreachable, and silently starves as the instrument fills: the bar is a bare div with no role/name/tabindex whose click mints a stop, its only affordance is a hover ghost (absent on touch), and each existing stop sterilises 44px of rail against the gesture with no feedback.
defects.evidence: Probe 1: bar `{role: null, tabindex: null, ariaLabel: null, cursor: "copy", tag: "DIV"}`. Probe 2 block 4 (iPhone 14, railW 324): a tap at 40% added a stop; the next tap 6% (~19px) away added nothing — `info` shows 3 stops, not 4 — because the guard at :87 `target.closest("[data-stop-id]")` reads it as a grab. 44/324 = 13.6% of the rail sterilised per stop. Source comment :35-41 claims the ghost makes the gesture 'self-evident, no instruction line needed'.
defects.mechanism: an affordance chosen to replace explanation that half the input modalities cannot perceive, plus operable-target inflation masking the surface gesture
defects.reproduction: On a touch device or an iPhone-14 Playwright context, tap the rail within ~22px of any handle: nothing is added and nothing is said. `node .../evidence/WBGSE-D-probe2.mjs` block 4.
defects.proposedCure: Make add a named action in the instrument's action row (default position = the largest gap, numerically editable), keeping the rail click as an accelerator rather than the only door.

defects.defect: Selection has no payload: `selectedStopId` has zero readers, and nothing in the product can edit a stop's colour. The component named StopEditor edits position and existence only; the select -> tune -> commit grammar has no tune.
defects.evidence: `grep -rn "selectedStopId" demo/` returns exactly three lines — GradientVisualizer.vue:51 (declaration), :140 (v-model write), :144 (write) — and no read. GradientVisualizer.vue's template has type/space/hue, easing and CSS regions and no stop inspector. GradientPane.vue:8 injects CSS_COLOR_KEY and never uses it. Canon VISUAL-CONSTITUTION.md:96 'select -> tune -> commit'.
defects.mechanism: a selection state invented for local styling, unlocking one action that is already reachable two other ways
defects.reproduction: The greps above; live, select any stop and observe that the only new affordance is the remove chip.
defects.proposedCure: Either give selection its payload — a stop inspector with swatch->picker, numeric position and the single remove action (which simultaneously discharges D2-05, D2-06's numeric arm and D2-14) — or delete selection and keep only drag+add.

defects.defect: The remove chip reserves no geometry: it is absolutely positioned on a 40px-tall container, protrudes 28px, overlaps the next section's rule by 8px and wins the hit-test there. Its glyph is the universal dismiss mark sitting on a divider, and it is visually orphaned from the handle it belongs to.
defects.evidence: Probe 2 block 3: `{"chip":{"y":244.7,"h":24,"bottom":268.7},"barBottom":240.7,"hrTop":260.7,"overlapsHr":true,"chipHitAtHrY":"Remove selected stop"}`; probe 1 `editorRootHeight: 40`. Screenshots `evidence/D-08-chip-on-divider.png` and `evidence/D-02-unsorted-drag.png` both show the X astride the hairline. Source :288 (`absolute w-6 h-6 top-11 z-20`). Composition law OPTICAL-BENCH-COMPOSITIONS.md:78 gives Gradient boundaries `[]` / reserve `none`, yet GradientVisualizer.vue:148,240,251 render three `<hr>` rules.
defects.mechanism: an absolutely-positioned affordance placed outside its own box with no reservation in the parent flow
defects.reproduction: Add a third stop, select the middle one, and look at the divider under the rail; `node .../evidence/WBGSE-D-probe2.mjs` block 3 prints the boxes.
defects.proposedCure: The remove action moves into the selected-stop inspector row that D2-08 requires; nothing then floats outside the rail's box, and the band below the instrument returns to the pure interval the composition's `[]`/`none` boundary law specifies.

defects.defect: Three destructive removal species (right-click, Delete/Backspace, chip) with no confirmation and no undo anywhere on the route; and at the 2-stop floor the Delete key is a silent no-op with no disabled state and no status.
defects.evidence: `node evidence/WBGSE-D-probe5.mjs`: `B after click-add: ["…0%","…50%","…100%"]` then `B after right-click: ["…0%","…100%"]` with `any dialog/confirm/undo affordance: {"dialogs":0,"undoText":[]}`. `A after Delete @2 stops:` labels unchanged, live regions contain only the unrelated palettes text. Sources :164-167 (contextmenu), :180-182 (Delete), :284-300 (chip), :66 (`removable` merely v-ifs the chip away). Canon PROPORTION-AUDIT.md:50 (PR-06) 'Three adjacent action species … REMOVE … One action/selection owner'; VISUAL-CONSTITUTION.md:83 requires explicit disabled states.
defects.mechanism: duplicated action species over one verb, with the unavailable arm expressed as absence rather than state
defects.reproduction: Right-click any handle with >=3 stops — the stop is gone, irreversibly. Focus a handle with exactly 2 stops and press Delete — nothing happens and nothing is announced.
defects.proposedCure: One removal owner in the inspector, with an explicit disabled state carrying its reason at the 2-stop floor; the context-menu and bare-Delete paths retire.

defects.defect: The protagonist is 40px tall. The route's dominant instrument is an h-10 strip; the actual render preview is an 80-96px tile; the pane shares the viewport 50/50 with an unrelated My Palettes companion. This forces every other geometry problem to be solved by invisible means.
defects.evidence: Measured rail 462x40 CSS desktop / 324x40 mobile (probe 1, probe 2 block 4); render tile `w-20 sm:w-24` at GradientVisualizer.vue:223. Canon: PROPORTION-AUDIT.md:53 (PR-09) 'one 19-22rem protagonist' = 304-352px; VISUAL-CONSTITUTION.md:49 and OPTICAL-BENCH-COMPOSITIONS.md:44 give Gradient a dominant meniscus preview at P122 golden 61.8%. Shipped shot docs/tranches/V/megatranche/audit/visual/shots/safari-desktop-light/gradient.png.
defects.mechanism: protagonist subordinated to its own support regions; PR-09 open at this site
defects.reproduction: Open http://localhost:9000/#/gradient at 1440x900 and measure the rail: 40px tall between a subtitle and a rule.
defects.proposedCure: Grant the instrument the 19-22rem stage the composition already assigns it; at that height the 20px dot, the 44px phantom targets and the exiled chip all become unnecessary.

defects.defect: `HANDLE_HALF = 10` duplicates a rem-derived size in JS. At a 20px root font — an ordinary WCAG 1.4.4 text-size setting — the handle grows to 25px while the inset stays 10px, and the 0% handle hangs off the rail's rounded end: the exact condition the file's 'end-handle truce' comment claims to have fixed.
defects.evidence: Probe 2 block 5: `before {"handleW":20,"handleLeftEdge":225,"barLeftEdge":224,"rootFS":"16px"}` → overhang -1.00px (inset); `after {"handleW":25,"handleLeftEdge":100.5,"barLeftEdge":102,"rootFS":"20px"}` → overhang +1.50px (protruding). Sources :53 (`const HANDLE_HALF = 10`), :235 (`w-5 h-5`), :288 (`top-11`), :380-390 (`max(1.5rem,100%)` / `--touch-target`) — four restatements of one constant.
defects.mechanism: a layout constant duplicated in four disagreeing declarations across two languages
defects.reproduction: On /#/gradient run `document.documentElement.style.fontSize='20px'` and measure the 0% handle against the rail's left edge; `node .../evidence/WBGSE-D-probe2.mjs` block 5.
defects.proposedCure: One source of truth: express the handle box in a single custom property that both the stylesheet and the pointer maths read, or measure the rendered box.

defects.defect: The protagonist is the only unnamed region on the route: Interpolation, Easing and CSS each carry an <h3>, while the stop rail has no heading, no label, no aria-label, no role and no group. The hierarchy inverts — support is announced, the protagonist is anonymous.
defects.evidence: Headings at GradientVisualizer.vue:149, 241, 253; the stop editor is rendered bare at :136-145. Probe 1: bar `{role: null, ariaLabel: null}`. Visible in docs/tranches/V/megatranche/audit/visual/shots/safari-desktop-light/gradient.png.
defects.mechanism: section identity granted to support regions and withheld from the protagonist
defects.reproduction: Read the route: three titled bands, one untitled instrument.
defects.proposedCure: The instrument owns a named region (heading plus a group with an accessible name) at the same rung as its siblings, or all four lose their headings together and interval does the grouping the composition's `[]`/`none` boundary law expects.

defects.defect: No visible value, ever: during a drag the position appears nowhere on screen — only in an invisible aria-label and in the CSS string far below — and there is no numeric entry for a stop's position.
defects.evidence: Source :234 (`:aria-label` is the only place the number appears near the control); GradientVisualizer.vue's template has no numeric position field. Canon VISUAL-CONSTITUTION.md:206 requires 'explicit add/move/remove/numeric alternatives'; PROPORTION-AUDIT.md:51 (PR-07) names 'invisible drag state'.
defects.mechanism: a continuous tuning gesture with no readout and no numeric twin
defects.reproduction: Drag any handle and try to land on 42% — the only feedback is the serialized CSS block far below.
defects.proposedCure: A reserved live value beside the axis (the domain-neutral Slider composition already specifies 'label, unit, reserved live value, optional numeric entry').

defects.defect: Crowding has no law: on the 324px mobile rail ten stops give 33.8px centre-to-centre gaps against 44px hit zones, so neighbours become mutually untappable; two stops may also occupy the same position, after which the lower one is unreachable by pointer forever.
defects.evidence: Probe 3 (10 stops, desktop 462px rail): gaps `48.8 48.9 48.8 48.9 49.2 48.9 48.8 48.9 48.8` px; mobile railW measured 324 (probe 2 block 4) → (324-20)/9 = 33.8px < the measured 44px coarse target. `addStop` (useGradientModel.ts:116-119) permits coincident positions; drag permits it. Rendered in `evidence/D-03-ten-hue-rings.png`.
defects.mechanism: no minimum separation, no fan-out, no overflow treatment, no cap on stop count
defects.reproduction: Paste a 10-stop gradient into the CSS block on a 390px viewport and try to grab the 5th stop.
defects.proposedCure: A separation law owned by the collection (minimum ordinal spacing or an explicit fan-out/overflow face), so target inflation cannot exceed the geometry the rail can actually disambiguate.

defects.defect: Design-system boundary: the stop is a hand-rolled circle built from a CSS `linear-gradient(c, c)` trick where the canon names a WatercolorDot face inside a named geometric seat, and the whole visual contract is a 40-line inline `:style` object that shadows any root-level class.
defects.evidence: `grep -rn "WatercolorDot" demo/ | wc -l` → 64 across 19 files (Mix, Generate, Extract, Picker sliders, Dock, ColorSpaceSelector, palettes); `grep -n "WatercolorDot" …/GradientStopEditor.vue` → no matches. Canon: VISUAL-CONSTITUTION.md:206, OPTICAL-BENCH-COMPOSITIONS.md:44 ('stop face inside seat') and :108 (P051 names the Gradient site explicitly). Source :241-264 is the inline style object; the file itself documents the shadowing trap twice (:30-33, :255-261) and then re-enters it for `transition`.
defects.mechanism: a producer species re-implemented locally, with per-instance overrides where root-level styling belongs
defects.reproduction: The two greps above.
defects.proposedCure: Consume the producer species: WatercolorDot face inside a named button seat, with the seat's material contract owned by glass-ui rather than by an inline style object.

defects.defect: In forced-colors the only colour-coded selection delta collapses: selection is border-alpha 0.8 -> 1.0 plus scale, and border-color is forced, so selection survives as a 5px diameter change with no accessible state behind it. Separately, the shipped forced-colors matrix cannot adjudicate this because it runs under WebKit, which does not emulate forced colors.
defects.evidence: Computed unselected border `oklab(0.999994 … / 0.8)` vs selected `border-white` (:236-240); no aria state (probe 5 `== C ==`). Focus is correctly re-expressed as a real outline in forced colors (:353-359) but the resting/selected boundary is not. Harness: docs/tranches/V/megatranche/audit/visual/states.mjs:25 declares `forced-colors-desktop` with the default ENGINE=webkit, and shots/forced-colors-desktop/gradient.png is treated identically to the ordinary light shot.
defects.mechanism: selection encoded only in a channel forced colors overwrites, measured by a harness blind to that mode
defects.reproduction: NONE for the forced-colors delta — hypothesis by construction; the WebKit row is not evidence. Re-run states.mjs with ENGINE=chromium to settle it in either direction.
defects.proposedCure: Give selection an accessible state (aria-pressed/aria-current on the seat) and a non-colour visual delta that survives forced colors; and pin the forced-colors matrix row to Chromium.

result.axis: L — library structure (module boundaries, ownership, direction of dependency, public surface)
result.modelObserved: Opus 5 (1M context), exact model id claude-opus-5[1m] — the tier this seat was spawned with. Declared, not inherited.

defects.defect: The eslint objects that structurally enforce the demo's acyclic module graph (G-DEMO-1 / G-DEMO-3a / G-DEMO-3b) have matched zero files since the W43 restructure: four of five globs target `demo/@/**`, which no longer exists, and the surviving `demo/color-picker/**` glob's pattern targets the `@components/*` alias W43 killed. The demo module graph is unguarded.
defects.evidence: eslint.config.js:232-238 and :276-279 glob `demo/@/components/**`, `demo/@/lib/**`, `demo/@/composables/**`. `ls -d demo/@` → `ls: demo/@: No such file or directory`. `grep -rn 'from "@components/' demo | wc -l` → 0. Decisive: `npx eslint --print-config demo/workbenches/gradient/GradientVisualizer/GradientEasingEditor.vue` → `no-restricted-imports => undefined`. vite.config.ts:70-73 states W43/RF-15 "killed the demo `@…` path aliases".
defects.mechanism: A structural invariant encoded against a directory layout; the layout was refactored and the encoding was not. Flat-config globs that match nothing fail silently.
defects.reproduction: `npx eslint --print-config demo/workbenches/gradient/GradientVisualizer/GradientEasingEditor.vue` and read `rules['no-restricted-imports']` — undefined. Negative control: `grep -rn 'color-picker/' demo/workbenches | wc -l` → 0, so the invariant currently HOLDS by discipline; only the enforcement is dead.
defects.proposedCure: Encode the tier, not the directory-of-the-day. Four no-restricted-imports objects, one per tier that physically exists (boot=demo/color-picker; shell=demo/shell+scenes; features=demo/workbenches+picker; shared=demo/color-session+palettes+platform+shared+ui), each banning `**/{tier-above}/**`. Add one CI assertion that every configured glob matches >=1 file — that is exactly the failure class this finding is.

defects.defect: The gradient's persisted domain type IS a Vue widget's v-model payload: `GradientInterval = EasingPickerValue`, imported from @mkbabb/glass-ui/easing. Three of its six fields are written only to satisfy the widget's type and read by nothing in the gradient tree.
defects.evidence: demo/workbenches/gradient/composables/useGradientModel.ts:12 (`import type { EasingPickerValue } from "@mkbabb/glass-ui/easing"`) and :49 (`export type GradientInterval = EasingPickerValue`). `grep -rn "\.points\b|\.steps\b|\.term\b" demo/workbenches/gradient/` → exactly 2 hits, easingCatalogue.ts:109 and :123, both WRITES inside the tile factory. easingCatalogue.ts:148-152 comments the filler out loud: "Neutral transient cache — steps mode never reads points." useGradientModel.ts:44 concedes css is "the persisted TRUTH" and fn "only a live cache".
defects.mechanism: The layer with the narrowest lifetime (a picker's transient authoring state) was made the type of the layer with the longest (persisted, parseable gradient truth) — direction of dependency inverted at the type level.
defects.reproduction: Deterministic from source: any glass-ui minor adding a 7th member to EasingPickerValue becomes a required field of the demo's persisted gradient model and of gradientParse's output, with no gradient reason. Today's cost is visible now: 6 fields carry 2 facts.
defects.proposedCure: `GradientInterval = { readonly css: string }` in a leaf `model/gradient-model.ts` (value.js already owns the concept as CssTimingFunction via /css). `easingFnOf` (useGradientCSS.ts:120-133) already memoizes css→EasingFunction, so the fn cache moves into the resolver. The EasingPickerValue adaptation becomes two four-line functions AT THE SEAT (EasingAuthoringStage, easingCatalogue) — which is where a widget boundary belongs. The model stops importing glass-ui entirely.

defects.defect: An invariant module-level catalogue (27 specimen tiles) and a full EasingPicker are instantiated once PER INTERVAL inside the v-for, though at most one row is open at a time. One interval row is 30.9% of the whole route's DOM.
defects.evidence: Measured live on http://localhost:9000/#/gradient: `{docNodes: 625, rowCount: 1, perRow: [{nodes: 193, tiles: 27, svgPaths: 41, pickers: 1, pathPointChars: 18541}]}` — 193/625 = 30.9%. SPECIMEN_FAMILIES is a module const (easingCatalogue.ts:198), identical in every row. openInterval is a single `ref<number|null>` (GradientEasingEditor.vue:61). Three downstream workarounds exist because of it: EasingSpecimenStrip.vue:41 ("sibling rows mount hidden twins of every data-specimen id"), its rowEl-scoped querySelector (:55) and no-scrollIntoView rule (:39-46, the O-19 flat-netting root cause), and the v-show-never-v-if picker law (GradientEasingEditor.vue:16-18).
defects.mechanism: Shared, stateless, invariant UI placed inside the iteration that consumes it — cost linear in interval count for a single-open surface.
defects.reproduction: Playwright evaluate on the live dev server (recorded in the report's probe log, row 6). Add stops via the rail and re-measure: perRow.nodes stays 193 and rowCount tracks interval count, so a 5-stop gradient is ~772 elements of easing editor against a 625-element baseline route.
defects.proposedCure: Hoist both invariants out of the v-for: the v-for renders head + ramp only (~12 nodes/row); ONE <EasingSpecimenStrip> and ONE <EasingAuthoringStage> sit below the row list bound to the open row. The strip's `visible` prop, its scroll-scoping workaround, the `tuneOpen: Record<number, boolean>` map (line 84) and the v-show law all delete. Route easing DOM becomes O(1) in interval count.

defects.defect: EasingAuthoringStage patches glass-ui's internals from outside via three :deep() selectors keyed on the producer's test id and internal class names (with three !important), and separately scrapes the DOM in a rAF to recover a viewBox that useEasingPicker already publishes as a reactive ComputedRef.
defects.evidence: EasingAuthoringStage.vue:88 `:deep([data-testid="easing-picker"])`, :93 `:deep(.glass-card)`, :104-115 `:deep(svg[role="img"])` with `block-size: auto !important; aspect-ratio: … !important; margin-inline: 0 !important`. Lines 44-67: `rootEl.value?.querySelector<SVGSVGElement>("svg[role='img']")?.viewBox.baseVal` driven by onMounted + a `watch(() => value.css)` + requestAnimationFrame. Producer already exports it: node_modules/@mkbabb/glass-ui/dist/components/easing/composables/useEasingPicker.d.ts — `/** The bezier-canvas viewBox … */ viewBox: ComputedRef<{ minY: number; height: number }>`, and useEasingPicker is exported from @mkbabb/glass-ui/easing (dist/components/easing/index.d.ts:3). The file's own header (:13-15) concedes "the overrides retire at the adopt".
defects.mechanism: A producer exposing geometry to its own SFC but not through its component contract, and a consumer closing the gap by scraping the DOM instead of filing a prop. Violates edict 4 (variants belong in glass-ui) and edict 5 (root-level styling, never per-instance).
defects.reproduction: Deterministic from source: rename the data-testid or drop role="img" from glass-ui's canvas <svg> in any 7.x patch — no type error, no lint error; the stage silently letterboxes and the one-column law silently reverts to the 18rem chrome rail inside a ~430px pane.
defects.proposedCure: Three props filed at the producer (BH/BI relay): `layout?: "auto" | "stacked"`, `surface?: Surface` (the axis already exists — Chip takes surface?: Surface), and `fit?: "viewbox"` or an @resize emission. All three :deep() blocks, all three !importants, vbRatio, syncVbRatio, the rAF and the watch delete; the stage becomes `<EasingPicker layout="stacked" surface="well" fit="viewbox" :playback="false" :readout="false">` and nothing else.

defects.defect: Four names for three types across the value.js↔glass-ui seam, bridged by two casts in this component's catalogue — and value.js declares the jump union TWICE, independently, in one file, with a runtime membership check guarding a type the compiler already closes.
defects.evidence: src/easing.ts:4 `EasingFunction = (progress: number) => number` vs glass-ui `EasingFn = (t: number) => number` (useEasingPicker.d.ts, commented "the value.js family shape"). src/easing.ts:13 `JumpPosition = "jump-start"|"jump-end"|"jump-none"|"jump-both"` AND :68 `jumpTerms = [same four] as const` — written out twice; :136 `if (!(jumpTerms as readonly string[]).includes(position)) return err(...)` is the runtime guard against a closed union. src/easing.ts:67 types bezierPresets values as an inline `readonly [number,number,number,number]` with no exported name; glass-ui declares `BezierPoints`. Casts: easingCatalogue.ts:136 `const position = term as JumpPosition;` and :108/:123 `[...points] as BezierPoints`.
defects.mechanism: Boundary vocabulary re-declared downstream instead of imported, and the upstream gave it two unlinked spellings to re-declare from.
defects.reproduction: Deterministic from source: add "jump-both-inclusive" to jumpTerms (src/easing.ts:68) and forget line 13. JumpTerm widens, JumpPosition does not, and easingCatalogue.ts:136's `as` SILENCES the resulting error — the demo compiles clean and steppedEase rejects at runtime with jump_position_invalid.
defects.proposedCure: In value.js: `export type JumpPosition = (typeof jumpTerms)[number];` (one line — kills the drift AND the runtime guard) and `export type BezierQuad = readonly [number,number,number,number]` from /easing. In glass-ui: delete EasingFn, JumpTerm and BezierPoints; import EasingFunction, JumpPosition and BezierQuad from @mkbabb/value.js/easing, which it already depends on (useEasingPicker.d.ts line 2 imports jumpTerms from it today). Both casts in easingCatalogue.ts delete.

defects.defect: value.js /easing publishes the curve callables but no presentation-neutral projection of one, so curve→SVG-path is forked three ways across the constellation — including glyphPath sitting in a demo leaf, which is pure library math with no DOM, Vue or CSS in it.
defects.evidence: demo/.../easing/easingCatalogue.ts:66-74 `glyphPath(fn, samples = 48)` — its own header (:58-65) names it an assay of keyframes.js `generateCurveSVGPath`. glass-ui ships two more: useEasingPicker.d.ts `bezierPathD: ComputedRef<string>` and `stepPathD: ComputedRef<string>`. src/subpaths/easing.ts exports CubicBezier, bezierPresets, steppedEase, easing, linearEasing and no path/sampling function.
defects.mechanism: The library published the semantics and withheld the projection, so the projection was re-derived at each consumer.
defects.reproduction: NONE — this is a structural claim over three quoted files, not a runtime hypothesis.
defects.proposedCure: `export function sampleCurvePath(fn: EasingFunction, samples = 48): string` in src/easing.ts, exported from /easing. glyphPath deletes; stepPathD deletes; keyframes.js's copy deletes. bezierPathD stays — it is an analytic `C` path, a genuinely different artifact, and that difference becomes visible instead of buried.

defects.defect: Two back-compat re-export barrels in the gradient composables — one measurably dead, one producing a LIVE dual path: two sibling workbenches import the same constant by two different routes (3 hops vs 1).
defects.evidence: useGradientModel.ts:19-29 re-exports 7 names under the comment "Re-exports (preserve public API surface)"; `for n in serializeGradient serializeCoalescedGradient serializeRailRamp linearInterval parseGradientCSS GradientParseResult ParsedGradientModel; do grep -rn "$n" demo --include='*.ts' --include='*.vue' | grep -v workbenches/gradient/composables/; done` → 2 hits, BOTH prose inside comments (GradientStopEditor.vue:9, easingCatalogue.ts:44). Every real consumer imports the origin: gradientParse.ts:22 and useGradientModel.ts:15 take linearInterval from ./useGradientCSS; the subject takes serializeIntervalRamp from ../composables/useGradientCSS (:31). Live dual path: useGradientInterpolation.ts:17 re-exports INTERPOLATION_SPACES with the comment "Re-exported here so the gradient tree's own consumers keep their import path", useGradientModel.ts:21 re-exports it again → GradientVisualizer.vue:19 reaches it in 3 hops while MixConfigBar.vue:18 imports it directly from color-session/color-space-meta in 1.
defects.mechanism: A barrel minted to preserve an import path nobody needed, leaving two live doors to one symbol. Edict 2 (no aliases, no dual paths).
defects.reproduction: The grep above: 7 re-exported names, 0 non-comment consumers. And the two live import paths at GradientVisualizer.vue:19-21 vs MixConfigBar.vue:18.
defects.proposedCure: Delete both re-export blocks. GradientVisualizer.vue imports INTERPOLATION_SPACES/HUE_INTERPOLATION_METHODS from color-session/color-space-meta exactly as MixConfigBar already does. One name, one door.

defects.defect: value.js is failure-explicit by design but publishes no unwrap: no subpath exports ok/err or an unwrap helper, only the Result type. The demo hand-rolls the unwrap-or-throw 17 times, twice as the same function five files apart.
defects.evidence: `cat src/foundation/result.ts` → exports only `Result`, `ok`, `err`; src/subpaths/color.ts:9 exports the Result TYPE alone; no subpath exports an unwrap. `grep -rn "throw new Error(\`" demo --include='*.ts' --include='*.vue' | grep -i error.code` → 17 sites (useGradientCSS.ts ×3, useGradientInterpolation.ts:37, easingCatalogue.ts:103, mixStage.ts:106, useMarkdownColors.ts ×2, generate-color.ts ×3, color-utils.ts:18, ink.ts ×4, palettes/mix.ts:36). Five are in this component's own chain. useGradientCSS.ts:71-77 and easingCatalogue.ts:98-104 are the SAME function, differing only in the error prefix; both are typed `ReturnType<typeof CubicBezier>` while also fed steppedEase results, which type-checks only by coincidence of shape.
defects.mechanism: A library published the discipline (explicit Result) and withheld the ergonomic, so seventeen consumers re-invented the escape hatch, each with its own message format and none with a shared type.
defects.reproduction: The grep above returns 17 hand-rolled sites; `diff` the two easingValue bodies (useGradientCSS.ts:71-77, easingCatalogue.ts:98-104) — identical but for the string literal.
defects.proposedCure: Publish the unwrap from the foundation as an eighth subpath: `export function unwrap<T, E extends {code: string}>(r: Result<T,E>, context: string): T { if (r.ok) return r.value; throw new Error(`${context}: ${r.error.code}`); }`. Seventeen hand-rolled sites collapse to seventeen call sites of one function with one message grammar, and easingValue stops existing twice.

defects.defect: The component imports useClipboard from the glass-ui ROOT BARREL when the composable's published home is the ./dom subpath — and on this route ./dom is already loaded, so the edge is a pure second door, not even a size trade.
defects.evidence: GradientEasingEditor.vue:29 `import { useClipboard } from "@mkbabb/glass-ui";`. glass-ui 7.0.0 publishes 74 subpaths; useClipboard's home is ./dom (dist/dom.js:134 exports it; dist/composables/dom/useClipboard.d.ts declares it). Measured from the live prebundle cache: `ls -la node_modules/.vite/deps/@mkbabb_glass-ui*.js` → `231357 @mkbabb_glass-ui.js` vs `4256 @mkbabb_glass-ui_dom.js` (54×). Static closure over dist/: root barrel 66 modules / 224,193 B vs dom.js 8 modules / 12,599 B. Live network on /#/gradient fetches BOTH (`@mkbabb_glass-ui.js` req #26 and `@mkbabb_glass-ui_dom.js` req #27), so dom.js is in the graph regardless. Same edge at GradientVisualizer.vue:12 (writeClipboard) and across the 19 demo/ui/* one-line barrels.
defects.mechanism: Root-barrel reach past a published narrow subpath — a second import path to a module the page already has. Edict 2.
defects.reproduction: `ls -la node_modules/.vite/deps/@mkbabb_glass-ui*.js` for the 54× size gap; browser_network_requests(filter: glass-ui) on /#/gradient shows both chunks fetched.
defects.proposedCure: `import { useClipboard } from "@mkbabb/glass-ui/dom";` — and a no-restricted-imports rule banning the bare `@mkbabb/glass-ui` group while allowing `@mkbabb/glass-ui/*`, so the class cannot recur. Which requires L-r2-1 to be fixed first.

defects.defect: Three props where one suffices: `:stops` and `:intervals` are the identical array references already inside `:model-state`.
defects.evidence: GradientVisualizer.vue:242-247 passes `:stops="stops" :intervals="intervals" :model-state="modelState"`. useGradientModel.ts:102-109 builds modelState as `{ …, stops: stops.value, intervals: intervals.value, … }` — the same references, not derived copies. GradientEasingEditor.vue:42-46 takes all three and :54-58 forwards all three as getters to useSpecimenRows, which then uses `model` for nothing but interpolationSpace/hueMethod (useSpecimenRows.ts:56-58) — while serializeIntervalRamp(modelState, …) at line 66 reads the stops back OUT of modelState.
defects.mechanism: A prop surface grown per-need instead of being the model.
defects.reproduction: Read useGradientModel.ts:102-109 against GradientVisualizer.vue:242-247 — the same two arrays arrive by two routes.
defects.proposedCure: One prop: `:model="modelState"`. useSpecimenRows(model) takes one getter. Three props → one, three getters → one, and "which stops are authoritative" stops being askable.

defects.defect: A type-level module cycle between the model, the serializer and the parser — which is why the module named for the composable also owns the types, which is why the dead re-export barrel felt necessary.
defects.evidence: useGradientModel.ts:15 imports values from ./useGradientCSS and :16 from ./gradientParse; useGradientCSS.ts:31-34 imports types back from ./useGradientModel; gradientParse.ts:22 imports linearInterval from ./useGradientCSS and :23-27 imports types from ./useGradientModel.
defects.mechanism: Types co-located with the composable that consumes them rather than in a leaf, producing mutual reference.
defects.reproduction: NONE at runtime — both back-edges are `import type`, so verbatimModuleSyntax erases them; I verified this and am NOT claiming a runtime cycle. The cycle is real in the type graph only.
defects.proposedCure: A leaf `model/gradient-model.ts` holding GradientStop, GradientInterval, GradientModelState, GradientType and nothing else. Everything imports down into it; nothing imports back out. The cycle and the barrel both vanish.

defects.defect: value.js publishes BezierPresetName for exactly the cast the demo writes by hand; the demo uses it zero times and re-derives it instead.
defects.evidence: src/subpaths/easing.ts:2 exports `BezierPresetName`. `grep -rn "BezierPresetName" demo | wc -l` → 0. easingCatalogue.ts:107 writes `bezierPresets[name as keyof typeof bezierPresets]`, where `name` comes from `Object.keys(bezierPresets)` (:178) typed string[] — so the cast is load-bearing. src/easing.ts:15 defines `BezierPresetName = keyof typeof PRESETS`.
defects.mechanism: A published type name unused because the library did not also publish the typed key list that would make the cast unnecessary.
defects.reproduction: The two greps above.
defects.proposedCure: Export `bezierPresetNames: readonly BezierPresetName[]` from /easing alongside bezierPresets; the demo iterates it and the `as keyof typeof` cast deletes.

defects.defect: Per-instance CSS override of the exact glass-ui variant the component is simultaneously requesting: .specimen-tile re-declares the flex/gap/padding recipe that shape="cell" already applies.
defects.evidence: EasingSpecimenStrip.vue:98-107 passes `shape="cell"`; node_modules/@mkbabb/glass-ui/dist/components/chip/chipVariants.d.ts defines SHAPE.cell = "glass-chip--cell flex-col gap-1.5 px-2 py-2.5 text-micro". EasingSpecimenStrip.vue:163-170 then sets `display:flex; flex-direction:column; align-items:center; gap:0.125rem; padding:0.3125rem 0.375rem 0.25rem; min-width:2.75rem`.
defects.mechanism: A size variant of an existing root variant expressed as consumer scoped CSS. Edict 5.
defects.reproduction: Read the two blocks side by side — the seat overrides the padding and gap it just requested.
defects.proposedCure: Add `xs` to Chip's SIZE map in glass-ui (BH/BI relay) and pass `size="xs" shape="cell"`. Six declarations delete here.

defects.defect: HYPOTHESIS (not this seat's axis, recorded for a routing seat): a persisted-route restore appears to win a race against the requested initial hash on a cold browser context.
defects.evidence: Playwright navigate to http://localhost:9000/#/gradient, then evaluate a few seconds later → `{href: "http://localhost:9000/#/browse", gradientSfc: 0, rowsRendered: 0, headingText: ["Browse", "My Palettes1 (1 saved)"]}`. Setting location.hash = "#/gradient" afterwards mounted the pane in ~1.0s and it held. The visual-audit matrix does NOT show this (settle 3586ms, captures correct).
defects.mechanism: Unknown — suspected boot-time route restore vs initial hash resolution ordering.
defects.reproduction: NONE — observed once, not deterministically reproduced. Labelled a hypothesis; no claim in this report is built on it.
defects.proposedCure: Hand to a routing/boot seat: assert the initial hash wins over any persisted-route restore, or that the restore only applies when the URL carries no route.

defects.defect: Measurement caveat recorded so no one re-derives a wrong number: the page's resource-timing buffer capped at its 250-entry default during my probes, silently dropping later entries.
defects.evidence: `performance.getEntriesByType('resource').length` returned exactly 250, and a probe consequently reported `gradientSfc: []` on a page that had plainly loaded the gradient modules (rowsRendered: 1, tiles: 27 in the same call).
defects.mechanism: Default resourceTimingBufferSize truncation.
defects.reproduction: Any evaluate reading performance.getEntriesByType('resource') on this app after full settle returns exactly 250.
defects.proposedCure: Any future perf probe on this app must call `performance.setResourceTimingBufferSize(2000)` via addInitScript before navigation. The chunk facts in L-r2-9 come from the network log and on-disk prebundle sizes, not from the truncated buffer.

result.strongestDefect: L-r2-2 — `GradientInterval = EasingPickerValue` (useGradientModel.ts:12,49). The premise names "wrong direction of dependency" and this is it in one line: the persisted domain type of the library's own showcase IS a Vue widget's transient v-model payload, three of whose six fields (`points`, `steps`, `term`) are written solely to satisfy the widget and read by nothing — proven by `grep -rn "\.points\b|\.steps\b|\.term\b" demo/workbenches/gradient/` returning exactly 2 hits, both WRITES in the tile factory, one of them commented "Neutral transient cache — steps mode never reads points." Every other ownership defect in the report is downstream of the same instinct: when a layer has no public door, take the type from whichever neighbour does. Runner-up by measurement: L-r2-3 (193 DOM elements per interval row = 30.9% of the route's DOM for an invariant module-const catalogue). Runner-up by blast radius: L-r2-1 (the demo module-graph lint guard has matched zero files since W43).
result.negativeProof: Verdict is DEFECTIVE, but four premise-predicted defects are provably ABSENT and are recorded first in the report so the finding list is not read as blanket condemnation: (1) The demo consumes value.js ONLY through the published exports map — `grep -rn "@src" demo/workbenches/gradient/ | wc -l` → 0; every library edge in this component's chain is `@mkbabb/value.js/easing` (easingCatalogue.ts:22-30), `/color` + `/easing` + `/css` (useGradientCSS.ts:12-29), `/color` (useGradientInterpolation.ts:8-9), `/css` (gradientParse.ts:21) — specifiers a real npm consumer can write verbatim. This is NOT a false proof of the public API; the T.W1 dogfood keystone holds. (2) verbatimModuleSyntax is fully satisfied — subject lines 30, 34, 36-40 are all `import type`, lines 27-29/31-33/35 are value imports of values; zero violations across the component and its four sub-modules. (3) The workbench tier does not reach up, despite the guard being dead: `grep -rn "color-picker/" demo/workbenches | wc -l` → 0 and `grep -rn 'from "\.\./\.\./\(shell\|scenes\)' demo/workbenches | wc -l` → 0; all 28 workbenches→color-session and 17 workbenches→palettes edges point downward into shared domain layers. (4) Runtime is clean — visual audit /#/gradient across all four Safari matrices: pageErrors 0, consoleErrors 0, overflowX 0, main 1 (REPORT.json); the route's 6 smallTapTargets belong to OTHER components (22×22 slug controls, 20×20 stop handles) and I measured this component's rail buttons live at 24×24, which clears the WCAG 2.5.8 floor — so I raise no tap-target finding. I also read the safari-desktop-light gradient.png: the component renders correctly (interval head, endpoint dots, micro glyph, live ramp, 27-tile strip, readout rail) with no visual defect.

result.axis: CHALLENGE-L — library structure / module boundaries / ownership (second, independent pass; merged as an addendum onto an existing first-pass report at the same axis)
result.modelObserved: Opus 5 — exact model id `claude-opus-5[1m]`, 1M context. Declared, not inherited.

defects.defect: The loupe canvas has two owners: `useLoupeCanvas` holds its ref by template-string (`useTemplateRef("loupeCanvasRef")`) while `ImageEyedropper.vue` owns the element's existence with `v-if`. `showLoupeAt` flips the flag and calls `drawLoupe` synchronously, so the ref is still null and the draw silently early-returns. On touch there is no follow-up pointermove and `hideLoupe` unmounts the element again, so the magnifier NEVER paints.
defects.evidence: useLoupeCanvas.ts:21 (useTemplateRef by string), :30 (silent early return), :56-59 (flip + synchronous draw); ImageEyedropper.vue:78,85 (v-if owns the element). jsdom+Vue reproduction output: 'sample #1 … drawLoupe() sees loupeCanvasRef = null -> EARLY RETURN, no paint' / 'after nextTick: <canvas>' / 'sample #2 … -> paints'. Visual: probe/shot-mobile-dark-tapped.png shows the loupe ring fully transparent — the fixture's purple/grey edge continues through the circle at 1:1 scale, not the 10x blow-up a painted loupe would show.
defects.mechanism: ownership split — element lifetime owned by the template, element reference owned by a composable, joined only by a string name and by Vue's flush ordering
defects.reproduction: node --input-type=module -e '<appendix A2 in the report>' — prints the null-ref early return on sample #1. Independently visible in docs/tranches/V/megatranche/audit/components/wb-extract-imageeyedropper/probe/shot-mobile-dark-tapped.png.
defects.proposedCure: Do not split existence from reference. The DPR-correct, paint-on-demand 2D surface is a design-system primitive: glass-ui `./canvas` publishes `useCanvas2D`/`useCanvasLifecycle` (loop-shaped) and needs a paint-on-demand sibling; the loupe becomes a `Loupe.vue` that owns its canvas outright through it. Relay the glass-ui half to the BH inbox per the standing relay invariant.

defects.defect: `useImageSampler.formatInColorSpace` is a second, DIVERGENT implementation of the app's canonical display-space formatter `formatForSelectedDisplaySpace`. For the four non-CSS spaces the eyedropper and the picker render the same color in the same selected space with notations that share no token.
defects.evidence: Canonical: demo/color-session/useColorPipeline.ts:174-179; `serializePickerColor` already answers for non-CSS spaces at demo/color-session/picker-color.ts:206-211. Duplicate: useImageSampler.ts:55-66 + :38-44. Measured on #ff0000 against dist/subpaths — hsv: eyedropper 'HSV 0 · 1 · 1' vs canonical 'oklch(62.795536392143% 0.257683303805 29.233880279628deg)'; kelvin: 'KELVIN 1000' vs 'oklch(65.925252512236% …)'; ictcp: 'ICTCP 0.4279 · -0.1157 · 0.2787' vs 'oklch(…)'; jzazbz: 'JZAZBZ 0.1344 · 0.1179 · 0.1119' vs 'oklch(…)'. Reachable: usePaneRouter.ts:139 forwards model.value.selectedColorSpace live; color-model.ts:74 declares all 17 spaces + hex selectable.
defects.mechanism: unique-semantic-ownership broken — the domain already decided, and the feature overrides the decision privately
defects.reproduction: node --input-type=module -e '<appendix B2 in the report>'. In-app: select HSV in the picker, open the eyedropper on /#/extract, sample pure red — picker reads oklch(62.79…%), eyedropper reads 'HSV 0 · 1 · 1'.
defects.proposedCure: Lift `formatForSelectedDisplaySpace` out of the `useColorPipeline` orchestration composable into `demo/color-session/color-model.ts` as a pure `formatForDisplaySpace(color, space)`; delete `formatInColorSpace` and `formatLibraryColor`. If the `HSV 0 · 1 · 1` shape is the better product answer it becomes the canonical one and the picker adopts it — the choice is made once, by the domain.

defects.defect: The sampler reads the alpha byte from the canvas and discards it. `data[3]` is never referenced; the offscreen canvas is created without `{alpha:false}`, and `image/*` is accepted, so a transparent PNG pixel is reported and saved as opaque #000000.
defects.evidence: useImageSampler.ts:116-118 (`formatHex(data[0], data[1], data[2])` — data[3] absent), :32-35 (`formatHex` has no alpha parameter), :83 (getContext without alpha:false); demo/workbenches/extract/ImageDropZone.vue:30 `accept="image/*"`. Library affordance that carries alpha: `rgb(r,g,b,alpha)` on src/subpaths/color.ts; `toRgba8` round-trips it at picker-color.ts:214; `pickerColorToHex` (picker-color.ts:213-217) already emits the 8-digit form when alpha<1.
defects.mechanism: a lossy carrier (6-digit hex string) chosen where the library's own byte↔color pair is alpha-complete in both directions
defects.reproduction: Drop any logo PNG with a transparent background on /#/extract, open the eyedropper, sample the transparent region: readout claims #000000 and 'Add to palette' writes an opaque black swatch. No warning.
defects.proposedCure: Stop going through a hex string: `rgb(data[0], data[1], data[2], data[3] / 255)`. Alpha survives end-to-end and the display side is already ready. Pairs with the first pass's `fromRgba8` proposal for src/color/operations.ts.

defects.defect: `justUnpinned` is a one-shot module-scope flag cleared ONLY inside `onTap`, but `onTap` fires only when the pointer did not move. A pan-after-pin leaves it stuck true and swallows the user's next tap.
defects.evidence: ImageEyedropper.vue:123 (`let justUnpinned = false`), :178-184 (capture-phase pointerdown sets it), :152-155 (onTap is the only reset); useInertiaGesture.ts:277-281 (`if (!didMove) options.onTap?.(…)`).
defects.mechanism: the interaction state machine is split across a gesture composable that owns the events and a shell that owns the mode, communicating through DOM capture ordering and a boolean
defects.reproduction: On /#/extract with an image loaded: (1) tap to sample — pinned; (2) press-drag to pan, release — onTap never fires, flag stays true; (3) tap to sample — swallowed, nothing happens; (4) tap again — works.
defects.proposedCure: The gesture composable owns every listener on the element it bound and owns tap semantics: add the mode/`onPointerDown` as first-class options on `useInertiaGesture` beside `onTap`/`onHover`. The capture-phase listener and the flag both disappear.

defects.defect: `DisplayColorSpace` is declared four times: the canonical home plus three re-mints inside the extract feature — and the eyedropper's re-mint is EXPORTED, so the library test suite imports the duplicate rather than the canonical type.
defects.evidence: Canonical demo/color-session/color-model.ts:29 (documented, 8 consumers). Re-mints: demo/workbenches/extract/ExtractPane.vue:30, ExtractWorkbench.vue:202, ImageEyedropper/composables/useImageSampler.ts:21 (exported). test/image-sampler-v4.test.ts:5 imports the re-mint. Grep: `grep -rn 'SpaceId | "hex"' demo src test e2e` → exactly those three.
defects.mechanism: one concept, four homes; the duplicate acquired a consumer and became load-bearing
defects.reproduction: NONE — static, proved by enumeration (the grep above).
defects.proposedCure: Delete all three re-mints; `import type { DisplayColorSpace } from "…/color-session/color-model"`. Type the pane props bag (usePaneRouter.ts:64 `Record<string, unknown>`) so the router cannot lose the type across the boundary.

defects.defect: The magnifier is DPR-blind: a fixed 110x110 backing store for a 110 CSS-px box, so on any devicePixelRatio > 1 the one surface whose job is pixel fidelity is composited upscaled. glass-ui publishes the DPR policy; zero demo modules consume it; a sibling workbench re-derives it by hand.
defects.evidence: ImageEyedropper.vue:85 `width="110" height="110"` (hard literal) vs constants.ts:8 LOUPE_SIZE=110 and ImageEyedropper.vue:194-195; useLoupeCanvas.ts:40 `imageSmoothingEnabled = false`. glass-ui useCanvas2D.d.ts: 'dprPolicy — Backing-store DPR policy. Defaults to the existing Canvas2D ceiling: min(devicePixelRatio, 2)'. `grep -rn "useCanvas2D|useCanvasLifecycle|glass-ui/canvas" demo` → 0 matches. `grep -rn devicePixelRatio demo` → 2 matches, neither here; demo/workbenches/mix/MixAnimationCanvas/composables/useMixingAnimation.ts:141 re-derives `Math.min(window.devicePixelRatio || 1, 2)` by hand. 11 hand-rolled `getContext("2d")` sites in demo.
defects.mechanism: a published design-system primitive exists and every consumer hand-rolls a worse version — owner edict 4
defects.reproduction: NONE for the on-screen blur (this machine reports dpr 1); the absence of any DPR term is proved by the greps and the consequence follows deterministically from the fixed backing store plus `w-full h-full`.
defects.proposedCure: glass-ui `./canvas` grows a paint-on-demand `useCanvas2DSurface` (element observation + min(dpr,2) backing store + context attrs + dispose, no rAF); the loupe and MixAnimationCanvas both consume it. This fix lands in glass-ui, not demo — relay it.

defects.defect: One user file is decoded three times and retained in three representations; the eyedropper alone holds two full-resolution canvases (one of which is never sampled and exists only to be CSS-transformed, with will-change-transform promoting it to a compositor layer at native size).
defects.evidence: useExtractSession.ts:29-36,166 (FileReader base64 data URL, never cleared); useImageQuantize.ts:18-26 (independent createImageBitmap + OffscreenCanvas decode of the same File); useImageSampler.ts:80-84 (offscreen canvas at natural size — needed) and :86-92 (visible canvas ALSO at natural size — not needed); ImageEyedropper.vue:71 `will-change-transform`. `node -e 'const b=4032*3024*4; …'` → 46.51 MiB each, 93.02 MiB retained for a phone photo (15.82 MiB at 1080p).
defects.mechanism: 'the decoded image' is a concept with no owner — the session owns a File and a base64 string, the quantizer owns a private decode, the sampler owns two more
defects.reproduction: NONE measured on-device; byte counts derived from W*H*4 and confirmed arithmetically. The three decode sites are proved by the file:line references.
defects.proposedCure: One `demo/workbenches/extract/image-source.ts`: takes the File once, yields an ImageBitmap consumed by BOTH the quantizer and the sampler plus an object URL (not base64) for display. The visible canvas becomes an `` under the same transform — one decoded copy, no native-resolution compositor layer. The `createObjectURL`/`revokeObjectURL` idiom already exists in-repo at demo/palettes/export.ts:88-131.
