defects.defect: LOUPE_SIZE has two homes — the constant and a hard-coded `110` literal for the canvas backing store — so the one edit the constant exists to enable silently corrupts the magnifier.
defects.evidence: constants.ts:8 `export const LOUPE_SIZE = 110`; ImageEyedropper.vue:85 `width="110" height="110"` (literal) vs :194-195 (`${LOUPE_SIZE}px` for the CSS box); useLoupeCanvas.ts:38 `ctx.arc(LOUPE_SIZE/2, LOUPE_SIZE/2, LOUPE_SIZE/2, …)` and :41-51 `drawImage(…, 0, 0, LOUPE_SIZE, LOUPE_SIZE)`.
defects.mechanism: dual source of truth for one number, with no type or test connecting them
defects.reproduction: Set LOUPE_SIZE = 160 in constants.ts. The CSS ring grows to 160px, the backing store stays 110x110; `ctx.arc(80,80,80,…)` centres the clip off-canvas and the 160-unit drawImage overflows a 110-unit surface — the magnified pixels occupy ~47% of the circle, clipped to the wrong disc, then stretched 1.45x. Nothing errors.
defects.proposedCure: Bind it (`:width="LOUPE_SIZE * dpr"`), or better, let the canvas substrate of L-7 size the backing store from the CSS box — which is the reason such a substrate exists.

defects.defect: The pixel path re-enters the library through the CSS PARSER to obtain numbers it already holds: bytes → hand-rolled hex string → parseCssColor → convert. `rgb()` is published on ./color for exactly this input.
defects.evidence: useImageSampler.ts:116-118 and :55-66 (parseCssColor(hex) then convertPickerColor); `rgb` is exported from src/subpaths/color.ts and already imported by picker-color.ts:19. Measured this pass: 'parse-roundtrip: 0.55us per sample / rgb() direct: 0.08us per sample / ratio 6.5x' (N=20000). First pass measured 1.26x at N=200000 — see §C of the report; magnitude is measurement-sensitive, direction is not.
defects.mechanism: the demo proves the parser where it should prove the constructors, and manufactures a failure mode (a throw inside a pointermove handler) that could not otherwise exist
defects.reproduction: node --input-type=module -e '<appendix C2 in the report>'. The manufactured throw is at useImageSampler.ts:60, whose message indexes `parsed.diagnostics[0].code` and would itself TypeError on an empty diagnostics array.
defects.proposedCure: `rgb(data[0], data[1], data[2], data[3]/255)`. The parse, the hex string, the throw and the alpha loss (L-18) all vanish together. Symmetrically, add the missing `fromRgba8` inverse to src/color/operations.ts and the ./color subpath, per the first pass.

defects.defect: `formatInColorSpace` is exported from the composable only because a test calls it, and the test pins the L-17 divergence as if it were the contract.
defects.evidence: useImageSampler.ts:55 (definition), :118 (the only in-module caller), :136 (exported anyway); ImageEyedropper.vue never references it; test/image-sampler-v4.test.ts:18,19,20,24,28 are the only consumers, and :24 asserts `toBe("HSV 0 · 1 · 1")`.
defects.mechanism: public surface shaped by a test rather than a consumer — the route by which a defect acquires tenure
defects.reproduction: NONE — static, proved by the grep in the report's §D2.
defects.proposedCure: Once L-17 lands the formatter lives in demo/color-session/ and is tested there, against the one implementation the whole app shares; the composable's return surface narrows to what ImageEyedropper.vue actually calls.

defects.defect: This component has ZERO coverage in the visual-audit matrix — the eyedropper overlay is never mounted by the harness, so every /#/extract row describes ImageDropZone/ExtractControls only.
defects.evidence: ImageEyedropper is mounted at ExtractWorkbench.vue:173 under `v-if="eyedropperActive && session.previewDataUrl.value"` — it requires an uploaded image. docs/tranches/V/megatranche/audit/visual/REPORT.md:122,137,152,167 show /#/extract with 0 pageErrors, 0 consoleErrors, 0 overflowX across all four Safari matrices; the 3 namelessButtons and 6 smallTapTargets belong to the drop zone. `ls shots/zoom-200-desktop` → adminusers, blob, browse, gradient, picker — no extract.png at all.
defects.mechanism: the capture harness has no fixture-image state, so the component's entire interactive surface is unphotographed
defects.reproduction: NONE needed — the absence is directly observable in REPORT.md and the shots tree.
defects.proposedCure: Add an image-fixture state for /#/extract to the capture harness (the states.mjs seam already exists). L-1 is precisely the class of failure a single screenshot would have caught — and the probe/ shot taken by hand did catch it.

result.strongestDefect: L-1 — the loupe canvas's existence is owned by the template (`v-if`) while its reference is owned by a composable (`useTemplateRef` by string name), and `showLoupeAt` draws synchronously in the same tick. The first paint always lands on an element that does not exist yet; on the touch path `hideLoupe` unmounts it again between samples, so the magnifier — the component's headline feature on the devices it was built for — never paints at all. Confirmed four independent ways: the first pass's getImageData counts (0 of 12100 non-transparent px on first hover; 0 after a synthetic touch tap), this pass's jsdom+Vue mechanism reproduction, and probe/shot-mobile-dark-tapped.png, in which the fixture's purple/grey edge runs straight through the loupe ring at 1:1 scale — the viewer is looking through an unpainted canvas.
result.negativeProof: Not SOUND overall, but the axis's headline risk is provably clean and must not be re-litigated downstream: (1) NO deep-import of library internals — `grep -rn \"@src|value.js/src\" demo/workbenches/extract` → no matches; both library specifiers (`@mkbabb/value.js/color`, `/css`) are keys of package.json#exports, and vite.config.ts:29-50 generates the self-alias set FROM that exports map with anchored regexes, so a deep-path import could not silently resolve. A real consumer could write every library import in this component verbatim. (2) NO unpublished glass-ui subpath — all four (`/dock`, `/watercolor-dot`, `/dom`, `/motion-core`) are keys of glass-ui 7.0.0's 74-key export map. (3) CORS/canvas tainting, the named component suspect, is a NON-ISSUE as shipped: the sole mount (ExtractWorkbench.vue:173) passes `session.previewDataUrl`, a same-origin `data:` URL from FileReader.readAsDataURL (useExtractSession.ts:29-36), which cannot taint a canvas — `getImageData` at useImageSampler.ts:116 cannot throw SecurityError on any reachable path. (4) `verbatimModuleSyntax` is clean across all five files. (5) Edict 6 (animations) is satisfied — `@keyframes swatch-pop` is component-scoped and single-use, and demo/styles/animations.css contains no swatch keyframe it duplicates. (6) Every custom property resolves: `--z-controls` (20), `--duration-fast`, `--ease-decelerate`, `--ease-spring` from glass-ui's shipped token sheets; `--shadow-color` from demo/styles/foundation.css:358/:514; `.glass-floating` from foundation.css:774. (7) `useRAFLoop` adoption at useInertiaGesture.ts:114-129 — pauseWhenHidden on, respectReducedMotion deliberately off with the PRM decision kept local and documented — is exemplary design-system consumption. The failure is not that the demo cheats on the library; it is that the demo's own internal boundaries are unowned, and (first pass L-10) the eslint rules written to guard them target `demo/@/`, a tree deleted at W43, so they match zero files.

result.axis: CHALLENGE-C — implementation (assume the component is improperly implemented)
result.modelObserved: Opus 5 (claude-opus-5[1m], 1M-context variant) — declared at spawn, not inherited
result.strongestDefect: D-1 — the magnifier loupe renders COMPLETELY BLANK on every first show, and permanently blank on the touch path: showLoupeAt() sets loupeVisible=true and calls drawLoupe() in the same synchronous tick, but the target canvas lives behind v-if="loupeVisible" so it is not in the DOM yet and drawLoupe silently early-returns. Measured three independent ways (loupeNonZeroPx=0 with no drawImage on the 110-wide canvas after a hover-less tap; 40 pointermoves → 39 loupe draws; visible empty circle in the screenshot). Because pinned=true then blocks onHover, nothing ever repaints it — the component's entire raison d'être is dead on mobile.
result.negativeProof: n/a — verdict is DEFECTIVE

defects.defect: The magnifier loupe renders blank on every first show and stays permanently blank on the touch path. `showLoupeAt` flips `loupeVisible` and calls `drawLoupe` in the same synchronous tick, but the canvas is behind `v-if="loupe.loupeVisible.value"`, so `loupeCanvasRef.value` is still null and the draw is silently skipped. Since `onTap` also sets `pinned=true`, `onHover` (the only path that would repaint) returns early forever.
defects.evidence: demo/workbenches/extract/ImageEyedropper/composables/useLoupeCanvas.ts:55-60 (showLoupeAt) and :27-30 (drawLoupe early return); ImageEyedropper.vue:78-86 (v-if + canvas). MEASURED (probe2 §A): A_pinned {loupeVisible:true, loupeNonZeroPx:9604, di110:2} → Escape → A_tapNoHover {loupeVisible:true, loupeNonZeroPx:0, di110:2} → A_afterOneMove {loupeNonZeroPx:0, di110:2}. Independent replication (probe4): {"pointermoves":40,"getImageDataCalls":40,"loupeDraws":39} — the missing draw is the first. Visual: .playwright-mcp/eyedropper-live.png shows an empty green-ringed circle.
defects.mechanism: synchronous paint into a v-if element that Vue has not flushed to the DOM yet (mount/paint ordering race)
defects.reproduction: http://localhost:9000/#/extract → upload any image → click the preview to open the eyedropper → tap once WITHOUT moving the pointer first (i.e. any touch tap). The loupe appears and is empty; it never fills. Scripted: .playwright-mcp/probe2.js section A.
defects.proposedCure: Keep the loupe canvas permanently mounted and gate visibility on opacity/visibility instead of v-if. This kills the race by construction, lets the already-declared `.loupe { transition: opacity }` (ImageEyedropper.vue:270 — currently dead CSS) actually run, and removes a DOM create/destroy from the hover path. (`await nextTick()` before drawLoupe is the patch, not the cure.)

defects.defect: `justUnpinned` is a component-scope latch whose only exit is inside `onTap`; a drag never reaches `onTap`, so after pin → press-drag → release the flag stays true and the NEXT legitimate tap is silently swallowed.
defects.evidence: ImageEyedropper.vue:123 (`let justUnpinned = false`), :151-155 (onTap's only clear), :176-185 (capture-phase pointerdown sets it); useInertiaGesture.ts:277-281 (onTap fires only when !hasMoved). MEASURED (probe-eyedropper.js): tapRed buttons=3 (pinned) → afterDrag buttons=1 → tapTransparent_1st buttons=1 (TAP SWALLOWED) → tapTransparent_2nd buttons=3. Cross-check: Escape-unpin (:226-235) does NOT set the flag and the next tap pins immediately (probe2 A_afterEscape buttons 1 → A_tapNoHover buttons 3).
defects.mechanism: cross-handler boolean latch with a single clear site that one of two gesture terminations never reaches
defects.reproduction: Open the eyedropper, tap to pin a color, then press and drag (this unpins and pans), release, then tap somewhere new — the tap does nothing; a second tap is required. Scripted: .playwright-mcp/probe-eyedropper.js.
defects.proposedCure: Delete the flag and fold unpin into useInertiaGesture's own state machine, which already tracks hasMoved/isPanning. 'A pointerdown while pinned suppresses the pointerup that ends THIS gesture' has a definite lifetime inside the gesture; as a component-scope boolean it has none.

defects.defect: Alpha is discarded when sampling: `formatHex(data[0], data[1], data[2])` never reads `data[3]`, so a fully transparent pixel is reported — and emitted to the palette via `pick`/`addToPalette` — as opaque black.
defects.evidence: useImageSampler.ts:32-35 (formatHex) and :116-118 (getImageData → formatHex, data[3] unread); ImageEyedropper.vue:212-224 (emits sampledColor). MEASURED: sampling the fully-transparent quadrant of the 200×200 probe fixture yields readout `oklch(0% 0 none)` and a solid black WatercolorDot swatch (.playwright-mcp/eyedropper-live.png, top bar); sampledColor = "#000000".
defects.mechanism: lossy channel projection — RGBA sampled, RGB formatted, no alpha branch
defects.reproduction: Upload a PNG with a fully transparent region (fixture: .playwright-mcp/probe.png, bottom-right quadrant) and sample inside it. Readout: oklch(0% 0 none); swatch: black; Add-to-palette inserts #000000.
defects.proposedCure: Read data[3]. Either refuse the sample and return null — reusing the existing out-of-bounds 'no sample here' path at useImageSampler.ts:114-115 — or carry alpha through into the emitted color. Never project a non-existent pixel onto black.

defects.defect: The overlay is inoperable by keyboard and invisible to assistive technology: no role, no aria-modal, no accessible name, no aria-live readout, focus never moves in, no focus trap, no focus restoration; the sampling canvas is aria-hidden with no keyboard alternative; and Add/Apply only render after a pointer-only pin.
defects.evidence: MEASURED on the live overlay: role=null, aria-modal=null, aria-label=null, [role=dialog] count 0, [aria-live] count 0, focusables inside overlay = 1, document.activeElement = BODY on open, Tab #1 → INPUT with insideOverlay:false, Tab #2 → INPUT with insideOverlay:false. Code: ImageEyedropper.vue:8 (bare div overlay), :74 (canvas aria-hidden), :35-37 (readout span, no aria-live), :43-58 (Add/Apply v-if="pinned", pinned only set from onTap). Entry point also gated: ImageDropZone.vue:21 sets tabindex=-1 once a preview exists. WCAG 2.1.1 (A), 4.1.2 (A), 2.4.3 (A) all fail.
defects.mechanism: hand-rolled modal overlay with no dialog semantics and a pointer-only interaction model
defects.reproduction: Open the eyedropper, press Tab twice: focus lands on inputs OUTSIDE the overlay (measured insideOverlay:false both times). There is no key that samples a color, and Add/Apply never appear without a mouse click.
defects.proposedCure: Adopt the glass-ui dialog primitive instead of hand-rolling `absolute inset-0 z-popover glass-floating` (owner edict 4) — that supplies role/aria-modal/focus trap/restoration for free — then add an aria-live="polite" readout and an arrow-key sample cursor bound to the same sampleAt the pointer already uses.

defects.defect: A malformed/undecodable image produces two unhandled promise rejections (one of them an Event, not an Error) and leaves a dead overlay with no error state: the canvas keeps its default 300×150 size and the readout says 'Tap to sample' forever.
defects.evidence: useImageSampler.ts:72-75 (`img.onerror = reject` — rejects with an Event); ImageEyedropper.vue:200-204, 237-240, 247 (loadAndFit called as a floating promise from onMounted and from watch, no catch). MEASURED (probe3.js, uploading 38 bytes of text named bad.png): pageErrors ["InvalidStateError: The source image could not be decoded.", "Event"]; in-page unhandledrejection ["The source image could not be decoded.", "error"]; eyedropper {mounted:true, cvBacking:[300,150], transform:"translate(0px,0px) scale(1)", readout:"Tap to sample", errorUI:0}.
defects.mechanism: unguarded async boundary — rejection with a non-Error value into a floating promise, with no error state in the view model
defects.reproduction: printf 'not an image' > bad.png; upload it on /#/extract (FileReader succeeds so the preview zone appears), click the preview to open the eyedropper. Two unhandled rejections fire; the overlay shows an unsized 300×150 canvas and no error message.
defects.proposedCure: Reject with a real Error from loadImage, and give the shell an `imageError` ref rendered in the same destructive register the sibling already uses (ExtractWorkbench.vue:80-85), with the close button as the escape.

defects.defect: The ResizeObserver calls fitToViewport() unconditionally on every size change, which reassigns zoom and recentres pan — destroying the user's inspection zoom on any window resize, panel reflow, or mobile URL-bar show/hide.
defects.evidence: useInertiaGesture.ts:353-360 (ResizeObserver → fitToViewport) and :152-167 (fitToViewport assigns zoom.value = fit unconditionally). MEASURED (probe2 §C): ctrl-wheel zoom to 2.6924, then change the overlay height → zoom becomes 1.61. {"beforeZoom":2.6924,"afterZoom":1.61}
defects.mechanism: initialisation logic wired to a continuous reflow signal — no separation of 'fit once' from 'reflow, preserving state'
defects.reproduction: Open the eyedropper, ctrl-wheel to zoom in, then resize the window (or on mobile, scroll so the URL bar collapses). The zoom snaps back to fit. Scripted: .playwright-mcp/probe2.js section C.
defects.proposedCure: Split fit (one-time, called from loadAndFit/onTransitionEnd where the component already calls it) from reflow (preserve the zoom ratio and the image-space centre point, then re-clamp pan). The ResizeObserver should only ever call the latter.

defects.defect: Transparent image pixels composite the page behind the translucent glass overlay, so the color the user SEES at a coordinate is (page ⊕ glass tint ⊕ image) while sampleAt returns the raw image pixel — a color instrument that displays a different color than it samples.
defects.evidence: useImageSampler.ts:84,91 (drawImage onto a transparent canvas); ImageEyedropper.vue:8 (glass-floating translucent overlay), :62-75 (no opaque backing in the viewport). VISUAL: .playwright-mcp/eyedropper-live.png — in the transparent quadrant you can read the k-slider, the reset control, and the 'DOMINANT oklch(45.20…718…)' readout of the panel BEHIND the overlay, straight through the image.
defects.mechanism: no opaque ground under an alpha-bearing specimen inside a translucent chrome layer
defects.reproduction: Upload a PNG with transparency (.playwright-mcp/probe.png) and open the eyedropper: the transparent quadrant shows the workbench underneath, not the image. Screenshot at .playwright-mcp/eyedropper-live.png.
defects.proposedCure: Paint an opaque ground under the image inside the viewport — the conventional alpha checkerboard, or the stage token the workbench already owns (bg-stage, ExtractWorkbench.vue:37) — so the specimen is composited against a known, declared background.

defects.defect: Both the offscreen sampling canvas and the visible canvas are sized to the image's NATURAL dimensions, and the visible one carries will-change:transform, permanently promoting a full-resolution compositor layer for the life of the overlay.
defects.evidence: useImageSampler.ts:80-92 (both canvases sized to naturalWidth/naturalHeight); ImageEyedropper.vue:71 (will-change-transform); useImageSampler.ts:97-101 (dispose nulls refs but never zeroes canvas.width). MEASURED (probe2 §D, 4000×3000 fixture): {"cvBacking":[4000,3000],"bytesVisibleCanvas":48000000,"totalCanvasBytesMin":96000000,"willChange":"transform","dataUrlChars":69926,"mem":{"usedMB":95}}.
defects.mechanism: unbounded backing-store allocation driven by user input, duplicated, plus forced layer promotion
defects.reproduction: Upload a 4000×3000 image (fixture .playwright-mcp/big.png) and open the eyedropper: 48 MB visible canvas backing store in a promoted GPU layer plus a 48 MB offscreen copy, on top of the decoded image and the base64 data URL held by useExtractSession.previewDataUrl.
defects.proposedCure: The visible canvas exists only to be transformed under the loupe and does not need native resolution — cap it to the viewport's device-pixel budget and keep native resolution only in the never-composited offscreen sampling canvas. Replace the static will-change with promotion only during an active gesture (gestureActive is already tracked and already drives a class at ImageEyedropper.vue:72).

defects.defect: The test gate is vacuous: the only test file (31 lines, 3 tests) exercises exactly one pure function, formatInColorSpace, on a sampler built with canvasRef: ref(null). Every defect in this report — including both BLOCKERs — lives in code no test executes.
defects.evidence: test/image-sampler-v4.test.ts (whole file, 31 lines). `npx vitest run test/image-sampler-v4.test.ts --reporter=basic` → "✓ test/image-sampler-v4.test.ts (3 tests) 2ms / Test Files 1 passed (1) / Tests 3 passed (3)". Coverage grep: `grep -rln "ImageEyedropper|useImageSampler|useLoupeCanvas|useInertiaGesture"` over test/ → one file; over e2e/ → only a prose comment at e2e/smoke/oracles/o7-card-census.spec.ts:16.
defects.mechanism: tests bound to the one pure, already-correct leaf while all stateful/DOM behaviour is untested
defects.reproduction: Named green-keeping mutations: (1) viewportToImage → return {ix:0,iy:0}; (2) sampleAt → return null; (3) formatHex → return '#000000'; (4) delete the bounds check at useImageSampler.ts:114-115; (5) delete useLoupeCanvas.ts entirely; (6) delete useInertiaGesture.ts entirely; (7) loadImage → throw on every input. All seven keep 3/3 green.
defects.proposedCure: Both composables are already injectable (useImageSampler takes a canvasRef; useLoupeCanvas takes getOffscreenCanvas + viewportToImage). A jsdom/happy-dom test feeding a real 2×2 ImageData and asserting sampleAt at four corners + one out-of-bounds + one alpha-0 pixel fails on every mutation above and would have caught D-3. Once the unpin latch lives inside the gesture composable (D-2's cure), the tap state machine becomes a pure unit test.

defects.defect: devicePixelRatio is ignored — the loupe canvas backing store is a hardcoded 110×110 regardless of DPR, so the deliberately crisp (imageSmoothingEnabled=false) pixel grid is bilinearly upsampled by the compositor. LOUPE_SIZE also has two sources of truth: the constant drives the CSS and the draw math, but the canvas attributes are literals.
defects.evidence: ImageEyedropper.vue:85 (`width="110" height="110"` literals); constants.ts:8 (LOUPE_SIZE = 110) used at ImageEyedropper.vue:191-196 and useLoupeCanvas.ts:35-51; useLoupeCanvas.ts:40 (imageSmoothingEnabled = false). `grep -n "devicePixelRatio|dpr"` over the ImageEyedropper directory → no matches. MEASURED at devicePixelRatio 2: loupe canvas {"backing":[110,110],"cssW":106} → 212 device pixels rendered from a 110-pixel backing store, a 1.93× upsample.
defects.mechanism: fixed-pixel backing store on a device-pixel-scaled display; duplicated dimension constant
defects.reproduction: Open the eyedropper on any retina display (probe measured devicePixelRatio: 2) and inspect the loupe canvas: backing 110×110, CSS box 106 px, 212 device px. The magnified pixel edges are smeared by the compositor.
defects.proposedCure: :width="LOUPE_SIZE * dpr" / :height="LOUPE_SIZE * dpr" with ctx.scale(dpr, dpr) in drawLoupe, and no literal dimensions anywhere — one constant, one truth.

defects.defect: The readout has unbounded precision, uses a different precision policy from the sibling format path, and is rendered in a `truncate` span with no `title` — violating the invariant the neighbouring component in the same workbench documents and follows.
defects.evidence: MEASURED readout for pure red: `oklch(62.795536392143% 0.257683303805 29.233880279628deg)` (55 chars, 12 decimal places). useImageSampler.ts:38-44 rounds library-space channels to 4 dp (`hsv` → `HSV 0 · 1 · 1`) while :63-65 hands CSS spaces to serializePickerColor unrounded. ImageEyedropper.vue:35-37 is `<span class="... truncate select-all">` with no title; contrast ExtractWorkbench.vue:134-141 which states 'the full readout rides title + select-all (never a lying readout)' and sets :title on its truncated readout.
defects.mechanism: two divergent formatting policies behind one readout slot, plus lossy visual truncation with no full-value affordance
defects.reproduction: Sample any saturated color with colorSpace=oklch: the readout is 55 characters at 12 decimals and is visually clipped by `truncate` with no hover title to recover the full value.
defects.proposedCure: One precision policy for both branches (round CSS-space channels the same way formatLibraryColor already rounds library-space channels), and put :title on the readout span so the truncated value is recoverable — exactly as the sibling does.

defects.defect: The capture-phase pointerdown listener is registered inside a watcher and never removed — no onWatcherCleanup, no unbind, and no counterpart in onBeforeUnmount, in a file whose own composable models the symmetric bind/unbind pattern.
defects.evidence: ImageEyedropper.vue:176-185 (addEventListener with {capture:true}, no cleanup); contrast useInertiaGesture.ts:337-344 (unbind) and :362-368 (onBeforeUnmount). ImageEyedropper.vue:242-245 removes the keydown listener and calls sampler.dispose() but knows nothing about this one.
defects.mechanism: asymmetric listener registration inside a reactive effect with no cleanup callback
defects.reproduction: NONE — code-level defect. Bounded in practice by the element becoming collectable on unmount, but it will double-register if viewportRef ever re-resolves within a single component lifetime.
defects.proposedCure: This listener exists only to implement the unpin latch (D-2). Removing it entirely — by folding unpin into the gesture composable, which already owns symmetric bind/unbind — cures both defects at once.

defects.defect: loadImage has no re-entrancy guard, generation token, or abort; onMounted and watch(() => imageUrl) both fire loadAndFit() as floating promises, so two overlapping loads both write imgWidth/imgHeight/offscreenCanvas and the last to DECODE wins rather than the last requested.
defects.evidence: useImageSampler.ts:68-95 (loadImage — no token, no abort, writes shared state after an await); ImageEyedropper.vue:200-204 (loadAndFit), :237-240 (onMounted, unawaited), :247 (watch, unawaited).
defects.mechanism: unsequenced async writes to shared state — classic last-writer-by-latency race
defects.reproduction: NONE — labelled a hypothesis. Reasoned from the code: change the image twice in quick succession (upload then camera capture) and the eyedropper can display, and sample, the wrong image. I did not construct the timing race in the browser.
defects.proposedCure: Give loadImage a monotonic generation token captured before the await and checked after it (or an AbortController), and drop the result if a newer load has started.

defects.defect: Wheel panning applies each delta directly AND seeds an inertia coast from the same delta, restarting the rAF coast on every wheel event; macOS trackpad momentum keeps delivering wheel events for ~1s, so the net pan should exceed the physical scroll distance.
defects.evidence: useInertiaGesture.ts:310-320 — `panX.value -= e.deltaX` (direct) followed by `velocityX = -e.deltaX * 0.3; startInertia();` (coast) in the same handler; startInertia (:131-142) stop/start-cycles the loop on every event.
defects.mechanism: double integration of one input signal — OS-supplied momentum plus author-supplied momentum
defects.reproduction: NONE — hypothesis, reasoned from the code, not measured. Two-finger scroll on a macOS trackpad inside the eyedropper viewport should overshoot.
defects.proposedCure: Wheel deltas are already positional; do not seed velocity from them at all. Reserve the coast for pointer-drag release, which is the one gesture the OS does not already provide momentum for.

defects.defect: The visual audit never renders this component, so its zero-defect record on /#/extract is vacuous — the overlay only mounts after a pointer click that follows an upload, which the capture harness never performs.
defects.evidence: docs/tranches/V/megatranche/audit/visual/REPORT.json, /#/extract, all four Safari matrices: counts.canvas = 1 (the atmosphere field only — the eyedropper's two canvases are absent). shots/zoom-200-desktop/ contains adminusers, blob, browse, gradient, picker — no extract. The 3 namelessButtons and 6 smallTapTargets recorded on /#/extract are other components' (JSON lists input 160×23, three 22×22 buttons 'Switch to slug'/'Generate new slug'/'Cancel', two span 12×24 slider labels). ExtractWorkbench.vue:25,173-180 shows the pointer-gated mount.
defects.mechanism: capture harness reaches only default route state; interaction-gated overlays are structurally invisible to it
defects.reproduction: grep the REPORT.json rows for /#/extract: canvas count is 1 in every matrix, and no eyedropper element appears in any a11y row.
defects.proposedCure: Add an interaction-state pass to the visual harness for pointer-gated overlays (upload a fixture, open the overlay, capture), or the component's a11y defects (D-4) remain permanently outside the gate.

defects.defect: Owner-edict deltas: the modal overlay is hand-rolled rather than adopting a glass-ui dialog primitive (edict 4 — and this hand-roll is the direct cause of D-4's missing semantics), and the icon hover tint reaches into a glass-ui DockControl's slot content from the consumer via a descendant selector plus a per-instance inline CSS var (edict 5).
defects.evidence: ImageEyedropper.vue:8 (`absolute inset-0 z-popover flex flex-col glass-floating rounded-panel` — hand-rolled overlay, no dialog primitive); :279-282 (`.eyedropper-action-btn:hover:not(:disabled) svg { color: var(--hover-color); transform: scale(1.2) }`); :10 (`:style="{ '--hover-color': sampledColor ?? '' }"` inline per-instance var). Edicts 1, 2, 3, 6, 7, 8 all PASS — verified: every type-only import is `import type`/inline `type` (ImageEyedropper.vue:99, useImageSampler.ts:11-19, useInertiaGesture.ts:1); useTemplateRef throughout; no defineModel, so the stale-read hazard does not apply.
defects.mechanism: design-system responsibilities implemented at the consumer instead of in glass-ui
defects.reproduction: NONE — structural/edict finding, read directly from the cited lines.
defects.proposedCure: Adopt the glass-ui dialog primitive for the overlay (which also cures D-4 for free), and move 'icon tints to the active color on hover' into DockControl as a variant plus a token, rather than a demo-side descendant selector over the design system's slot content.

result.axis: CHALLENGE-D — design (visual truth, state coverage, motion, design-system boundary, proportion & seat law)
result.modelObserved: Opus 5 (claude-opus-5[1m], 1M-context variant) — explicitly declared for this seat, not inherited.
result.strongestDefect: D-01 — a collapsed interval row paints ZERO focus pixels when focused. `overflow-hidden` on the row (GradientEasingEditor.vue:114) clips a box-shadow-only focus ring (`outline:none` + `box-shadow: var(--focus-ring-shadow)`, lines 228-231) whose head button is flush with the clip rect on all four sides when the disclosure panel is `display:none`. Measured by pixel diff against a byte-identical unclipped control: shipped case delta = 0 px, control delta = +4352 px. With N stops there are N-1 rows and at most one open, so N-2 rows are permanently focus-invisible; the 2-stop default is why every existing capture missed it.
result.negativeProof: Not applicable (verdict is DEFECTIVE), but the report records a full negative-results table so the next seat does not re-spend budget: `--motion-accent` glyph ink measures 5.90:1 on the rail well and 6.23:1 on the plate (floored by construction via useSafeAccentFn("resting"), useSpecimenRows.ts:40,69); muted literal on well 5.08:1; the dark/light well material step is correctly quiet in both schemes (light plate L=0.545 vs rail L=0.608; dark plate L=0.103 vs rail L=0.079); prefers-reduced-motion IS covered by the global guard at demo/styles/animations.css:184-192; the "missing empty state" is not a defect because useGradientModel.ts:83,123 guarantees >=1 interval; overflowX is 0 and pageErrors/consoleErrors are [] on /#/gradient in all four matrices; verbatimModuleSyntax and Vue 3.5 reactive-props-destructure are compliant; the six harness small-tap-target rows on /#/gradient belong to the dock and stop seats, not this component.

defects.defect: A focused collapsed interval row has no visible focus indicator at all: the row's `overflow-hidden` clips a box-shadow-only focus ring whose element is flush with the clip rect on all four sides.
defects.evidence: demo/workbenches/gradient/GradientVisualizer/GradientEasingEditor.vue:114 (`rounded-card border border-card-edge overflow-hidden`) + :228-231 (`outline:none; box-shadow: var(--focus-ring-shadow)`) + :144 (`v-show`). Live measurement at 1512x806: row rect x=224 w=462 h=197.45 overflow:hidden border 1px; head rect x=225 w=460 h=38.95 -> inset left/right/top = exactly 1.00px; computed box-shadow = '...0.3) 0px 0px 0px 2px, ...0.15) 0px 0px 8px 0px'. Pixel diff of two device-scale screenshots of frames/repro.html: `changed px: 21648, bbox x: 1027 1968 y: 92 177` (case B region only; case A byte-identical). Ring px outside head box: A focused = 3584, A control = 3584 (delta 0); B focused = 7936, B control = 3584 (delta +4352).
defects.mechanism: clipping-container-vs-outside-painted-focus-indicator (outline:none + box-shadow ring inside overflow:hidden)
defects.reproduction: docs/tranches/V/megatranche/audit/components/wb-gradient-easingeditor/frames/repro.html served over http; focus case A's `.interval-head` and screenshot, focus case B's and screenshot; diff. Artifacts kept at frames/D-01-focus-A-clipped-0px.png and frames/D-01-focus-B-control-4352px.png. In-app: any gradient with >=3 stops leaves >=1 collapsed row; tab to it.
defects.proposedCure: Delete the hand-rolled disclosure and seat glass-ui 7's `Collapsible` (which owns its own trigger/content boxes, focus register and reduced-motion carve-out). The per-row card box and its clip should go entirely (see D-07) — the composition's binding boundary inventory is `none`, so the clip has no job. Do not merely swap box-shadow for outline.

defects.defect: The named-curve selection surface hides 70.6% of itself on desktop and 79.9% on mobile, and renders a family divider hairline against a family it does not draw.
defects.evidence: Live probe at 1512x806: `tiles: 27, families: 8, familyNames: [css,sine,quad,cubic,expo,circ,back,steps], visibleTiles: 8, scrollW: 1482, clientW: 436` -> 70.6% hidden, 2 of 8 families visible. At 390x664: `scrollW 1482, clientW 298` -> 79.9% hidden. Divider source: EasingSpecimenStrip.vue:145-148 `.strip-family + .strip-family { border-left: 1px solid var(--card-edge) }`, visible as a bare rule at the strip's right edge in shots/safari-desktop-light/gradient.png and shots/keyboard-focus-desktop/gradient.png; in shots/rtl-desktop/gradient.png the same edge truncates the eyebrow to the fragment 'ad' (from 'quad'). The mega-tranche harness's own `bleeding` list for /#/gradient (REPORT.json) is exclusively strip nodes: strip-row, strip-family, family-eyebrow, family-tiles, glass-chip.glass-capsule, tile-label.
defects.mechanism: one-axis flattening of a two-axis catalogue into a horizontally-overflowing rail inside a narrow inspector
defects.reproduction: Load http://localhost:9000/#/gradient at 1512x806; read document.querySelector('.specimen-strip').scrollWidth / .clientWidth and document.querySelectorAll('.specimen-tile').length.
defects.proposedCure: Restore the two-axis IA the strip deliberately folded away (EasingSpecimenStrip.vue:141 'compactness: no second control row'): a family selector plus that family's variants at full column width, or wrap to a grid inside the 436px column. Not 'add a scrollbar'.

defects.defect: In RTL the row's interval label inverts to `2 -> 1`, contradicting the eased-ramp specimen rendered 20px below it; ordinals/CSS literals are not LTR-isolated as the constitution requires.
defects.evidence: useSpecimenRows.ts:62 mints `label: `${i + 1} → ${i + 2}`` as a bare string; GradientEasingEditor.vue:124 renders it with no isolation. shots/rtl-desktop/gradient.png: the head reads `linear / (dots) 2 → 1` while the ramp beneath still runs green->blue (stop1->stop2), and the endpoint dot pair has also reversed. result.axis: CHALLENGE-C — implementation defect hunt: demo/workbenches/gradient/GradientVisualizer/GradientEasingEditor.vue (+ easing/ children and gradient composables)
result.modelObserved: Opus 5 (claude-opus-5[1m], 1M-context variant) — the model this seat was explicitly spawned with; declared, not inherited.
result.strongestDefect: C-1 — Pressing any of the three `back`-family specimen tiles (ease-in-back / ease-out-back / ease-in-out-back — 3 of 27 tiles, in the default-open row on arrival) throws `Gradient color mix failed: color_progress_out_of_range` and replaces the ENTIRE Gradient pane with the ErrorBoundary. Overshoot easings produce f(t) outside [0,1] by construction (measured 18–21 of 33 samples out of range); `mixColors` rejects progress outside [0,1] (src/color/operations.ts:88) and three unclamped call sites feed it directly. Dragging the picker's own control point above y=1 reproduces it too — the producer's sr-only text advertises a y range of −0.6..1.6, 2.2× wider than the consumer can survive.
result.negativeProof: N/A — verdict is DEFECTIVE. (Hazards checked and found ABSENT, recorded in the report so the next seat need not re-spend the probes: (1) the copy state machine is SOUND — glass-ui/dist/useClipboard-D36OTaeT.js:41 sets status="pending" synchronously before its first await, so the apparent cross-row false-tick between `copiedIndex.value = index` and `await copy(css)` cannot be observed by any render; (2) no defineModel in this component — no WritableComputedRef stale-read hazard; (3) no rAF LOOP — the two requestAnimationFrame calls are one-shots that never reschedule, so this is not a PRM-RAF epidemic site; (4) no ValueUnit wrapping; (5) no reka-ui slider in this subtree; (6) no WebGL/canvas, nothing on the critical path; (7) verbatimModuleSyntax clean — all 8 type-only imports across the 4 files use `import type`; (8) not a god module (295 lines with a genuine easing/ extraction); (9) the route's single nameless button is a .dock-icon-button, `closest("[id^='easing-interval-'], .interval-head")` === false — this component contributes ZERO nameless buttons; (10) the route's 6 small tap targets all belong to the dock slug controls and GradientStopEditor handles, none to this component; (11) closed accordion rows are display:none so the ~27-name-per-row duplication is invisible to AT.)

defects.defect: Pressing any `back`-family specimen tile — or dragging a picker control point outside y∈[0,1] — throws and destroys the whole Gradient pane. 3 of 27 catalogue tiles are a live crash in the default app state.
defects.evidence: Probe output: `ease-out-back  rails=[] CRASH=["This panel hit an unexpected error.Gradient color mix failed: color_progress_out_of_range Try again"]` — same for ease-in-back and ease-in-out-back; linear/ease/steps/step-start/step-end/ease-in-out-expo all CRASH=no. Guard: src/color/operations.ts:88 `if (progress < 0 || progress > 1) return err({ code: "color_progress_out_of_range" });`. Unclamped call sites: demo/workbenches/gradient/composables/useGradientCSS.ts:199-208 (sampleCoalescedStops), demo/workbenches/gradient/GradientVisualizer/easing/useSpecimenRows.ts:52-59 (fn(0.5)), demo/workbenches/gradient/GradientVisualizer.vue:78-85 (colorAtPosition). Measured ranges on the real sampling grid (vite-node against src/subpaths/easing): ease-in-back min=-0.0969 out-of-range 18/33 fn(0.5)=-0.0636; ease-out-back max=1.0868 out-of-range 19/33 fn(0.5)=1.0676; ease-in-out-back min=-0.0923 max=1.0927 out-of-range 21/33. Drag repro: `AFTER DRAG: {"literal":null,"crash":["...color_progress_out_of_range..."]}`. Catalogue built by blind enumeration: easingCatalogue.ts:178 `for (const name of Object.keys(bezierPresets))` with no compatibility filter; GradientEasingEditor.vue:73-76 emits with no validation.
defects.mechanism: missing-domain-boundary: an easing callable's output (a motion value, unbounded) is fed straight into a color-mix progress parameter (a ratio strictly on [0,1]) at three separate sites, with no clamp at the sampling law that owns the domain.
defects.reproduction: 1. open http://localhost:9000/#/gradient (easing row `1 → 2` is open on arrival). 2. click the `back` family's `out` tile (`[data-specimen='ease-out-back']`). 3. the entire pane is replaced by the ErrorBoundary reading "This panel hit an unexpected error. Gradient color mix failed: color_progress_out_of_range". Scripted: node scratchpad/wbge-probe4.mjs ease-out-back ease-in-back ease-in-out-back. Recoverable via "Try again" (probe 7: crash 1 → 0, heads back to 1) but all pane state is lost.
defects.proposedCure: Progress into a color mix is a ratio on [0,1] and the sampling law is the ONE place that owns it. Add a private `rampProgress = (t) => Math.min(1, Math.max(0, t))` in useGradientCSS and route sampleCoalescedStops' easedT, useSpecimenRows' fn(0.5) and colorAtPosition's easedT through it — matching CSS's own behaviour (an overshoot timing function on a <color> interpolation clamps to the endpoint colour). The overshoot stays visible where it belongs: in the glyph, which samples the raw callable and needs no clamp, and in the authoring canvas. Do NOT delete the back family — the curves are legitimate and the picker authors them freely; the defect is the missing domain boundary, not the curves.

defects.defect: The component's own stated "zero letterbox" law (O-17 clause 1) is dead code against glass-ui 7.0.0: the picker renders `svg[role="group"]`, not `role="img"`, so `syncVbRatio` no-ops forever and all three `:deep(svg[role="img"])` declarations select nothing. 59.4% of the authoring canvas renders nothing.
defects.evidence: EasingAuthoringStage.vue:47-53 queries `svg[role='img']`; :104-115 styles `:deep(svg[role="img"])` with !important. Measured live DOM (probe 5, #easing-authoring-0): `{"svgs":[{"role":"group","aria":"Easing curve 1 → 2","viewBox":"0 -0.1 1 1.2000000000000002","box":{"w":410,"h":200}}],"stageStyleAttr":"--vb-ratio: 1.2;"}` — role is "group". Measured geometry via the oracle's own getScreenCTM method (probe 6): `{"elementBox":{"w":410,"h":200},"drawnPlot":{"w":166.7,"h":200},"letterbox":{"left":121.7,"right":121.7,"top":0,"bottom":0},"vbRatioVar":"1.2","svgComputed":{"aspectRatio":"1 / 1","blockSize":"200px"}}` — computed aspect-ratio is the PRODUCER's inline `1 / 1`, not the seat's `calc(1/1.2)`; block-size is the producer's 200px clamp, not the seat's `auto`. O-17 requires ≤1px on all four edges; measured 121.7px on two. Laws 1 and 2 DO still hold (gridCols "436px", cardShadow "none", cardBackdrop "none") — only the role-keyed law broke, and it broke with no console error, no type error, no exception.
defects.mechanism: brittle-producer-dom-coupling: a consumer reaches into a producer's private DOM (an ARIA role attribute) to correct the producer's geometry, and hand-rolls a rAF mirror of state the producer already owns. The glass-ui 7.0.0 adopt changed the role; the coupling failed open and silent.
defects.reproduction: 1. open http://localhost:9000/#/gradient. 2. press the sliders icon in the readout rail (`aria-label="Author a custom curve"`). 3. inspect `#easing-authoring-0 svg` — role="group", inline style `aspect-ratio: 1 / 1; block-size: clamp(200px, 38cqi, 320px)`. 4. its viewBox is 1×1.2 with preserveAspectRatio=xMidYMid meet in a 410×200 box → drawn plot 166.7×200 centred, 121.7px dead on each side. Scripted: node scratchpad/wbge-probe5.mjs and wbge-probe6.mjs.
defects.proposedCure: Retire the seat override entirely and take the geometry from glass-ui: the picker should expose its live viewBox ratio as a custom property on its own root (a `--easing-vb-ratio` alongside the `--easing-curve-accent` it already stamps, observed in the live DOM) and size its canvas from it. The component header already books this — "the overrides retire at the P7 adopt" — and the adopt has landed (@mkbabb/glass-ui@7.0.0 installed, W44 closed); this is the glass-ui-first edict, the fix belongs upstream. If the producer packet cannot land now, the interim seat must not be able to break in silence: bind to the stable contract (`[data-testid="easing-picker"] svg[viewBox]`) AND make the miss loud — syncVbRatio should console.error on a failed query rather than `return`, so the next producer bump surfaces on first boot instead of in an audit two tranches later.
