defects.mechanism: vacuous-gate: the only tests that exercise this component live in a browser suite that CI never invokes; the unit suite that CI does invoke has zero coverage of it.
defects.reproduction: npx playwright test e2e/smoke/oracles/o17-easing-composition.spec.ts --project=smoke  → 3 failed. npx playwright test e2e/smoke/views/gradient.spec.ts --project=smoke -g "easing row carries its live ramp"  → 1 failed. grep -rn "e2e|playwright" .github/workflows/  → empty. Mutation that keeps every CI gate green: invert glyphPath's `const y = 1 - fn(t)` to `const y = fn(t)` (easingCatalogue.ts:69) — every portrait in the catalogue and every head glyph renders upside down and lint, tsc, build and vitest are all unchanged. So is shipping C-1.
defects.proposedCure: An e2e suite that is not in the pipeline is not a gate. Add a `demo / e2e` job to .github/workflows/ci.yml running `npx playwright install --with-deps chromium webkit` + `npx playwright test`, and fix the two stale assertions (the O-17 role selector, the steps(4, end) → steps(4, jump-end) literal) in the same wave so the job lands green. Until then, read the O-17 GREEN claims in the record as aspiration, not certification.

defects.defect: Interval identity is positional: inserting a stop mid-ramp silently re-hosts every downstream authored curve onto a different colour pair, and the accordion's index-keyed disclosure state follows the index rather than the interval.
defects.evidence: Reproduced (probe 9): BEFORE insert `{"heads":["1 → 2linear","2 → 3ease-in-out-expo"],"stops":["0%","50%","100%"],"open":["easing-interval-1"],"tune":["false","true"]}` — ease-in-out-expo authored for 50%→100%. AFTER inserting a stop at 24%: `{"heads":["1 → 2linear","2 → 3ease-in-out-expo","3 → 4linear"],"stops":["0%","24%","50%","100%"],"open":["easing-interval-1"],"tune":["false","true","false"]}` — the curve is still on row `2 → 3`, which now means 24%→50%; the interval it was authored for is now `3 → 4`, reset to linear. Mechanism: useGradientModel.ts:89-100 the sync watch is append/truncate-only (`while (intervals.value.length < needed) intervals.value.push(linearInterval())`) and only observes `stops.value.length`, while addStop (:116-120) inserts positionally sorted and removeStop (:122-125) filters by id. GradientEasingEditor keys ALL its own state on the same ordinal: openInterval (:61), tuneOpen (:84), copiedIndex (:95), the DOM ids `easing-interval-${row.index}` (:145) / `easing-authoring-${row.index}` (:205), the v-for :key (:113), and the update-interval emit (:49).
defects.mechanism: positional-identity: per-item state keyed on an array ordinal over a list whose items are inserted and removed in the middle, so identity shifts silently under every non-tail edit.
defects.reproduction: node scratchpad/wbge-probe9.mjs — or manually: 1. open /#/gradient. 2. click the stop bar at 50% (3 stops, 2 intervals). 3. open row `2 → 3` and press the `expo in-out` specimen tile. 4. click the stop bar at 25%. 5. row `2 → 3` still reads ease-in-out-expo but now spans 24%→50%; the 50%→100% interval you authored is now row `3 → 4`, linear.
defects.proposedCure: Give the interval a stable identity derived from the pair it spans, not from its ordinal. Stops already carry uid() (useGradientModel.ts:66-69) — hold intervals in a Map<string, GradientInterval> keyed on the LEFT stop's id. Insertion then splits an interval instead of shifting a list: the new stop's key gets a fresh linearInterval(), every existing key keeps its curve, removal drops exactly one entry. GradientEasingEditor keys its accordion, disclosure, v-for :key, DOM ids and emit on that same id — which also fixes the v-for :key="row.index" that currently makes Vue reuse row DOM across a shift, the reason the disclosure appears to 'stick' to the wrong interval.

defects.defect: Every accordion row mounts in full — specimen strip and a live EasingPicker — although the accordion can display exactly one row at a time; ~75% of the mounted DOM is permanently display:none.
defects.evidence: Row body is v-show (GradientEasingEditor.vue:144); the authoring stage's v-if (:208) guards only `intervals[row.index]`, always truthy. Measured (probes 1 and 2, Chromium 1440×900, /#/gradient): 2 stops / 1 interval → allElements 511, buttons 53, [data-specimen] 27, easing-picker 1, visible rows 1. 5 stops / 4 intervals → allElements 1109, buttons 149, [data-specimen] 108, easing-picker 4, visible rows STILL 1. Delta +598 elements, +96 buttons, +81 hidden tile buttons, +3 fully-wired hidden EasingPicker instances (each with drag handlers and its own curve sampling), plus one useMediaQuery matchMedia subscription per strip (EasingSpecimenStrip.vue:47). Cost on an unrelated interaction, 120 ArrowRight presses on the Direction slider, CDP Performance.getMetrics deltas (probe 8): 1 interval `{scriptMs 13.9, layoutMs 20.7, recalcMs 191.6}` vs 4 intervals `{scriptMs 16.9, layoutMs 26.1, recalcMs 258.0}` → script/tick 0.116ms → 0.141ms (+22%), style recalc +34.7%, layout +26%.
defects.mechanism: eager-mount: a v-show accordion mounts the bodies of rows that have never been disclosed, so mount cost scales with item count rather than with disclosure.
defects.reproduction: node scratchpad/wbge-probe2.mjs — or manually: open /#/gradient, click the stop bar at 25%, 50% and 75%, then run in the console `({elements: document.querySelectorAll('*').length, pickers: document.querySelectorAll('[data-testid="easing-picker"]').length, tiles: document.querySelectorAll('[data-specimen]').length, visibleRows: [...document.querySelectorAll("[id^='easing-interval-']")].filter(e=>getComputedStyle(e).display!=='none').length})` → {elements: 1109, pickers: 4, tiles: 108, visibleRows: 1}.
defects.proposedCure: Keep the alive-once-opened property without the eager fan-out. The v-show choice is documented (:16-18, 'Picker instances stay ALIVE … no remount/echo discipline') and is right for the OPEN row, but does not justify mounting rows never opened. Wrap the existing v-show in `v-if="everOpened.has(row.id)"` — a Set populated by toggleInterval — which gives exactly the stated invariant (no remount, no echo) at one-row cost on arrival. Give the authoring stage the same treatment keyed on tuneOpen: a user who never presses the sliders icon should never pay for an EasingPicker.

defects.defect: The specimen rows and the open interval's ramp recompute on `type` and `direction` changes, neither of which can affect either — the whole per-row derivation (49-sample glyph, colour parse+mix, 27-tile scan, WCAG floor walk) re-runs on every direction-slider tick.
defects.evidence: useSpecimenRows.ts:42-72 reads `modelState()` wholesale; useGradientModel.ts:102-109 rebuilds modelState whenever ANY of type/direction/stops/intervals/interpolationSpace/hueMethod changes. openIntervalRamp (GradientEasingEditor.vue:63-67) likewise re-runs a full sampleCoalescedStops (2 parseColorIn + 33 mixColors) per direction tick. Cost per row per recompute: glyphPath = 49 easing evals + 98 toFixed(3) + string build, measured 13.2 µs/call (`glyphPath(48) x20000 = 265.0ms` via vite-node against the real src/subpaths/easing); plus interpolateStopColors; plus tileIdFor's linear scan over 27 tiles; plus safeCss → certifyAccentInk's WCAG floor walk. Observed coupling: +22% script/tick when interval count goes 1→4 during a direction drag (probe 8, C-5 evidence). Tell-tale: serializeIntervalRamp already hardcodes `type: "linear", direction: 90` in its sub-model (useGradientCSS.ts:243-244) — it demonstrably does not want those fields.
defects.mechanism: over-broad-reactive-dependency: a monolithic modelState object serves as both the serializer's input and the reactivity graph, so consumers that need four of its six fields subscribe to all six.
defects.reproduction: node scratchpad/wbge-probe8.mjs (drives 120 ArrowRight presses on [role='slider'] and reads CDP ScriptDuration/RecalcStyleDuration deltas at 1 vs 4 intervals; the ratio scales with interval count even though direction cannot affect any interval).
defects.proposedCure: modelState is doing double duty. Pass the specimen derivation only what it consumes: useSpecimenRows(() => stops, () => intervals, () => interpolationSpace, () => hueMethod). type/direction then cannot reach it. Apply the same narrowing to serializeIntervalRamp, which already discards them.

defects.defect: A failed clipboard write is completely silent, and a successful one is never announced — the CopyResult is discarded, no onCopyError is passed, and the route has zero aria-live regions.
defects.evidence: GradientEasingEditor.vue:100-103 `async function copyLiteral(index, css) { copiedIndex.value = index; await copy(css); }` — the typed `{ ok: false, reason: "clipboard-api" | "no-api" }` return (glass-ui useClipboard.d.ts) is thrown away and no onCopyError option is supplied; on failure the button silently keeps the Copy glyph and the only trace is a console.warn inside glass-ui. Confirmation is an aria-label swap on the button that already has focus (:181 `copiedRow === row.index ? 'Copied' : \`Copy ${row.css}\``) — not reliably announced by any major screen reader. Measured (probe 1): `document.querySelectorAll("[aria-live]").length === 0` on /#/gradient. The house idiom exists elsewhere: demo/palettes/browser/admin/PaginationBar.vue:17 aria-live="polite" aria-atomic, demo/color-picker/ErrorBoundary.vue:20 role="alert".
defects.mechanism: discarded-result + unannounced-async-state: an async operation's typed failure channel is dropped on the floor, and its success is signalled only by mutating the accessible name of the focused control.
defects.reproduction: NONE for the failure branch (would require revoking clipboard permission) — the discarded CopyResult and absent onCopyError are established by reading GradientEasingEditor.vue:100-103 against the glass-ui type surface. The zero-live-region measurement IS reproduced: open /#/gradient and run `document.querySelectorAll('[aria-live]').length` → 0.
defects.proposedCure: One polite live region per bench, owned by the editor root, fed by the EXISTING copyStatus: success → "Copied <literal>", failure → "Copy failed — clipboard unavailable". One node, no new component, no new shared/ directory; it covers the silent failure and the unannounced success on the same wire.

defects.defect: The seat styles the producer's private internals across a version boundary — three :deep() blocks, two !important declarations, a hardcoded .fading-scroll DOM contract — all booked as temporary overrides that the glass-ui 7 adopt was to retire; one of the three is now dead code that silently drops the component's stated invariant.
defects.evidence: EasingAuthoringStage.vue:88 `:deep([data-testid="easing-picker"])`, :93 `:deep(.glass-card)`, :104 `:deep(svg[role="img"])` with `block-size: auto !important` and `aspect-ratio: … !important`; header comment :20-21 "each recorded on the P7 EasingPicker-v2 packet; the overrides retire at the adopt". EasingSpecimenStrip.vue:60 `el?.closest<HTMLElement>(".fading-scroll")` — a hardcoded producer class. Adopt has landed: `node -p "require('./node_modules/@mkbabb/glass-ui/package.json').version"` → 7.0.0. The third override is dead (see C-2). .fading-scroll does still exist in glass-ui 7 (dist/fading-scroll-DhxXIhm2.js:84 emits `class: ["fading-scroll", …]`) so the scroll-reveal is intact — same coupling category, same silent-failure mode.
defects.mechanism: cross-boundary-styling: the consumer compensates for producer chrome from outside the producer, so every producer bump can invalidate the compensation without any signal.
defects.reproduction: NONE required beyond the C-2 measurement, which is the live consequence. The edict violations are established by reading EasingAuthoringStage.vue:86-116 against the installed glass-ui 7.0.0 and the component's own retire-at-adopt comment.
defects.proposedCure: Retire all three at the producer. Laws 1 (one column) and 2 (wells not cards) are legitimate glass-ui variants — land them as EasingPicker props/variants upstream (`:layout="single"`, `:surface="well"`) rather than consumer :deep() overrides; law 3 is C-2's cure. That satisfies edicts 2 (no legacy), 4 (glass-ui is the design system) and 5 (root-level styling) in one move and removes the whole class of silent breakage.

defects.defect: toggleTune clones the entire disclosure record on every press, which Vue 3 does not require, and the record is never pruned when intervals shrink.
defects.evidence: GradientEasingEditor.vue:84-88 `const tuneOpen = ref<Record<number, boolean>>({}); function toggleTune(index) { tuneOpen.value = { ...tuneOpen.value, [index]: !tuneOpen.value[index] }; }`. `ref({})` is deep-reactive in Vue 3 — a key addition on the returned proxy triggers the dependency the template registered on the missing-key read, so `tuneOpen.value[index] = !tuneOpen.value[index]` is exact. The spread is a Vue-2-era reflex costing a fresh object allocation and a full re-render trigger per press. Stale entries persist: probe 9 shows `tune: ["false","true"]` → `["false","true","false"]` with the true entry now pointing at a different interval.
defects.mechanism: contrivance: a defensive immutability idiom carried over from a reactivity system that needed it, applied to one that does not.
defects.reproduction: NONE — established by reading GradientEasingEditor.vue:84-88 against Vue 3.5 reactive-proxy semantics (key additions on a deep ref ARE tracked). The stale-entry half is visible in probe 9's `tune` array.
defects.proposedCure: `tuneOpen.value[index] = !tuneOpen.value[index]`. The never-pruned half disappears with C-4's stable-id cure — a Map keyed on the left stop's id has entries removed exactly when the interval is.

defects.defect: Two requestAnimationFrame callbacks are scheduled per authoring emission for identical work, and neither handle is retained for cancellation.
defects.evidence: EasingAuthoringStage.vue:57-67 — `onAuthored` calls `requestAnimationFrame(syncVbRatio)` then emits; the emission updates the parent's interval, which changes the `value.css` prop, which fires `watch(() => value.css, () => requestAnimationFrame(syncVbRatio), { flush: "post" })`. Both callbacks perform the same querySelector + viewBox read + ref write. During a control-point drag this is two redundant rAF-scheduled DOM queries per pointer-move. Neither rAF id is stored, so neither can be cancelled on unmount (currently harmless: syncVbRatio is null-guarded via `rootEl.value?.`).
defects.mechanism: double-scheduling: a side effect is attached both to the local emitter and to the round-trip prop change that the same emission causes, so it runs twice per event by construction.
defects.reproduction: NONE — established by reading EasingAuthoringStage.vue:57-67; the redundancy is currently masked because C-2 makes syncVbRatio a no-op, and becomes live work the moment C-2 is cured.
defects.proposedCure: Drop the rAF from onAuthored. The `value.css` watcher alone is sufficient and correct — value.css changes on every geometry change, which is exactly the stated trigger set, and `flush: "post"` already guarantees the DOM has been patched. Retain the rAF id and cancel it in onScopeDispose.

defects.defect: The readout-rail icon buttons measure exactly 24×24 CSS px — passing WCAG 2.2 SC 2.5.8 by equality with zero margin.
defects.evidence: Probe 1 measured boxes: `[{"w":24,"h":24,"label":"Copy cubic-bezier(0, 0, 1, 1)"},{"w":24,"h":24,"label":"Author a custom curve"}]`. Composition: .rail-btn `padding: 0.3125rem` (5px) + a `w-3.5 h-3.5` icon (14px) = 24px exactly (GradientEasingEditor.vue:269-280, :184-196). The two buttons are 6px apart (gap-1.5), so the SC 2.5.8 spacing exception would not rescue them if the size shrank. For contrast, the specimen tiles measure 45.2×43.8 and 44.0×43.8 — comfortably clear.
defects.mechanism: floor-equality: a target size derived from tokens lands exactly on the accessibility minimum, so any future icon-size or padding token shift silently breaks conformance.
defects.reproduction: open /#/gradient and run `[...document.querySelectorAll('.rail-btn')].map(e=>{const r=e.getBoundingClientRect();return {w:r.width,h:r.height,label:e.getAttribute('aria-label')}})` → both 24×24.
defects.proposedCure: Raise .rail-btn padding to 0.375rem (6px → 26px) or add an ::before pseudo-target, so the control carries headroom above the floor rather than sitting on it. Better still, adopt the glass-ui ghost icon-button primitive at its certified size instead of hand-rolling the rail button here (edict 4).

defects.defect: Module-level easing resolution cache with no eviction and no size cap.
defects.evidence: useGradientCSS.ts:69 `const resolvedEasingCache = new Map<string, EasingFunction>();` — populated at :131, never cleared. Reached only for literal-only intervals (easingFnOf short-circuits on interval.fn at :122, which authored intervals always carry), so growth is bounded by the number of distinct easing literals ever parsed from pasted CSS. Contrast demo/color-session/useContrastSafeColor.ts's tintLCache, which DOES cap itself: `if (tintLCache.size > 512) tintLCache.clear();`.
defects.mechanism: unbounded-cache: a memo keyed on unbounded user input with no eviction policy.
defects.reproduction: NONE — hypothesis on the growth path; the missing cap is established by reading useGradientCSS.ts:69-133. Small in practice, unbounded in principle.
defects.proposedCure: Adopt the house idiom already present one directory over: `if (resolvedEasingCache.size > 256) resolvedEasingCache.clear();` after the set at :131.

result.axis: CHALLENGE-D — design (visual truth, state coverage, motion, design-system boundary, proportion/seat law)
result.modelObserved: Opus 5 — claude-opus-5[1m] (1M context). Declared at spawn, observed and confirmed; not inherited.
result.strongestDefect: D-1 — the instrument disagrees with itself about what is on the screen. At the measured fit zoom 0.4233 the composited specimen pixel is rgb(127,0,128) while the readout reports lab(29.568301979097% 68.287364602547 -112.029709525105) = #0000FF. The stage resamples with smoothing (no image-rendering declaration), the loupe explicitly disables smoothing (useLoupeCanvas.ts:40), and sampleAt takes one nearest texel (useImageSampler.ts:111-119) — three resampling rules over one bitmap. probe/shot-forced-colors.png shows the contradiction inside a single frame: crisp red/blue texels inside the loupe, flat purple in the stage around it. The component's sole purpose is to hand you the color under the cursor, and it does not.
result.negativeProof: N/A — verdict is DEFECTIVE. The one positive result worth recording so it is not re-litigated: the motion register is sound. .eyedropper-canvas transform @ --duration-fast/--ease-decelerate is ratified KEEP at demo/DESIGN.md:255; swatch-pop 0.65s is a registered bespoke literal at demo/DESIGN.md:265; prefers-reduced-motion is covered by the global guard (demo/styles/animations.css:184-192) and the rAF coast is explicitly PRM-gated (useInertiaGesture.ts:131-142); no animated property forces layout. Accessible names are also NOT missing — the AT tree resolves all three controls from `title` (button "Close eyedropper" / "Add to palette" / "Apply as current color"), so the route's namelessButtons:3 in visual/REPORT.json is not this component.

defects.defect: The sampled color is not the color displayed under the cursor — stage, loupe and sampler use three different resampling rules over the same bitmap, and the displayed color additionally changes with devicePixelRatio while the sample does not.
defects.evidence: Measured composited pixels from probe/shot-desktop-light-pinned.png: (300,560)=[127,0,128], (350,500)=[159,0,96], (301,561)=[183,0,72]. Readout at that location: lab(29.568301979097% 68.287364602547 -112.029709525105) = #0000FF. Measured stage zoom 0.4233. probe/shot-forced-colors.png shows crisp red/blue texels in the loupe and flat purple in the surrounding stage in ONE frame. DPR dependence: same region reads flat purple in shot-desktop-light-pinned.png (DPR 1) and resolved red/blue moire in shot-zoom200.png (DPR 2).
defects.mechanism: useImageSampler.ts:111-119 sampleAt takes one nearest source texel via Math.floor((rx-panX)/zoom); the visible canvas (ImageEyedropper.vue:69-75) has no image-rendering declaration so the compositor smooths; useLoupeCanvas.ts:40 sets imageSmoothingEnabled=false. No single sampling model.
defects.reproduction: node docs/tranches/V/megatranche/audit/components/wb-extract-imageeyedropper/probe/probe.mjs (displayedVsSampled.zoom 0.4233, displayedCentrePixel [95,0,160]) then probe2.mjs (hoverReadout = pure-blue lab). Or by eye: probe/shot-forced-colors.png.
defects.proposedCure: One resampling law owned in one place. zoom>=1: stage paints image-rendering:pixelated so a texel is a visible square and the loupe is that same law magnified. zoom<1: the sample is the area-average over the 1/zoom x 1/zoom source box the pointer's display pixel actually covers. Stage, loupe, reticle and readout then read one SamplerModel instead of three.

defects.defect: Every second tap is a dead tap that also discards the pin, leaving the PREVIOUS color displayed as if it were the current sample. On touch this is the only sampling interaction.
defects.evidence: probe2.mjs tapCycle: tap purple -> lab(29.5683...) pinned(3 buttons); tap grey -> readout UNCHANGED lab(29.5683...), unpinned(1 button); tap grey again -> lab(53.585013452169% 0 0) pinned; tap purple -> readout UNCHANGED lab(53.5850...), unpinned.
defects.mechanism: ImageEyedropper.vue:176-185 adds a capture-phase pointerdown listener that unpins and raises `justUnpinned`; onTap (:151-155) consumes the flag with an early return. Touch has no hover, so half of all taps are no-ops while the readout keeps showing a color from a different part of the image.
defects.reproduction: node .../probe/probe2.mjs — see tapCycle table.
defects.proposedCure: Delete justUnpinned and the second, never-removed event-binding mechanism (the composable already binds the element at useInertiaGesture.ts:327-350). A tap always samples and always pins; re-sampling the same texel is idempotent; unpin belongs to Escape/close, which already own it (:226-235).

defects.defect: The magnifier loupe never draws a single pixel on touch — the user taps to sample and gets an empty ring with the raw image running straight through it.
defects.evidence: probe.mjs, WebKit 390x844 @3x hasTouch, after page.touchscreen.tap(): mobile.loupe.paintedPx = 0 of totalPx 12100. Visible in probe/shot-mobile-dark-tapped.png. Desktop after hover: paintedPx 9684 (the disc IS painted) — hover is the only thing masking it.
defects.mechanism: useLoupeCanvas.ts:55-60 showLoupeAt sets loupeVisible=true then synchronously calls drawLoupe; the canvas is behind v-if (ImageEyedropper.vue:78-86) so loupeCanvasRef.value is still null and drawLoupe returns at :30. Every subsequent touch repeats it because the capture pointerdown handler calls hideLoupe(), unmounting the canvas again.
defects.reproduction: node .../probe/probe.mjs -> mobile.loupe.paintedPx: 0.
defects.proposedCure: The loupe canvas is a fixed 110px node — keep it mounted and drive visibility with opacity, which is what the CSS already animates (:270). The v-if buys nothing and costs the first frame, which on touch is the only frame.

defects.defect: The answer is truncated mid-number and cannot be recovered: 12 decimal places of Lab for an 8-bit sample, in a box half the width it needs, with no title attribute.
defects.evidence: probe2.mjs readout: chars 55, clientW 275, scrollW 555, truncated true, title null, font 'Fira Code' 16.4px — 49.5% of the value is on screen. Mobile capture shows `lab(53.5850…`. At the audit's own 200% zoom simulation (720x450@2x) readoutClientW = 117px, about 7 Fira characters.
defects.mechanism: 12-decimal float serialization fed to a `truncate` span with no title and no expansion. The sibling file in the same feature solved this and says why — ExtractWorkbench.vue:134-141 'truncate may trim trailing digits ... the full readout rides title + select-all (never a lying readout)' — and adds :title. useImageSampler.ts:39-41 rounds to 4dp but only on the non-CSS path; the CSS path (:63-64 serializePickerColor) has no equivalent.
defects.reproduction: node .../probe/probe2.mjs — readout block.
defects.proposedCure: Quantize at the source (an 8-bit sample carries no information past ~3 Lab decimals) for every space, not only library spaces; then reserve the widest legal representation of the selected space per VISUAL-CONSTITUTION §4, and give the readout its own line when the space is verbose instead of sharing a 275px row with two action buttons.

defects.defect: In RTL the specimen canvas is rendered 692px outside its own clipping stage and disappears entirely, while the sampler keeps returning values for an image nobody can see.
defects.evidence: probe4.mjs — LTR: canvasX 201, stageX 201, w 508 (aligned). RTL: stageX 731 but canvasX 39, w 508 — zero overlap, and the stage is overflow-hidden. Transform identical in both, matrix(0.423333,0,0,0.423333,0,139.04). rtlRead still returns lab(29.568301979097% ...).
defects.mechanism: The canvas is an inline-level element positioned by static flow; its layout box is the full attribute width (1200px), so in an RTL block it right-aligns from the stage's right edge (1239-1200=39) and the transform is applied on top of an accidental origin. In LTR canvasX == stageX by coincidence, and viewportToImage (useImageSampler.ts:103-109) silently depends on that coincidence. Separately the readout inherits direction:rtl with unicode-bidi:normal (measured) for a string full of parentheses and minus signs.
defects.reproduction: node .../probe/probe4.mjs.
defects.proposedCure: State the specimen's origin instead of inheriting it from flow: absolutely position the canvas at the stage's physical top-left — exactly the frame viewportToImage already assumes. Add dir=ltr / unicode-bidi:isolate on the readout per VISUAL-CONSTITUTION §6.1.

defects.defect: No keyboard path into the eyedropper, nothing operable inside it, and focus is not returned on close — a direct violation of the Extract clause that names this component.
defects.evidence: Entry: measured tabindex="-1" on the only opener when a preview exists (ImageDropZone.vue:19), with @keydown.enter.space gated by !disableClick (:21-22). Inside: probe2.mjs keyboardSampling before === after across ArrowRight x2, ArrowDown, Home, End. Focus: probe.mjs overlayContainsActive false, tabbableOutsideOverlay 7; probe2.mjs afterClose.active 'BODY '.
defects.mechanism: No keyboard model exists for the sampler coordinate; the only key handler is Escape (ImageEyedropper.vue:226-235). VISUAL-CONSTITUTION §7 Extract: 'Eyedropper and sampler have keyboard/numeric alternatives.' §5.2 image-sampler row specifies named x/y controls with Home/End. §5.1 requires focus return to the exact connected opener.
defects.reproduction: node .../probe/probe2.mjs — keyboardSampling and afterClose.
defects.proposedCure: Expose the sampler coordinate (already a model in viewportToImage) as the two named numeric axes §5.2 specifies, with Home/End, and let reticle, loupe and readout read that one model. Make the opener a named control instead of a tabindex=-1 region, and restore focus to it on close.

defects.defect: The overlay is a modal in geometry and nothing in semantics: no role, no name, no aria-modal, no focus containment, no status region — and the sampled value and pinned state are announced nowhere.
defects.evidence: probe.mjs: overlayRole null, overlayAriaModal null, overlayAriaLabel null, overlayTabindex null; tabbableInsideOverlay 1, tabbableOutsideOverlay 7; activeElementOnOpen is the drop zone behind it. probe5.mjs: liveRegions 0 across the entire document. Measured AT tree: 'button "Close eyedropper" / separator / text: lab(29.568...) / button "Add to palette" / button "Apply as current color"' — the value is bare text, the pinned state absent.
defects.mechanism: ImageEyedropper.vue:8 hand-rolls `absolute inset-0 z-popover glass-floating` as a third overlay species while glass-ui already ships dialog housing and §5.1 already specifies overlay focus/announcement behaviour.
defects.reproduction: node .../probe/probe.mjs (focus block) and probe5.mjs (afterAdd.liveRegions).
defects.proposedCure: Use the producer dialog housing: initial focus, containment, accessible name, and one role=status carrying the sampled value and the pinned state. Do not mint a fourth overlay species in demo/.

defects.defect: The sampler stage is translucent structural glass, so the drop-zone preview and the result card read through it — the same photograph is on screen twice at two scales, with the answer legible underneath the question.
defects.evidence: Measured overlay background oklab(0.936408 0.005529 0.013284 / 0.808) with backdrop-filter blur(11px) saturate(1.6). Visible in probe/shot-desktop-light-open.png, shot-mobile-dark-tapped.png and shot-zoom200.png: the ImageDropZone preview reads as two pale rectangles above the specimen and 'Extracted Palette 3' plus three swatches read through below it.
defects.mechanism: ImageEyedropper.vue:8 selects `glass-floating` — the STRUCTURAL glass tier per VISUAL-CONSTITUTION §2 ('dock, header, primary plate'). A sampler stage is a specimen well ('opaque/quiet neutral stage') and its chrome is the instrument veil ('denser neutral veil'). The source comment at :4-7 records the substitution of a hand-minted bg-card/75 for this producer rung as the fix; it moved the defect rather than closing it.
defects.reproduction: Open the eyedropper on /#/extract with any image; see probe/shot-desktop-light-open.png.
defects.proposedCure: Two tiers, not one: an opaque specimen well for the stage and an instrument veil for the chrome bar that genuinely floats over live color. The double image disappears as a consequence.

defects.defect: 45.1% of the sampling stage is empty — the overlay inherits the workbench rectangle rather than the specimen's aspect, so the protagonist occupies barely half its own instrument.
defects.evidence: probe2.mjs geom: stage 508 x 616.8, specimen 508 x 338.7, specimenAreaPctOfStage 54.9. Starkly visible in probe/shot-forced-colors.png where the empty band renders as naked white. Also measured: specimen x=201 == stage x=201, i.e. 0px inset, against px-3 (12px) on the chrome bar directly above it.
defects.mechanism: ImageEyedropper.vue:8 `absolute inset-0` makes the overlay inherit the ExtractWorkbench rect, whose aspect has nothing to do with the specimen; fitToViewport (useInertiaGesture.ts:152-167) then contains inside it. VISUAL-CONSTITUTION §3 law 2 caps empty content at 15% of the stage; law 8 requires one full-strength protagonist.
defects.reproduction: node .../probe/probe2.mjs — geom block.
defects.proposedCure: Ratify the sampler as its own composition and size the stage to the specimen's aspect (or let the specimen cover and pan), with the chrome bar docked to it — not a workbench-shaped hole with a picture floating in the middle.

defects.defect: The pinned state is carried by color alone, at 1.65:1 contrast, and collapses to be byte-identical with the unpinned state in forced-colors mode.
defects.evidence: probe3.mjs, Chromium forcedColors active — unpinned: border-color rgb(0,0,0), box-shadow none; pinned: border-color rgb(0,0,0), box-shadow none; identical: true. Light mode measured ring-vs-interior contrast 1.65:1 (non-text minimum 3:1) via probe/pixels.mjs over shot-desktop-light-pinned.png. --primary measured oklch(0.470927 0.126432 129.83403) — hue 129.8 degrees, green, which approaches 1:1 over green imagery by construction.
defects.mechanism: ImageEyedropper.vue:273-276 carries the entire distinction on border-color: var(--primary) and box-shadow — exactly the two properties forced-colors neutralizes. VISUAL-CONSTITUTION §4.1: 'Focus remains visibly distinct from selection in both schemes, forced colors and reduced transparency.'
defects.reproduction: node .../probe/probe3.mjs — forcedColors block.
defects.proposedCure: State over arbitrary imagery cannot ride one color. A dual-tone ring (light core + dark casing, the standard optical-loupe treatment) survives any backdrop and any forced palette, and a geometry delta (ring weight, or the reticle appearing) carries the state without color at all.

defects.defect: The success flourish fires exactly once per session and is silent forever after; it is also the only record that a commit happened, and the two different verbs produce identical feedback.
defects.evidence: probe6.mjs after clicking 'Add to palette': at t+60ms animationName swatch-pop-5659b98f, duration 0.65s, playState running; at t+2000ms stillPulsingAfter2s: true — the .swatch-pulse class is still applied, so @animationend never reset the flag. probe5.mjs: liveRegions 0.
defects.mechanism: @animationend="swatchPulse = false" (ImageEyedropper.vue:22) is bound on the <WatercolorDot> COMPONENT; the reset never runs, swatchPulse latches true, and a second Add produces no class change, no re-animation and no feedback of any kind. onAddToPalette and onApplyColor (:212-224) are otherwise identical. Under prefers-reduced-motion the global guard (demo/styles/animations.css:184-192) zeroes the animation, so the truth is then carried by nothing at all. VISUAL-CONSTITUTION §5: 'A transient flourish may celebrate success but never carries the only truth.'
defects.reproduction: node .../probe/probe6.mjs — anim + stillPulsingAfter2s.
defects.proposedCure: State the durable truth (the palette gained a swatch) once in the status region D-7 requires, and distinguish 'added' from 'applied'. If the flourish is kept, key it (:key) so it restarts on repeat instead of depending on a DOM event bubbling out of a producer component.

defects.defect: Any container resize silently discards the user's zoom and pan and snaps the view back to fit — on mobile that is every URL-bar collapse and every rotation.
defects.evidence: probe6.mjs: after ctrl-wheel zoom {zoom 2.4314, panX -721, panY -664.1}; after setViewportSize(1100x760) {zoom 0.4233, panX 0, panY 133.8}.
defects.mechanism: useInertiaGesture.ts:354-360 observes the stage and calls fitToViewport(), which unconditionally overwrites zoom, panX and panY (:162-166). Refit is treated as a geometry event when it is a content event.
defects.reproduction: node .../probe/probe6.mjs — zoomed vs afterResize.
defects.proposedCure: On resize, preserve the image coordinate at the stage centre and the zoom, then re-clamp; refit only when the image itself changes.

defects.defect: Hovering the action buttons paints their icons with the sampled color — an arbitrary user color used as ink on chrome, measured as low as 1.45:1 — via a per-instance descendant override of a glass-ui root.
defects.evidence: ImageEyedropper.vue:279-282 sets `.eyedropper-action-btn:hover:not(:disabled) svg { color: var(--hover-color); transform: scale(1.2) }` with --hover-color = the sampled color (:10). Measured bar backdrop rgb(220,213,206) bright / rgb(197,190,183) dark. Contrast of a sampled white icon: 1.45:1 and 1.84:1; sampled mid-grey: 2.72:1. Non-text minimum 3:1.
defects.mechanism: A consumer reaching past a glass-ui DockControl root into its svg child and inventing a local hover register. Owner edict 5 (root-level styling); VISUAL-CONSTITUTION §4.2 ('W17 deletes descendant corrections'); §4.1 rendered-contrast rule.
defects.reproduction: Computed from measured backdrops with probe/pixels.mjs contrast(); the CSS is unconditional at :279-282.
defects.proposedCure: Delete it. Hover belongs to the producer. The sampled color already has a dedicated carrier — the WatercolorDot two elements away.

defects.defect: The readout's legibility is a function of the user's photograph: it passes AA over a bright image and fails over a dark one.
defects.evidence: Ink rgb(112,89,66) (measured computed color). Composited bar backdrop over a bright specimen rgb(220,213,206) -> 4.52:1. Over probe-dark.png (rgb(8,8,10) specimen) the bar composites to rgb(197,190,183) -> 3.57:1, below the 4.5:1 AA floor for 16.4px text. Scanned the whole readout band in shot-desktop-light-darkspecimen.png: best 3.57.
defects.mechanism: A static text-muted-foreground token over a 0.808-alpha backdrop-blurred surface whose backdrop is arbitrary user imagery. The sibling file already diagnosed this exact failure class — ExtractWorkbench.vue:285-292 uses --ink-muted 'boot-stamped, floor-clamped ... never the STATIC text-muted-foreground that failed the text floor over the live-ambient plate in light'. The eyedropper uses the token that comment names as the defect.
defects.reproduction: node .../probe/probe3.mjs (produces shot-desktop-light-darkspecimen.png) then the pixels.mjs contrast scan over the readout band.
defects.proposedCure: Opaque chrome (which D-8 requires anyway), or the certified floor-clamped --ink-muted rung.

defects.defect: A DockSeparator divider inside a composition whose binding inventory says the retained dividing line count is `none`.
defects.evidence: ImageEyedropper.vue:15 renders <DockSeparator />; confirmed in the measured AT tree as '- separator'. OPTICAL-BENCH-COMPOSITIONS.md §5: 'Extract | [] | none | none', closing with 'Any additional line, automatic P122 divider, consumer-hidden producer line, terminal row rule, caster stroke or corner rule is a defect.'
defects.mechanism: An ad-hoc line added inside a P122 workbench whose grouping job is explicitly stated as 'image/specimen material and interval separate stage from controls'.
defects.reproduction: node .../probe/probe2.mjs — ariaTree contains '- separator'.
defects.proposedCure: Remove it; interval and material already separate the close control from the readout.

defects.defect: The eyedropper overlay is an unratified composition — a full-bleed sampler sheet with its own chrome bar, protagonist, mobile behaviour and boundary set that appears in none of the eighteen ratified frames.
defects.evidence: VISUAL-CONSTITUTION §3.1 and OPTICAL-BENCH-COMPOSITIONS.md §5/:113 enumerate exactly eighteen separately named low-fi -> real-render pairs, each recording protagonist/support rects, collapse behaviour, mobile sequence, Card equation, boundary/reserve and main-landmark count. No sampler-overlay pair exists. §5: 'changing topology requires an explicit revision to this artifact and the affected pair, never an ad hoc local Card, divider, reserve or breakpoint.'
defects.mechanism: The second protagonist of Extract was built as an element rather than decided as a composition, which is why D-8 (material tier), D-9 (stage aspect) and D-15 (divider) were each decided locally and wrongly.
defects.reproduction: Read OPTICAL-BENCH-COMPOSITIONS.md §5 table — Extract has one row and it describes the stage/controls split, not the sampler overlay.
defects.proposedCure: Ratify the sampler as a named composition; D-8, D-9, D-13, D-14, D-15 then close as consequences of one decision instead of five patches.

defects.defect: All three eyedropper controls are below the touch-target floor.
defects.evidence: probe2.mjs aria[]: Close eyedropper 40x40, Add to palette 40x40, Apply as current color 40x40 — against a 44x44 floor. Context: /#/extract already reports 6 small tap targets in all four Safari matrices (visual/REPORT.json) before the eyedropper is even opened.
defects.mechanism: PROPORTION-AUDIT.md PR-12 ('Touch padding bloats/misaligns visual glyphs' — TIGHTEN, 'invisible/seat geometry preserves target floor while optics follow rung') was never applied here.
defects.reproduction: node .../probe/probe2.mjs — aria block.
defects.proposedCure: Keep the optical rung and grow the invisible seat to the 44px floor, per PR-12's stated mechanism.

defects.defect: The loupe is optically wrong in four independent ways: it is centred under the finger, its backing store ignores devicePixelRatio, its magnification is 9.64x not the intended 10x because LOUPE_SIZE is used as a border-box, and it has no reticle marking which texel is the sample.
defects.evidence: probe.mjs mobile: loupe backing 110x110, CSS box 106x106, dpr 3 -> 318 device px painted from a 110px bitmap (2.89x upscale of a deliberately nearest-neighbour image). The 110->106 delta comes from ImageEyedropper.vue:194-195 setting LOUPE_SIZE as width/height while :265 declares a 2px border, so 110/11=10 px per texel becomes 9.64 and the crisp blocks are resampled by 0.964. probe/shot-forced-colors.png: the loupe shows a red/blue checker while the readout says blue — unverifiable by eye.
defects.mechanism: constants.ts LOUPE_SIZE/LOUPE_PIXELS are treated as CSS px rather than as a model; VISUAL-CONSTITUTION §5.2 requires 'reticle, loupe and numeric value remain one model'.
defects.reproduction: node .../probe/probe.mjs — mobile.loupe backing vs cssRect vs dpr.
defects.proposedCure: Size the backing store to LOUPE_SIZE * devicePixelRatio, make LOUPE_SIZE the content box, offset the loupe from the touch point on coarse pointers, and draw the reticle on the sampled texel — the same model D-1 and D-6 need.

defects.defect: Empty, loading, error, CORS/tainted and out-of-bounds states do not exist; out-of-bounds in particular leaves a stale color displayed as if it were current.
defects.evidence: useImageSampler.ts:114-115 sampleAt returns null out of bounds and the caller (ImageEyedropper.vue:156-162) does nothing — no message, no cursor change, stale readout retained. loadImage rejects on img.onerror (useImageSampler.ts:72-75) and onMounted(() => { loadAndFit(); ... }) (:237-240) never catches. img.crossOrigin='anonymous' (:70) routes every non-CORS cross-origin URL into that same silent arm; a tainted-canvas getImageData (:116) would throw inside a pointermove handler. No loading affordance exists between mount and decode.
defects.mechanism: The component has one happy path and no state machine around it.
defects.reproduction: Out-of-bounds is directly reproducible: tap the empty 45.1% of the stage (D-9) and observe the unchanged readout. The missing catch on loadAndFit is CONFIRMED by reading; its live reachability is a HYPOTHESIS pending a parent that can supply a remote URL — today ExtractWorkbench only passes same-origin data URLs.
defects.proposedCure: Give the overlay the four states it can actually occupy — decoding, ready, out-of-bounds, undecodable — with the decoding and error arms visible and the out-of-bounds arm clearing rather than preserving the stale sample.

defects.defect: Two full-resolution copies of the bitmap are held simultaneously, and dispose() releases only one of them.
defects.evidence: useImageSampler.ts:80-92 draws the same decoded image into an offscreen canvas AND the visible canvas. Measured for probe-1200.png: visibleCanvasBytes 3,840,000 — and the offscreen canvas is the same size again. For a 4032x3024 phone photo that is 48.8 MB x 2, alongside the live and the base64 previewDataUrl the parent retains. dispose() (:97-101) nulls the offscreen reference but never shrinks the visible canvas.
defects.mechanism: The visible layer was implemented as a second copy of the sampling authority instead of a view of it.
defects.reproduction: node .../probe/probe4.mjs — mem.visibleCanvasBytes 3840000 for a 1200x800 source; the offscreen canvas is created at the same dimensions at useImageSampler.ts:80-83.
defects.proposedCure: One bitmap: the offscreen canvas is the sampling authority and the visible layer paints only what it shows.

defects.defect: A composable silently owns a template ref declared in a different file's template, so renaming that ref breaks the loupe with no type error.
defects.evidence: useLoupeCanvas.ts:21 calls useTemplateRef<HTMLCanvasElement>("loupeCanvasRef"), resolving a ref NAME declared at ImageEyedropper.vue:85; the returned loupeCanvasRef handle is never bound by the caller.
defects.mechanism: Encapsulation is nominal — the composable's real interface is an undeclared string contract with the consumer's template.
defects.reproduction: Rename ref="loupeCanvasRef" in ImageEyedropper.vue:85; vue-tsc stays green and the loupe stops drawing.
defects.proposedCure: The consumer owns its template refs and passes the element ref in as a dep, exactly as it already does for canvasRef (ImageEyedropper.vue:115,130).

defects.defect: The pulse class re-declares a utility class's size in hand-written CSS, so the two can diverge silently.
defects.evidence: ImageEyedropper.vue:21 `swatchPulse ? 'swatch-pulse' : 'w-7 h-7'` with :285-289 `.swatch-pulse { width: 1.75rem; height: 1.75rem }` — 1.75rem is w-7.
defects.mechanism: A magic number duplicated across the template and the scoped stylesheet.
defects.reproduction: Change w-7 to w-8 at :21; the pulsed state keeps 1.75rem and the swatch jumps size when the pulse starts.
defects.proposedCure: Keep the size utility on the element in both states and let .swatch-pulse carry only the animation.
